These mountains are in reality like alarm bells: when the water is on their right and left like mountains, they fear and are awed, for they do not regard themselves as free from fear. Thus they remain between fear and hope: ﴿So each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 63].
* Also in it, among the signs of Allah beyond the parting of the water: the water's remaining solid so that it does not flow, and Allah is capable of all things: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verse 57–63 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says: (﴿So We expelled them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 57], i.e., Pharaoh and his people, from Egypt, so that they would pursue Musa and his people. ﴿From gardens﴾, meaning orchards that lay along both banks of the Nile, ﴿and springs﴾, meaning flowing rivers in the mansions, from the Nile, ﴿and treasures﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 58], meaning apparent wealth in gold and silver. They were called treasures because the right of Allah was not paid from them. ﴿And a noble station﴾, meaning a fine assembly for the amirs and viziers, surrounded by their followers).

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿We expelled them﴾. The pronoun refers to the family of Pharaoh.

In His saying ﴿So We expelled them﴾ in the form of majesty (al-'azamah), this suits the context, because those who magnified themselves and became arrogant were met with something greater, which is the power of Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿We expelled them from gardens﴾.

The author says: (orchards that lay along both banks of the Nile). Gardens (jannat) is not said of orchards unless they have so many trees and crops that their land is concealed by them and those within them are concealed by them. As for a place with a few palm trees or little cultivation, it is not called a garden.

In His saying ﴿from gardens﴾ there is an indication of their abundance, and perhaps many of them had an orchard.

As for his saying: (﴿springs﴾, flowing rivers in the mansions, from the Nile), it should be said: in the mansions and elsewhere. Even the gardens, which are orchards, if they contain flowing rivers, this without doubt gladdens and delights the heart, so it is more general than being in the mansions or in these gardens.

As for His saying ﴿and treasures﴾, the author says: (apparent wealth). But there is a point to consider in his explaining them as apparent wealth. If we explain them as wealth that is hoarded, whether it was actually hoarded due to the abundance and plenty of wealth, such that they had no need to spend it, and they hoarded it in the earth to draw upon for the future; or we say: whether it was hoarded in the sense of buried or not buried, because gold and silver is called a treasure if its zakat is not paid, and this is a legal (shar'i) treasure, and if it is buried it is called a linguistic treasure.

The point is that we say: treasures are the great and abundant wealth of gold and silver, whether these treasures were coins or ornaments with which they adorned themselves.

He says: ﴿and treasures and a noble station﴾. The station, the author says: (the assembly). It may be that what is meant is the place of residence, i.e., by station is meant the dwelling, so it is more general than the assembly, the dwelling.

And "noble" (karim) means good. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the choicest of their wealth" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1671), and Muslim (19/29), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], meaning its best. So these people were enjoying every aspect: a noble station in which there is security, tranquility, comfort, and good in appearance and condition; likewise also in terms of the abundant wealth that was available to them, to the point that they hoarded it because they were free from need of it.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., Our expulsion was as We have described, ﴿and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾. That is, ﴿thus﴾ may be the predicate of an omitted subject; meaning our expulsion of them was thus, or the sense is: the matter is thus. The point is that ﴿thus﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, so it is an independent sentence apart from what precedes it and what follows it.

Then He said: ﴿and We caused them to inherit﴾, meaning these gardens, springs, treasures and noble station We caused them to inherit (﴿the Children of Israel﴾ after the drowning of Pharaoh and his people), so they became theirs.

As for His saying ﴿the Children of Israel﴾: Israel is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, and its meaning is "servant of Allah" (Abdullah). They were attributed to him because the Children of Israel descended from him.

As for His saying ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾, there is a difficulty in it, since the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Booty was made lawful for me, and it was not made lawful for anyone before me" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (438), and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir.]]. Here Allah caused the dwellings and wealth of Pharaoh and his people to be inherited by the Children of Israel. Does this contradict the hadith or not? Do you understand the intended point?
* Student: It does not contradict the hadith.
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: Because Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One who gave it to them as possession, whereas there the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) took possession of it by revelation from Allah, glorified and exalted.
* Shaykh: The Messenger says: "I am only a distributor, and Allah is the Giver" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (71), and Muslim (1037/100), from the hadith of Mu'awiyah.]]. Yes, but (...).
* Student: (...); because booty is what is taken from the disbelievers after fighting in the land of war, whereas these, Allah, glorified and exalted, permitted the drowning of Pharaoh in the sea (...) without war.
* Shaykh: Correct. Booty is what is taken from the wealth of the disbelievers by fighting and what is attached to it. This is its legal definition, and this is what is taken by fighting. These people perished, and their dwellings remained for whom? For the Children of Israel, even if the Children of Israel did not dwell in them, others besides them would have dwelt in them. So this matter was not something they seized with their hands; rather it was from Allah, mighty and majestic, due to the destruction of these people. That is, when they perished, it became an inheritance for the Children of Israel, a predestined inheritance, because it had to be so.
* Student: There is another answer, which is to say, as Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms, after the reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105]. This is something Allah, glorified and exalted, wrote from the beginning of creation, that the earth belongs to the believers. So this is the indication that takes it out of the category of spoils, and therefore the booty is not lawful.
* Shaykh: No, now it is not merely land: gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station. Even these treasures are movable property.
* Student: Alright, they were living with them.
* Shaykh: Who?
* Student: The Children of Israel.
* Shaykh: They were living on one side of Egypt, on the side of the city, but now they took the treasures of Pharaoh and the family of Pharaoh.
The main correct answer is the first, that we say: booty is what is taken by fighting and what is attached to it, and anything other than that is not called booty in the legal sense.
* Student: Did all the Children of Israel leave Egypt?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. It is apparent that they all left with Musa: ﴿that you travel by night with My servants﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. This is general.
* Student: Afterward they returned?
* Shaykh: Afterward they returned; they came back to Egypt and settled there.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, after this.
* Student: After that?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Someone may say: Musa fled from Pharaoh, crossed the sea, and did not fight with Pharaoh; rather these were destroyed by Allah, glorified and exalted. There was no war between Musa and Pharaoh (...), there is no booty, nor is there... I mean by this (...) that the dwellings of Pharaoh were ruined and Pharaoh left these dwellings and met Musa at the sea; so what was taken in that place is what is not lawful for Musa, but (...) is not booty.
* Shaykh: But there was no fighting at all.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: There was no fighting.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But we say: ﴿and We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾, its apparent meaning is problematic with His saying: "Booty was made lawful for me." We say: in fact there is no booty here; that is, to say that it is booty is not correct; it is not booty. But someone may say: when someone reads this verse for the first time, it occurs to his mind: how does Allah cause them to inherit to the Children of Israel, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Booty was not made lawful for anyone before me." Its answer is that we say: this is not from the category of booty.
* Student: The Children of Israel who believed with Musa, what if we say that (...) 'Abdullah ibn Ishaq; does it necessarily follow that Musa, peace be upon him, met Ibrahim, peace be upon him?
* Shaykh: No, a long period; the descendants, that is.
* Student: Was he the prophet who came directly after Ibrahim, or was Yusuf between them?
* Shaykh: Ishaq and Ya'qub, and after Yusuf there came to the people of Egypt Yusuf ibn Ya'qub; a messenger came to the people of Egypt. Therefore the believer said: ﴿And Yusuf had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ [Ghafir 34].
The point is that we now say: the answer to this is that this inheritance is not from the category of booty, because booty is what is taken from disbelievers by fighting and what is attached to it.

﴿And We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel. So they pursued them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 59–60] (they overtook them ﴿at sunrise﴾, at the time of the sun's rising). The waw in His saying ﴿So they pursued them﴾ refers to Pharaoh, and the pronoun to the Children of Israel. On this basis, His saying ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾ is, in meaning, a parenthetical clause, because the inheritance of the Children of Israel took place after Pharaoh and his people had drowned. Is this understood?

In mentioning ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾ there is a reason for placing it before what follows: because when He said ﴿We expelled them﴾, it was as if someone said: who took their place?
So He said: ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾. Because of the connection with the expulsion it was placed first; otherwise the order would require it to be mentioned after the mention of the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.
(﴿So they pursued them﴾, i.e., overtook them). It is said: taba'ahu, and ittaba'ahu, and atba'ahu, with the same meaning. From it is His saying: ﴿So Satan followed him, and he became of those astray﴾ [al-A'raf 175]; atba' means taba'a or ittaba'a; all three have the same meaning. ﴿So they pursued them﴾ means they followed them or pursued them, in the sense of overtaking them.
(﴿at sunrise﴾, at the time of sunrise). It also refers to the direction of the east, as we say: "we go east" (nushrriq), i.e., toward the east. So in reality they were ﴿sunrising﴾, either as the author said: at the time of sunrise, or heading toward the east; both meanings are correct. "Mushriq" meaning heading toward the east is with regard to place, and "mushriq" meaning at the time of sunrise is with regard to time. It is customary that departure at the start of the day is more energetic and preferable for people. The Messenger (ﷺ) used to go out early, but he would remain until the shadows declined, the sun passed its zenith, and the winds blew. ﴿They pursued them at sunrise﴾.
* Student: Perhaps someone will say: why did Musa and those with him leave at night, while Pharaoh did not leave after them until after sunrise?
* Shaykh: This has many answers. What do you say?
* Students: Did he not know about them?
* Shaykh: No, he did not know until after a while, because he sent to the cities gatherers, he assembled the people and went out. But what will you answer: that this one left at night and that one left by day?
* Student: I say: because daylight is what would make it clear; but if they had left at night, perhaps they would hide in some place.
* Shaykh: We said: why did Musa and his people leave at night?
* Students: To hide.
* Shaykh: To hide, out of fear for themselves from Pharaoh; they left at night. But this one did not leave in fear, so that he would wait, and the night would pass; he left openly, proclaiming that he was manifest and victorious in himself.

(﴿When the two hosts saw each other﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 61], i.e., each saw the other). The two hosts meant are the host of Musa and the host of Pharaoh.
(﴿The companions of Musa said: Indeed, we are overtaken﴾, the host of Pharaoh will overtake us, so we have no power against it).
﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾: they emphasized the overtaking with "inna" and the "lam"; meaning, overtaken with certainty. How so? Because the sea was before them and the family of Pharaoh behind them, so they must overtake them. Where would they go? There was nothing before them but the sea; if they plunged into the sea they would drown, and by their belief at that moment they would not plunge into it, because they did not know of the matter; so they would not plunge into the sea, and nothing remained but for the family of Pharaoh to overtake them. That is why they said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾, with the nominal sentence emphasized by "inna" and "lam". But Musa answered them by saying: (﴿No!﴾, i.e., they will not overtake us). He said this out of faith in Allah, the Exalted, and trust in His promise, and that He, glorified and exalted, had commanded them to leave only to protect them from Pharaoh and his family.
(﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾, by His help, ﴿He will guide me﴾ to the path of salvation. Allah, the Exalted, said, and so on).
First: he did not say "No, indeed I will be guided," but put forward the companionship of Allah, because it is stronger in strengthening his people: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾. Whoever has Allah with him, nothing will harm him.
Then he said, also emphasizing the effect of this companionship: ﴿He will guide me﴾. The "sin" (sa) indicates certainty and nearness.
The meaning of "will guide me" here is "will show me": ﴿He will guide me﴾, i.e., He will show me a path by which I will be saved.
Was Musa aware of this path at that time?
* Student: No, he did not know.
* Shaykh: He did not know, but he was confident of salvation; for this reason he used the "sin" which indicates certainty and also nearness, because the context requires that. These people emphasized that they were overtaken, and they are answered with emphasis that they will not overtake. This is affirmed first by mentioning the companionship of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾, and secondly by His saying ﴿He will guide me﴾, because the "sin", as is known among the grammarians, indicates certainty and nearness.
﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾, and indeed what Musa, peace be upon him, was certain of occurred: that Allah, the Exalted, would guide him to the path of salvation. ﴿So We revealed to Musa﴾.
* Student: The author's statement here, "by His help," does it not suggest that this involves (...) a interpretation of the attributes, meaning (...) His companionship?
* Shaykh: The companionship meant here is the special companionship that entails help and support. If by "by His help" he intends that it is an explanation of the companionship in its essential meaning, this is not correct; but if he intends by "by His help" that it is an effect of that, this is correct. So the author cannot be objected to, because it admits the possibility that he means: "with me, by His help," i.e., this companionship will have the effect of help.
﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 63]. This (an-adriba) is not suitable, because "darab" does not come in the quadriliteral form; therefore the nun must be kasra: ﴿an idrib﴾, and this "an" is, as we said previously, explanatory (tafsiriyyah).
(﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾, so he struck it). ﴿Then it parted﴾: is the author's assumption that he struck it correct? Yes; because the sea did not split merely by the revelation, but by the striking.
In His saying ﴿Strike﴾ and ﴿it parted﴾ there is an indication that Musa, peace be upon him, hastened to strike the sea, and that the sea split immediately, without delay.
The meaning of (﴿parted﴾: split into twelve parts ﴿and each part was like a huge mountain﴾, a massive mountain, between them passages they traversed, from which the rider's saddle and felt were not wetted).
He says: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾. Which staff? The staff that he always carried, leaning upon it and herding his sheep with it, and in which he had other uses; this staff therefore had great benefits, and among the signs of Allah in it were three signs. This was one of them. What is the second?
* Students: A serpent.
* Shaykh: That when he threw it, it became a clear serpent. The third: when he struck the rock with it, springs gushed forth. These are three signs. As for the rest of its uses, leaning on it, herding sheep with it, repelling an attacker and the like, these are not signs; they are ordinary matters.
As for His saying ﴿the sea﴾, what is meant? The Red Sea, also called the Sea of Qulzum. This sea split ﴿and each part was like a huge mountain﴾, a great mountain, meaning in its size and height; because the sea floor is long and deep, so it was like a huge mountain in size and height. Its apparent meaning is that it was also wide, because "huge mountain" includes size, height and width, and so it was. This is among the signs of Allah, because a staff when struck does not cover a wide place, yet these twelve mountains had without doubt a wide place, and the paths would also be wide. Moreover, among the signs of Allah in this striking, beyond the splitting of the sea, was that it became dry land, drying immediately in an instant: ﴿a dry path, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. This too is among the signs of Allah: that Allah removed fear from them and cast it away from them. Otherwise, human nature would require, when water stands on his right and left like mountains, that he be afraid, would it not? That he be afraid. But Allah, glorified and exalted, cast fear away from them, so they never feared at all.

In his commentary on Surah 26, verses 57–63 (part 2 of 3):

On His saying: ﴿like a great mountain﴾. It is evident that the water did not change. That is, it did not freeze in the familiar sense, so that it would become white and solid. Rather, it remained in its natural state, dark, yet it stood firm. This is greater than if it had frozen while in a state contrary to its nature. Had it frozen in that way, there would have been one sign, namely the swiftness of freezing at that moment. But is its not flowing a sign from the signs of God, or is it a common matter?
* Students: It is a sign from the signs of God.
* The Shaykh: It is a common matter.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, while it is solid (...). Being solid is a natural, ordinary matter. But that it remains liquid and yet does not flow, this is more eloquent than that. There are two signs in it: that it does not flow, and that it does not flow while remaining in its natural state. And God, exalted is He, is capable of all things.
* Also in it: a proof that everything obeys the command of God, and that God, exalted is He, is able to reverse things from their natural properties, let alone change their attributes. This fire, whose nature is to burn and to give heat, became cool and safe for Abraham immediately. And this water, whose nature is to drown and to flow, became a safe, solid thing that did not flow for the Children of Israel.

The scholars have said: there is no sign given to any of the prophets except that a similar one was given to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. So what is the corresponding sign for this matter?
* A student: What happened to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas when he wanted to go on the campaign, so the river became dry.
* The Shaykh: Dry?
* The student: Yes, I mean when Salman al-Farisi was with him.
* The Shaykh: It did not become dry.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes (...), but it was water.
* The student: Why (...).
* The Shaykh: But it does not contradict. It did not become dry. This is more eloquent, that it remained in its natural state, flowing as it was, and these horses, camels and foot soldiers walked upon it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is an example. But if someone says: this was not in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?
* Students: The karamat (miraculous favours granted to saints) of his followers (...).
* The Shaykh: The karamah of his followers is a mu'jizah (miracle) for him.

But that it remains liquid and yet does not flow, this is more eloquent than that. There are two signs in it: that it does not flow, and that it does not flow while remaining in its natural state. And God, exalted is He, is capable of all things.
* Also in it: a proof that everything obeys the command of God, and that God, exalted is He, is able to reverse things from their natural properties, let alone change their attributes. This fire, whose nature is to burn and to give heat, became cool and safe for Abraham immediately. And this water, whose nature is to drown and to flow, became a safe, solid thing that did not flow for the Children of Israel.

The scholars have said: there is no sign given to any of the prophets except that a similar one was given to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. So what is the corresponding sign for this matter?
* A student: What happened to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas when he wanted to go on the campaign, so the river became dry.
* The Shaykh: Dry?
* The student: Yes, I mean when Salman al-Farisi was with him..
* The Shaykh: It did not become dry.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes (...), but it was water.
* The student: Why (...).
* The Shaykh: But it does not contradict. Only it did not become dry. This is more eloquent, that it remained in its natural state, flowing as it was, and these horses, camels and foot soldiers walked upon it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is an example. But if someone says: this was not in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
* Students: The karamat of his followers (...).
* The Shaykh: The karamah of his followers is a mu'jizah for him (...).

A rock in the middle of the water, so they rested upon it, then (...). This too is among the signs.

The conclusion is that it may be said: what happened to the Children of Israel also happened to this Ummah in a similar way. This is because the karamah of the Prophet's followers is a mu'jizah for him, since the meaning of karamah is a testimony that what this honoured person follows is true. So if the followers of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are given a testimony that what they follow is true, it means that what the Messenger ﷺ brought is true.
* A student: ﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 63), "and it split, and each part was like a great mountain." The twelve, these twelve: did he strike twelve times or one strike?
* The Shaykh: No, one strike.
* The student: One strike, and they became twelve.
* Another student: (...) twelve thousand (...).
* The Shaykh: We do not know whether they were twelve entering by a path, or ten thousand, or a thousand. We do not know.
* The student: (...) their number.
* The Shaykh: Twelve thousand men?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: According to the view that says: six hundred thousand.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This one says: their number was six hundred thousand.
* The student: (...) twelve.
* The Shaykh: We do not know. In any case, they were twelve tribes. The tribes (asbat) in the Children of Israel are like the tribes among the Arabs. They were twelve tribes. We do not know how many members each tribe had. It may be few or many (...), each tribe (...) perhaps five hundred persons, or more or less.
* A student: His saying: ﴿So it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 63) is a proof of multitude, because (...) wisdom (...) twelve (...), a great path; they are few.
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: (...) the tribes of the Children of Israel are few (...) wisdom, so they must be many, each one like a great mountain.
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, each part..
* The student: Each part like a great mountain.
* The Shaykh: "Firq" does not mean the path. In the Arabic language, the water that is between them like mountains is not the same as the path. ﴿each part was like a great mountain﴾ means: of water. The water between them was like mountains.

Some of those who transmit the israliyyat (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) mention that these mountains had openings through which they could see one another, for added security. But God knows best whether this is true or not. Nothing is known about it.
* A student: (...) the Children of Israel before the battle occurred (...)?
* The Shaykh: There was no battle.
* The student: Before the victory came to the Children of Israel over Pharaoh (...).
* The Shaykh: It seems I was (...).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we repeated it two or three times.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) in meaning?
* The student: In meaning, but it is (...). If he says: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so We brought them out﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 57), it comes to mind (...), so the answer is: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 59).
* The Shaykh: This is the point of connection (munasabah). That is, looking at the sequence, the inheritance (awrathnaha) comes after mention of the drowning. But looking at the natural order, the inheritance comes after the drowning. However, looking at the order of correspondence, the fitness of the inheritance to the bringing out places it before the mention of the drowning.
* A student: Your words, O Shaykh: looking at the condition of the Children of Israel (...) does this not indicate that their faith (...) was weak?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not the apparent meaning. Note that sometimes you find a statement attributed to a whole nation while what is meant is some of them. Indeed, God sometimes addresses the Children of Israel in the time of the Messenger ﷺ by the deed of their forefathers.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Those are not the ones who said: ﴿Make for us a god﴾ (Al-A'raf 138).
* The student: They are the ones who said: ﴿Show us God openly﴾ (An-Nisa' 153).
* The Shaykh: They are the ones who said: ﴿Show us God openly.﴾
* The student: Is it not (...)?
* The Shaykh: Indeed, yes, those are the chosen ones.
* The student: Those are the chosen ones.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that this in reality shows that however far they reached in perfection, they are not like this Ummah.
* A student: Their faith was weak, because they reached the point of worshipping an idol.
* The Shaykh: No, I mean they asked for it?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: They asked for a god.
* The student: They asked, I mean..
* The Shaykh: But they were prevented from this.
* The student: They worshipped the calf.
* The Shaykh: They worshipped the calf after Musa had left them.
* The student: Unless we say (...) at the beginning.
* The Shaykh: In any case, whatever their state was, even if their faith was weak at the very beginning, we do not know about their faith. But the apparent meaning of the verses is that God bestowed this favour upon them because of the completeness of their faith. You know that when a person is given blessings, his condition may change. They went out at first while in few numbers, weakness, and fear, and they were closer to faith than when they were given this bounty. This is because the custom is that when a person is blessed, arrogance and exultation arise in him. This is the custom.
* A student: Can it not be said that after this, they became factions, their descendants, or (...)?
* The Shaykh: This is not the apparent meaning. The apparent meaning is that they multiplied according to the known generations, and that Musa (...), whose descendants, as it is said, were those who wandered, who remained in the wilderness and were forbidden the land for forty years.
* A student: This does not mean (...)?
* The Shaykh: This is what is said: that it was forbidden to them for forty years, in order that their circumstances and conditions might change in the creation of another generation.
* A student: We affirm that their faith..
* The Shaykh: The point is that we affirm their faith on that day was good and strong when Pharaoh was drowned. For this reason they achieved this great victory over Pharaoh, and Pharaoh was drowned. The context of the verses indicates this.
* A student: This may be a blessing and a trial, and the one whose faith is weak...
* The Shaykh: Yes, but we do not say (...).
* The student: He is tried with a blessing.
* The Shaykh: He is tried with a blessing or with a calamity.
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But who says that their faith is weak? Who says this?
* The student: Evidence that it did not occur.
* The Shaykh: It did not occur yet. A person changes.
* The student: That is, the Muhajirun, when they believed, believed with strong faith, and the Ansar, when they believed, nothing of that sort happened from them.
* The Shaykh: You cannot compare the Children of Israel with this Ummah. Do not compare them. The question of comparison is not valid, because they are not equal. The Children of Israel were tested with the fish, and they did not endure and resorted to tricks. This Ummah was tested with game while in the state of ihram, and they endured, and other matters. Do not compare the faith of this Ummah with the faith of those who came before.
* The student: No, I do not intend comparison. I only mean that when faith is good and present from the beginning, generally it averts from them these dangerous matters in particular, though minor sins may occur.
* The Shaykh: In any case, we cannot say that at that time they were not believers, because they witnessed faith and other things on earth. There is no objection to their conditions changing afterwards.
* A student: We say: had they not been believers, they would not have endured the harm of Pharaoh when he cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. This is a proof of great strength of faith.
* The Shaykh: No, those sorcerers, there is no doubt about the strength of their faith, and the sorcerers were from the family of Pharaoh.
* The student: Other than those who went with Musa?
* The Shaykh: Yes, other than them. This speech is about the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel are other than the sorcerers. The sorcerers were Copts, from the family of Pharaoh.
* A student: ﴿They said: We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us﴾ (Al-A'raf 129). Is this a proof that they had...?
* The Shaykh: They had patience.
* The student: They had patience (...) before and after, (...) the strength of their faith (...).
* The Shaykh: In any case, their saying: ﴿We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us﴾ (Al-A'raf 129), was the promise of Musa to them..
* The student: Their souls were weak.
* The Shaykh: (...) weak faith. We say: the basic position is that their faith at that hour was strong. This is the basic position, and that victory is only deserved by the believers, and only the righteous servants of God inherit the earth, is it not so? But there is no objection to conditions arising and deeds renewing, so they or some of them turn away from them.
* A student: The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise" (agreed upon; al-Bukhari 3208, Muslim 2643/1, from Ibn Mas'ud). We said: if a person's deed appears to people in such a way, while his faith is somewhat weak, then we cannot say about these people that at the beginning, when they went with Pharaoh, their faith was strong, and then God, glory be to Him, changed them.
* The Shaykh: There is no contradiction. Did they change? Did they worship? There was only the one who worshipped the calf (...), and finally God bestowed favour upon them and Musa came to them (...).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How long did Musa remain among them?
* The student: Forty days.
* The Shaykh: That was in the wilderness only.
* The student: Yes, when we say that they changed, I mean their very bodies (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we say that even their conditions change. There is no doubt about this. In any case, let us leave this argument. In reality, this is mere argument with no benefit. This is just argument with no benefit.

We say: the basic position is that whoever is victorious is truly a believer, and whoever is given victory by God and inherits the homes is one of the righteous servants of God. This is the basic position. Then, if their conditions change, we say: God knows how these conditions developed. There is no real benefit in this. There is no practical matter that we wish to apply now, so that we know how to act. It is a matter in which God related to us conditions of the Children of Israel showing that these people believed and then conditions arose for them. Looking at their general conditions, we know that their faith was not like the faith of this Ummah, and that this Ummah is more complete in faith and more complete in deed.
* A student: No, we (...). Can we conclude from this that it is possible for there to be complete faith at the beginning, and then it decreases severely until it reaches this level?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is possible.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, this is not what I mentioned, except at the end during the session on the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (...) with them at the beginning.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all.
* The student: (...) there is no doubt that they were believers, and that they..
* The Shaykh: There is no problem that faith was present. But what has confused you now is, for example, how their conditions developed until they said: ﴿Make for us a god, as they have gods﴾ (Al-A'raf 138). Nothing prevents that some of them said this, or that their conditions fluctuated. God knows best.
* A student: His saying (...).
* The Shaykh: The firqah, the group.
* The student: The group of water.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the group of water. Each part and piece of it became like a great mountain.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...).
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is possible that God is reminding them of their previous faults, perhaps they will refrain. Or He mentions this to show that this is their habit and disposition. This has two possibilities: either He clarifies their fault, perhaps their conditions will be reformed, and what was reformed in their conditions becomes the conditions of those who remain, a demolition of what came before.
Or it may be said: this is an explanation that this is their nature and disposition, for example. Then, along with the rebuke of these people, there is consolation for the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his companions.
* A student: What they became after the Messenger ﷺ, and after Islam, does not indicate...
* The Shaykh: What they became was worse, because now they have become disbelievers. After the sending of the Messenger, and indeed after the sending of Jesus, peace be upon him, they disbelieved and became disbelievers with no faith in them ever.
* A student: (...) even the seventy chosen ones among them.
* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that they were opponents, and that they had an excuse. Whoever wants to know about their conditions should refer to Ighathat al-Lahfan by Ibn al-Qayyim. This is without doubt.

But the discussion concerns those who inherited the land of Pharaoh at that time. We do not now have the right to say whether their faith was complete or incomplete. We only know from the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 105), that at that time they were only righteous, and their conditions changed afterwards.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿When the two groups saw each other﴾ (...) ﴿And We brought near the others, there (64). And We saved Musa and those with him, all of them (...)﴾ ﴿...heirs of the Garden of Bliss﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 61–85).
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. Regarding what has preceded of the verses * And among the benefits:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 57–63 (part 3 of 3):

* First: an explanation of Allah's punishment of the tyrants, which is by removing blessings from them, either by expelling them from them or by removing the blessings themselves. This is drawn from His saying: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 57].
* Also in it: punishment after enjoyment is more severe. For this reason, the text specifies what they were enjoying of bliss, rather than merely saying "We expelled them from their places" or "from their homes." Explicit mention of the blessings they had enjoyed indicates that punishment after such ease is more severe.
* Also in it: a warning to tyrants that their blessings may be removed because of their tyranny. In our time, Allah has opened to people kinds of bliss that were not even imagined before, and certainly were not known. It is feared that these people will be expelled from this bliss if they transgress and become arrogant against the command of Allah, the Exalted.
* Also in it is a lesson: a person may be seized from the very direction in which he sees himself rising and prevailing. Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities to summon the people to fight Musa and his people, and they set out following them, thinking they would overtake them. Yet this very departure brought about their destruction and ruin. A parallel to this in this nation is what the Quraysh did when they set out for Badr. Abu Jahl used to say: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr, where we will serve wine, have singing girls play for us, and drink wine, so that the Arabs will hear of us and will forever stand in awe of us." But they were seized from the very direction from which they came.
* In this is evidence of the strength of Musa's faith, peace be upon him, in his saying: ﴿By no means! Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 62].
The aspect of the strength of his faith is that he was in this distressing situation in which a person sees nothing but that he is about to perish. For this reason his companions said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 61].
* Also in it: the complete power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in splitting the sea and drying it immediately.
* Also in it is evidence that everything has a cause. Even the signs that Allah makes manifest through a person have a cause, for Allah, the Exalted, did not split the sea except after He revealed to Musa to strike the sea with his staff, and he struck it, and it split.
* Also in this is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, just as He guides to the path of meaning, also guides to the path of the senses. This is seen in His saying: ﴿By no means! Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 62]. The intended meaning here is not the guidance of knowledge or the granting of success in righteous deeds, but rather guidance to the path of salvation by which one is saved. Thus Allah, the Exalted, guided him.
* Also in it: Allah, the Exalted, made this water like mountains, like great mountains on their right and left, so that in that, i.e., in their crossing, pride and arrogance would not seize them. These mountains are in reality like alarm bells: when the water is on their right and left like mountains, they fear and are awed, for they do not regard themselves as free from fear. Thus they remain between fear and hope: ﴿So each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 63].
* Also in it, among the signs of Allah beyond the parting of the water: the water's remaining solid so that it does not flow, and Allah is capable of all things: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verse 57–63 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says: (﴿So We expelled them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 57], i.e., Pharaoh and his people, from Egypt, so that they would pursue Musa and his people. ﴿From gardens﴾, meaning orchards that lay along both banks of the Nile, ﴿and springs﴾, meaning flowing rivers in the mansions, from the Nile, ﴿and treasures﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 58], meaning apparent wealth in gold and silver. They were called treasures because the right of Allah was not paid from them. ﴿And a noble station﴾, meaning a fine assembly for the amirs and viziers, surrounded by their followers).

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿We expelled them﴾. The pronoun refers to the family of Pharaoh.

In His saying ﴿So We expelled them﴾ in the form of majesty (al-'azamah), this suits the context, because those who magnified themselves and became arrogant were met with something greater, which is the power of Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿We expelled them from gardens﴾.

The author says: (orchards that lay along both banks of the Nile). Gardens (jannat) is not said of orchards unless they have so many trees and crops that their land is concealed by them and those within them are concealed by them. As for a place with a few palm trees or little cultivation, it is not called a garden.

In His saying ﴿from gardens﴾ there is an indication of their abundance, and perhaps many of them had an orchard.

As for his saying: (﴿springs﴾, flowing rivers in the mansions, from the Nile), it should be said: in the mansions and elsewhere. Even the gardens, which are orchards, if they contain flowing rivers, this without doubt gladdens and delights the heart, so it is more general than being in the mansions or in these gardens.

As for His saying ﴿and treasures﴾, the author says: (apparent wealth). But there is a point to consider in his explaining them as apparent wealth. If we explain them as wealth that is hoarded, whether it was actually hoarded due to the abundance and plenty of wealth, such that they had no need to spend it, and they hoarded it in the earth to draw upon for the future; or we say: whether it was hoarded in the sense of buried or not buried, because gold and silver is called a treasure if its zakat is not paid, and this is a legal (shar'i) treasure, and if it is buried it is called a linguistic treasure.

The point is that we say: treasures are the great and abundant wealth of gold and silver, whether these treasures were coins or ornaments with which they adorned themselves.

He says: ﴿and treasures and a noble station﴾. The station, the author says: (the assembly). It may be that what is meant is the place of residence, i.e., by station is meant the dwelling, so it is more general than the assembly, the dwelling.

And "noble" (karim) means good. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the choicest of their wealth" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1671), and Muslim (19/29), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], meaning its best. So these people were enjoying every aspect: a noble station in which there is security, tranquility, comfort, and good in appearance and condition; likewise also in terms of the abundant wealth that was available to them, to the point that they hoarded it because they were free from need of it.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., Our expulsion was as We have described, ﴿and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾. That is, ﴿thus﴾ may be the predicate of an omitted subject; meaning our expulsion of them was thus, or the sense is: the matter is thus. The point is that ﴿thus﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, so it is an independent sentence apart from what precedes it and what follows it.

Then He said: ﴿and We caused them to inherit﴾, meaning these gardens, springs, treasures and noble station We caused them to inherit (﴿the Children of Israel﴾ after the drowning of Pharaoh and his people), so they became theirs.

As for His saying ﴿the Children of Israel﴾: Israel is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq, and its meaning is "servant of Allah" (Abdullah). They were attributed to him because the Children of Israel descended from him.

As for His saying ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾, there is a difficulty in it, since the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Booty was made lawful for me, and it was not made lawful for anyone before me" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (438), and Muslim (521/3), from the hadith of Jabir.]]. Here Allah caused the dwellings and wealth of Pharaoh and his people to be inherited by the Children of Israel. Does this contradict the hadith or not? Do you understand the intended point?
* Student: It does not contradict the hadith.
* Shaykh: How?
* Student: Because Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One who gave it to them as possession, whereas there the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) took possession of it by revelation from Allah, glorified and exalted.
* Shaykh: The Messenger says: "I am only a distributor, and Allah is the Giver" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (71), and Muslim (1037/100), from the hadith of Mu'awiyah.]]. Yes, but (...).
* Student: (...); because booty is what is taken from the disbelievers after fighting in the land of war, whereas these, Allah, glorified and exalted, permitted the drowning of Pharaoh in the sea (...) without war.
* Shaykh: Correct. Booty is what is taken from the wealth of the disbelievers by fighting and what is attached to it. This is its legal definition, and this is what is taken by fighting. These people perished, and their dwellings remained for whom? For the Children of Israel, even if the Children of Israel did not dwell in them, others besides them would have dwelt in them. So this matter was not something they seized with their hands; rather it was from Allah, mighty and majestic, due to the destruction of these people. That is, when they perished, it became an inheritance for the Children of Israel, a predestined inheritance, because it had to be so.
* Student: There is another answer, which is to say, as Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And We had already written in the Psalms, after the reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya' 105]. This is something Allah, glorified and exalted, wrote from the beginning of creation, that the earth belongs to the believers. So this is the indication that takes it out of the category of spoils, and therefore the booty is not lawful.
* Shaykh: No, now it is not merely land: gardens, springs, treasures and a noble station. Even these treasures are movable property.
* Student: Alright, they were living with them.
* Shaykh: Who?
* Student: The Children of Israel.
* Shaykh: They were living on one side of Egypt, on the side of the city, but now they took the treasures of Pharaoh and the family of Pharaoh.
The main correct answer is the first, that we say: booty is what is taken by fighting and what is attached to it, and anything other than that is not called booty in the legal sense.
* Student: Did all the Children of Israel leave Egypt?
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. It is apparent that they all left with Musa: ﴿that you travel by night with My servants﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. This is general.
* Student: Afterward they returned?
* Shaykh: Afterward they returned; they came back to Egypt and settled there.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, after this.
* Student: After that?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Someone may say: Musa fled from Pharaoh, crossed the sea, and did not fight with Pharaoh; rather these were destroyed by Allah, glorified and exalted. There was no war between Musa and Pharaoh (...), there is no booty, nor is there... I mean by this (...) that the dwellings of Pharaoh were ruined and Pharaoh left these dwellings and met Musa at the sea; so what was taken in that place is what is not lawful for Musa, but (...) is not booty.
* Shaykh: But there was no fighting at all.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: There was no fighting.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: But we say: ﴿and We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾, its apparent meaning is problematic with His saying: "Booty was made lawful for me." We say: in fact there is no booty here; that is, to say that it is booty is not correct; it is not booty. But someone may say: when someone reads this verse for the first time, it occurs to his mind: how does Allah cause them to inherit to the Children of Israel, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Booty was not made lawful for anyone before me." Its answer is that we say: this is not from the category of booty.
* Student: The Children of Israel who believed with Musa, what if we say that (...) 'Abdullah ibn Ishaq; does it necessarily follow that Musa, peace be upon him, met Ibrahim, peace be upon him?
* Shaykh: No, a long period; the descendants, that is.
* Student: Was he the prophet who came directly after Ibrahim, or was Yusuf between them?
* Shaykh: Ishaq and Ya'qub, and after Yusuf there came to the people of Egypt Yusuf ibn Ya'qub; a messenger came to the people of Egypt. Therefore the believer said: ﴿And Yusuf had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you continued in doubt about what he brought you﴾ [Ghafir 34].
The point is that we now say: the answer to this is that this inheritance is not from the category of booty, because booty is what is taken from disbelievers by fighting and what is attached to it.

﴿And We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel. So they pursued them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 59–60] (they overtook them ﴿at sunrise﴾, at the time of the sun's rising). The waw in His saying ﴿So they pursued them﴾ refers to Pharaoh, and the pronoun to the Children of Israel. On this basis, His saying ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾ is, in meaning, a parenthetical clause, because the inheritance of the Children of Israel took place after Pharaoh and his people had drowned. Is this understood?

In mentioning ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾ there is a reason for placing it before what follows: because when He said ﴿We expelled them﴾, it was as if someone said: who took their place?
So He said: ﴿We caused them to inherit to the Children of Israel﴾. Because of the connection with the expulsion it was placed first; otherwise the order would require it to be mentioned after the mention of the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.
(﴿So they pursued them﴾, i.e., overtook them). It is said: taba'ahu, and ittaba'ahu, and atba'ahu, with the same meaning. From it is His saying: ﴿So Satan followed him, and he became of those astray﴾ [al-A'raf 175]; atba' means taba'a or ittaba'a; all three have the same meaning. ﴿So they pursued them﴾ means they followed them or pursued them, in the sense of overtaking them.
(﴿at sunrise﴾, at the time of sunrise). It also refers to the direction of the east, as we say: "we go east" (nushrriq), i.e., toward the east. So in reality they were ﴿sunrising﴾, either as the author said: at the time of sunrise, or heading toward the east; both meanings are correct. "Mushriq" meaning heading toward the east is with regard to place, and "mushriq" meaning at the time of sunrise is with regard to time. It is customary that departure at the start of the day is more energetic and preferable for people. The Messenger (ﷺ) used to go out early, but he would remain until the shadows declined, the sun passed its zenith, and the winds blew. ﴿They pursued them at sunrise﴾.
* Student: Perhaps someone will say: why did Musa and those with him leave at night, while Pharaoh did not leave after them until after sunrise?
* Shaykh: This has many answers. What do you say?
* Students: Did he not know about them?
* Shaykh: No, he did not know until after a while, because he sent to the cities gatherers, he assembled the people and went out. But what will you answer: that this one left at night and that one left by day?
* Student: I say: because daylight is what would make it clear; but if they had left at night, perhaps they would hide in some place.
* Shaykh: We said: why did Musa and his people leave at night?
* Students: To hide.
* Shaykh: To hide, out of fear for themselves from Pharaoh; they left at night. But this one did not leave in fear, so that he would wait, and the night would pass; he left openly, proclaiming that he was manifest and victorious in himself.

(﴿When the two hosts saw each other﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 61], i.e., each saw the other). The two hosts meant are the host of Musa and the host of Pharaoh.
(﴿The companions of Musa said: Indeed, we are overtaken﴾, the host of Pharaoh will overtake us, so we have no power against it).
﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾: they emphasized the overtaking with "inna" and the "lam"; meaning, overtaken with certainty. How so? Because the sea was before them and the family of Pharaoh behind them, so they must overtake them. Where would they go? There was nothing before them but the sea; if they plunged into the sea they would drown, and by their belief at that moment they would not plunge into it, because they did not know of the matter; so they would not plunge into the sea, and nothing remained but for the family of Pharaoh to overtake them. That is why they said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken﴾, with the nominal sentence emphasized by "inna" and "lam". But Musa answered them by saying: (﴿No!﴾, i.e., they will not overtake us). He said this out of faith in Allah, the Exalted, and trust in His promise, and that He, glorified and exalted, had commanded them to leave only to protect them from Pharaoh and his family.
(﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾, by His help, ﴿He will guide me﴾ to the path of salvation. Allah, the Exalted, said, and so on).
First: he did not say "No, indeed I will be guided," but put forward the companionship of Allah, because it is stronger in strengthening his people: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾. Whoever has Allah with him, nothing will harm him.
Then he said, also emphasizing the effect of this companionship: ﴿He will guide me﴾. The "sin" (sa) indicates certainty and nearness.
The meaning of "will guide me" here is "will show me": ﴿He will guide me﴾, i.e., He will show me a path by which I will be saved.
Was Musa aware of this path at that time?
* Student: No, he did not know.
* Shaykh: He did not know, but he was confident of salvation; for this reason he used the "sin" which indicates certainty and also nearness, because the context requires that. These people emphasized that they were overtaken, and they are answered with emphasis that they will not overtake. This is affirmed first by mentioning the companionship of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord﴾, and secondly by His saying ﴿He will guide me﴾, because the "sin", as is known among the grammarians, indicates certainty and nearness.
﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾, and indeed what Musa, peace be upon him, was certain of occurred: that Allah, the Exalted, would guide him to the path of salvation. ﴿So We revealed to Musa﴾.
* Student: The author's statement here, "by His help," does it not suggest that this involves (...) a interpretation of the attributes, meaning (...) His companionship?
* Shaykh: The companionship meant here is the special companionship that entails help and support. If by "by His help" he intends that it is an explanation of the companionship in its essential meaning, this is not correct; but if he intends by "by His help" that it is an effect of that, this is correct. So the author cannot be objected to, because it admits the possibility that he means: "with me, by His help," i.e., this companionship will have the effect of help.
﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 63]. This (an-adriba) is not suitable, because "darab" does not come in the quadriliteral form; therefore the nun must be kasra: ﴿an idrib﴾, and this "an" is, as we said previously, explanatory (tafsiriyyah).
(﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾, so he struck it). ﴿Then it parted﴾: is the author's assumption that he struck it correct? Yes; because the sea did not split merely by the revelation, but by the striking.
In His saying ﴿Strike﴾ and ﴿it parted﴾ there is an indication that Musa, peace be upon him, hastened to strike the sea, and that the sea split immediately, without delay.
The meaning of (﴿parted﴾: split into twelve parts ﴿and each part was like a huge mountain﴾, a massive mountain, between them passages they traversed, from which the rider's saddle and felt were not wetted).
He says: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾. Which staff? The staff that he always carried, leaning upon it and herding his sheep with it, and in which he had other uses; this staff therefore had great benefits, and among the signs of Allah in it were three signs. This was one of them. What is the second?
* Students: A serpent.
* Shaykh: That when he threw it, it became a clear serpent. The third: when he struck the rock with it, springs gushed forth. These are three signs. As for the rest of its uses, leaning on it, herding sheep with it, repelling an attacker and the like, these are not signs; they are ordinary matters.
As for His saying ﴿the sea﴾, what is meant? The Red Sea, also called the Sea of Qulzum. This sea split ﴿and each part was like a huge mountain﴾, a great mountain, meaning in its size and height; because the sea floor is long and deep, so it was like a huge mountain in size and height. Its apparent meaning is that it was also wide, because "huge mountain" includes size, height and width, and so it was. This is among the signs of Allah, because a staff when struck does not cover a wide place, yet these twelve mountains had without doubt a wide place, and the paths would also be wide. Moreover, among the signs of Allah in this striking, beyond the splitting of the sea, was that it became dry land, drying immediately in an instant: ﴿a dry path, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Ta-Ha 77]. This too is among the signs of Allah: that Allah removed fear from them and cast it away from them. Otherwise, human nature would require, when water stands on his right and left like mountains, that he be afraid, would it not? That he be afraid. But Allah, glorified and exalted, cast fear away from them, so they never feared at all.

In his commentary on Surah 26, verses 57–63 (part 2 of 3):

On His saying: ﴿like a great mountain﴾. It is evident that the water did not change. That is, it did not freeze in the familiar sense, so that it would become white and solid. Rather, it remained in its natural state, dark, yet it stood firm. This is greater than if it had frozen while in a state contrary to its nature. Had it frozen in that way, there would have been one sign, namely the swiftness of freezing at that moment. But is its not flowing a sign from the signs of God, or is it a common matter?
* Students: It is a sign from the signs of God.
* The Shaykh: It is a common matter.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, while it is solid (...). Being solid is a natural, ordinary matter. But that it remains liquid and yet does not flow, this is more eloquent than that. There are two signs in it: that it does not flow, and that it does not flow while remaining in its natural state. And God, exalted is He, is capable of all things.
* Also in it: a proof that everything obeys the command of God, and that God, exalted is He, is able to reverse things from their natural properties, let alone change their attributes. This fire, whose nature is to burn and to give heat, became cool and safe for Abraham immediately. And this water, whose nature is to drown and to flow, became a safe, solid thing that did not flow for the Children of Israel.

The scholars have said: there is no sign given to any of the prophets except that a similar one was given to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. So what is the corresponding sign for this matter?
* A student: What happened to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas when he wanted to go on the campaign, so the river became dry.
* The Shaykh: Dry?
* The student: Yes, I mean when Salman al-Farisi was with him.
* The Shaykh: It did not become dry.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes (...), but it was water.
* The student: Why (...).
* The Shaykh: But it does not contradict. It did not become dry. This is more eloquent, that it remained in its natural state, flowing as it was, and these horses, camels and foot soldiers walked upon it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is an example. But if someone says: this was not in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?
* Students: The karamat (miraculous favours granted to saints) of his followers (...).
* The Shaykh: The karamah of his followers is a mu'jizah (miracle) for him.

But that it remains liquid and yet does not flow, this is more eloquent than that. There are two signs in it: that it does not flow, and that it does not flow while remaining in its natural state. And God, exalted is He, is capable of all things.
* Also in it: a proof that everything obeys the command of God, and that God, exalted is He, is able to reverse things from their natural properties, let alone change their attributes. This fire, whose nature is to burn and to give heat, became cool and safe for Abraham immediately. And this water, whose nature is to drown and to flow, became a safe, solid thing that did not flow for the Children of Israel.

The scholars have said: there is no sign given to any of the prophets except that a similar one was given to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. So what is the corresponding sign for this matter?
* A student: What happened to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas when he wanted to go on the campaign, so the river became dry.
* The Shaykh: Dry?
* The student: Yes, I mean when Salman al-Farisi was with him..
* The Shaykh: It did not become dry.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes (...), but it was water.
* The student: Why (...).
* The Shaykh: But it does not contradict. Only it did not become dry. This is more eloquent, that it remained in its natural state, flowing as it was, and these horses, camels and foot soldiers walked upon it.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is an example. But if someone says: this was not in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
* Students: The karamat of his followers (...).
* The Shaykh: The karamah of his followers is a mu'jizah for him (...).

A rock in the middle of the water, so they rested upon it, then (...). This too is among the signs.

The conclusion is that it may be said: what happened to the Children of Israel also happened to this Ummah in a similar way. This is because the karamah of the Prophet's followers is a mu'jizah for him, since the meaning of karamah is a testimony that what this honoured person follows is true. So if the followers of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, are given a testimony that what they follow is true, it means that what the Messenger ﷺ brought is true.
* A student: ﴿So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 63), "and it split, and each part was like a great mountain." The twelve, these twelve: did he strike twelve times or one strike?
* The Shaykh: No, one strike.
* The student: One strike, and they became twelve.
* Another student: (...) twelve thousand (...).
* The Shaykh: We do not know whether they were twelve entering by a path, or ten thousand, or a thousand. We do not know.
* The student: (...) their number.
* The Shaykh: Twelve thousand men?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: According to the view that says: six hundred thousand.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: This one says: their number was six hundred thousand.
* The student: (...) twelve.
* The Shaykh: We do not know. In any case, they were twelve tribes. The tribes (asbat) in the Children of Israel are like the tribes among the Arabs. They were twelve tribes. We do not know how many members each tribe had. It may be few or many (...), each tribe (...) perhaps five hundred persons, or more or less.
* A student: His saying: ﴿So it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 63) is a proof of multitude, because (...) wisdom (...) twelve (...), a great path; they are few.
* The Shaykh: How?
* The student: (...) the tribes of the Children of Israel are few (...) wisdom, so they must be many, each one like a great mountain.
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, each part..
* The student: Each part like a great mountain.
* The Shaykh: "Firq" does not mean the path. In the Arabic language, the water that is between them like mountains is not the same as the path. ﴿each part was like a great mountain﴾ means: of water. The water between them was like mountains.

Some of those who transmit the israliyyat (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) mention that these mountains had openings through which they could see one another, for added security. But God knows best whether this is true or not. Nothing is known about it.
* A student: (...) the Children of Israel before the battle occurred (...)?
* The Shaykh: There was no battle.
* The student: Before the victory came to the Children of Israel over Pharaoh (...).
* The Shaykh: It seems I was (...).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we repeated it two or three times.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) in meaning?
* The student: In meaning, but it is (...). If he says: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so We brought them out﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 57), it comes to mind (...), so the answer is: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 59).
* The Shaykh: This is the point of connection (munasabah). That is, looking at the sequence, the inheritance (awrathnaha) comes after mention of the drowning. But looking at the natural order, the inheritance comes after the drowning. However, looking at the order of correspondence, the fitness of the inheritance to the bringing out places it before the mention of the drowning.
* A student: Your words, O Shaykh: looking at the condition of the Children of Israel (...) does this not indicate that their faith (...) was weak?
* The Shaykh: No, that is not the apparent meaning. Note that sometimes you find a statement attributed to a whole nation while what is meant is some of them. Indeed, God sometimes addresses the Children of Israel in the time of the Messenger ﷺ by the deed of their forefathers.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Those are not the ones who said: ﴿Make for us a god﴾ (Al-A'raf 138).
* The student: They are the ones who said: ﴿Show us God openly﴾ (An-Nisa' 153).
* The Shaykh: They are the ones who said: ﴿Show us God openly.﴾
* The student: Is it not (...)?
* The Shaykh: Indeed, yes, those are the chosen ones.
* The student: Those are the chosen ones.
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that this in reality shows that however far they reached in perfection, they are not like this Ummah.
* A student: Their faith was weak, because they reached the point of worshipping an idol.
* The Shaykh: No, I mean they asked for it?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: They asked for a god.
* The student: They asked, I mean..
* The Shaykh: But they were prevented from this.
* The student: They worshipped the calf.
* The Shaykh: They worshipped the calf after Musa had left them.
* The student: Unless we say (...) at the beginning.
* The Shaykh: In any case, whatever their state was, even if their faith was weak at the very beginning, we do not know about their faith. But the apparent meaning of the verses is that God bestowed this favour upon them because of the completeness of their faith. You know that when a person is given blessings, his condition may change. They went out at first while in few numbers, weakness, and fear, and they were closer to faith than when they were given this bounty. This is because the custom is that when a person is blessed, arrogance and exultation arise in him. This is the custom.
* A student: Can it not be said that after this, they became factions, their descendants, or (...)?
* The Shaykh: This is not the apparent meaning. The apparent meaning is that they multiplied according to the known generations, and that Musa (...), whose descendants, as it is said, were those who wandered, who remained in the wilderness and were forbidden the land for forty years.
* A student: This does not mean (...)?
* The Shaykh: This is what is said: that it was forbidden to them for forty years, in order that their circumstances and conditions might change in the creation of another generation.
* A student: We affirm that their faith..
* The Shaykh: The point is that we affirm their faith on that day was good and strong when Pharaoh was drowned. For this reason they achieved this great victory over Pharaoh, and Pharaoh was drowned. The context of the verses indicates this.
* A student: This may be a blessing and a trial, and the one whose faith is weak...
* The Shaykh: Yes, but we do not say (...).
* The student: He is tried with a blessing.
* The Shaykh: He is tried with a blessing or with a calamity.
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But who says that their faith is weak? Who says this?
* The student: Evidence that it did not occur.
* The Shaykh: It did not occur yet. A person changes.
* The student: That is, the Muhajirun, when they believed, believed with strong faith, and the Ansar, when they believed, nothing of that sort happened from them.
* The Shaykh: You cannot compare the Children of Israel with this Ummah. Do not compare them. The question of comparison is not valid, because they are not equal. The Children of Israel were tested with the fish, and they did not endure and resorted to tricks. This Ummah was tested with game while in the state of ihram, and they endured, and other matters. Do not compare the faith of this Ummah with the faith of those who came before.
* The student: No, I do not intend comparison. I only mean that when faith is good and present from the beginning, generally it averts from them these dangerous matters in particular, though minor sins may occur.
* The Shaykh: In any case, we cannot say that at that time they were not believers, because they witnessed faith and other things on earth. There is no objection to their conditions changing afterwards.
* A student: We say: had they not been believers, they would not have endured the harm of Pharaoh when he cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. This is a proof of great strength of faith.
* The Shaykh: No, those sorcerers, there is no doubt about the strength of their faith, and the sorcerers were from the family of Pharaoh.
* The student: Other than those who went with Musa?
* The Shaykh: Yes, other than them. This speech is about the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel are other than the sorcerers. The sorcerers were Copts, from the family of Pharaoh.
* A student: ﴿They said: We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us﴾ (Al-A'raf 129). Is this a proof that they had...?
* The Shaykh: They had patience.
* The student: They had patience (...) before and after, (...) the strength of their faith (...).
* The Shaykh: In any case, their saying: ﴿We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us﴾ (Al-A'raf 129), was the promise of Musa to them..
* The student: Their souls were weak.
* The Shaykh: (...) weak faith. We say: the basic position is that their faith at that hour was strong. This is the basic position, and that victory is only deserved by the believers, and only the righteous servants of God inherit the earth, is it not so? But there is no objection to conditions arising and deeds renewing, so they or some of them turn away from them.
* A student: The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed one of you does the deeds of the people of Paradise" (agreed upon; al-Bukhari 3208, Muslim 2643/1, from Ibn Mas'ud). We said: if a person's deed appears to people in such a way, while his faith is somewhat weak, then we cannot say about these people that at the beginning, when they went with Pharaoh, their faith was strong, and then God, glory be to Him, changed them.
* The Shaykh: There is no contradiction. Did they change? Did they worship? There was only the one who worshipped the calf (...), and finally God bestowed favour upon them and Musa came to them (...).
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: How long did Musa remain among them?
* The student: Forty days.
* The Shaykh: That was in the wilderness only.
* The student: Yes, when we say that they changed, I mean their very bodies (...).
* The Shaykh: No, we say that even their conditions change. There is no doubt about this. In any case, let us leave this argument. In reality, this is mere argument with no benefit. This is just argument with no benefit.

We say: the basic position is that whoever is victorious is truly a believer, and whoever is given victory by God and inherits the homes is one of the righteous servants of God. This is the basic position. Then, if their conditions change, we say: God knows how these conditions developed. There is no real benefit in this. There is no practical matter that we wish to apply now, so that we know how to act. It is a matter in which God related to us conditions of the Children of Israel showing that these people believed and then conditions arose for them. Looking at their general conditions, we know that their faith was not like the faith of this Ummah, and that this Ummah is more complete in faith and more complete in deed.
* A student: No, we (...). Can we conclude from this that it is possible for there to be complete faith at the beginning, and then it decreases severely until it reaches this level?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is possible.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, this is not what I mentioned, except at the end during the session on the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (...) with them at the beginning.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all.
* The student: (...) there is no doubt that they were believers, and that they..
* The Shaykh: There is no problem that faith was present. But what has confused you now is, for example, how their conditions developed until they said: ﴿Make for us a god, as they have gods﴾ (Al-A'raf 138). Nothing prevents that some of them said this, or that their conditions fluctuated. God knows best.
* A student: His saying (...).
* The Shaykh: The firqah, the group.
* The student: The group of water.
* The Shaykh: Yes, the group of water. Each part and piece of it became like a great mountain.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...).
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It is possible that God is reminding them of their previous faults, perhaps they will refrain. Or He mentions this to show that this is their habit and disposition. This has two possibilities: either He clarifies their fault, perhaps their conditions will be reformed, and what was reformed in their conditions becomes the conditions of those who remain, a demolition of what came before.
Or it may be said: this is an explanation that this is their nature and disposition, for example. Then, along with the rebuke of these people, there is consolation for the Messenger, peace be upon him, and his companions.
* A student: What they became after the Messenger ﷺ, and after Islam, does not indicate...
* The Shaykh: What they became was worse, because now they have become disbelievers. After the sending of the Messenger, and indeed after the sending of Jesus, peace be upon him, they disbelieved and became disbelievers with no faith in them ever.
* A student: (...) even the seventy chosen ones among them.
* The Shaykh: Yes, there is no doubt that they were opponents, and that they had an excuse. Whoever wants to know about their conditions should refer to Ighathat al-Lahfan by Ibn al-Qayyim. This is without doubt.

But the discussion concerns those who inherited the land of Pharaoh at that time. We do not now have the right to say whether their faith was complete or incomplete. We only know from the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ (Al-Anbiya' 105), that at that time they were only righteous, and their conditions changed afterwards.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. ﴿When the two groups saw each other﴾ (...) ﴿And We brought near the others, there (64). And We saved Musa and those with him, all of them (...)﴾ ﴿...heirs of the Garden of Bliss﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 61–85).
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with God from the accursed Satan. Regarding what has preceded of the verses * And among the benefits:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 57–63 (part 3 of 3):

* First: an explanation of Allah's punishment of the tyrants, which is by removing blessings from them, either by expelling them from them or by removing the blessings themselves. This is drawn from His saying: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 57].
* Also in it: punishment after enjoyment is more severe. For this reason, the text specifies what they were enjoying of bliss, rather than merely saying "We expelled them from their places" or "from their homes." Explicit mention of the blessings they had enjoyed indicates that punishment after such ease is more severe.
* Also in it: a warning to tyrants that their blessings may be removed because of their tyranny. In our time, Allah has opened to people kinds of bliss that were not even imagined before, and certainly were not known. It is feared that these people will be expelled from this bliss if they transgress and become arrogant against the command of Allah, the Exalted.
* Also in it is a lesson: a person may be seized from the very direction in which he sees himself rising and prevailing. Pharaoh sent heralds into the cities to summon the people to fight Musa and his people, and they set out following them, thinking they would overtake them. Yet this very departure brought about their destruction and ruin. A parallel to this in this nation is what the Quraysh did when they set out for Badr. Abu Jahl used to say: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr, where we will serve wine, have singing girls play for us, and drink wine, so that the Arabs will hear of us and will forever stand in awe of us." But they were seized from the very direction from which they came.
* In this is evidence of the strength of Musa's faith, peace be upon him, in his saying: ﴿By no means! Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 62].
The aspect of the strength of his faith is that he was in this distressing situation in which a person sees nothing but that he is about to perish. For this reason his companions said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 61].
* Also in it: the complete power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in splitting the sea and drying it immediately.
