* Student: They have tools (...), their physical strength...

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that they had strength, but you should remember that people among us in the past made things that are not made in the present time.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: They made (...) which they call al-nadiyya. They shaped the geometry in the finest way.

* Student: (...) the jass.

* The Shaykh: Jass, jass is soft.

* Student: Carving.

* The Shaykh: But this is carving (...).

* Student: They engrave them.

* The Shaykh: Yes, they engrave them and decorate them, and they make a rim for them on top. Also what they call jarawa; you say jaru. It is a correct Arabic name. The jaru, you now find (...), and yet it is large enough to hold a great deal of water.

* Student: And it does not break.

* The Shaykh: It does not break when carved. Some of them also place (...) on top.

* Student: And digging wells?

* The Shaykh: Digging wells as well.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best.

* Student: How was the punishment ordered upon the hamstringing of the she-camel, with (...) preceding the hamstringing of the she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because this was a sign, being a sign for them and a proof of his truthfulness (...). It means that hamstringing her was an aggression against the message. That is, she was not an ordinary camel.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: This is disbelief. That is, if they dared to commit this great boldness against the sign of the Messenger, it means they reached the extreme limit, or this was made a sign and a condition for their destruction, in addition to their disbelief.

* Student: Is it not (...) ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾ [al-Isra' 59], that she was not born of a she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Why?

* Student: "Atayna-hum" means "We gave them."

* The Shaykh: ﴿Mubsiratan﴾ means a sign that makes things clear, showing the truth.

* Student: But (...).

* The Shaykh: (...).

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No (...).

* * *

* Student: ﴿When their brother Lut said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Do you approach males among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people. They said: If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be among those expelled. He said: Indeed I am of those who detest your deed. My Lord, save me and my family from what they do. So We saved him and his family entirely, except an old woman among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful. The companions of the thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the losers. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their things and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations. They said: You are only of those bewitched. And you are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful. He said: My Lord is most knowing of what you do. But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a tremendous day. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–191].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Previously was the story of Thamud, to whom Salih was sent. In its beginning there is His saying: ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 145], which was mentioned previously in the story of 'Ad and Nuh.

And in His saying: ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 146], what is the proof of?

* Student: Of their not remaining in (...).

* The Shaykh: That is, they could not (...) without messengers and gratitude for the blessing.

What is the intended meaning of the interrogative form?

* Student: The interrogative is for astonishment and denunciation.

* The Shaykh: That is, they cannot be left alone. It is a negation and a rebuke.
* A student: A warning.
* The Shaykh: No, the rebuke includes a warning, because when they are rebuked, they are being warned.
And in His saying ﴿secure﴾, what is the indication?
* The student: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security, and that it is one of the things that requires great thanks to Allah, the Exalted, and that He is the Giver of security (...).
* The Shaykh: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security. This is correct, for the blessing of security may be set against the blessing of being fed, given drink and being quenched.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 148]?
* A student: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ means that the palm tree is among the finest kinds of fruit, for it is soft and easy to digest.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect?
* The student: Which aspect? That it should be...
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is the aspect by which it is preferred over others?
* The student: ﴿whose spathes are soft﴾, that it...
* The Shaykh: Over others?
* The student: That it yields its fruit every season.
* The Shaykh: But is nothing taken from the context?
* The student: (...) soft spathe in softness and the...
* The Shaykh: No. Who knows?
* The student: To Allah belongs the favour; He has bestowed favour...
* Another student: Specification after generalization.
* The Shaykh: Specification after generalization indicates added excellence and special care.

And what is derived from His saying: ﴿and you hew out homes from the mountains﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149]? What do you derive from it?
* The student: It shows their strength (...).
* The Shaykh: Strength.
* The student: Yes, strength. (...) their houses were hewn in the mountains.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Good, strength. What else?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it: strength, greatness, vigour, and so on. But in another sense other than physical strength.
* The student: In terms of skill in engineering.
* The Shaykh: Good, skill in engineering, because this requires skill, since it is a hidden matter, not something in front of you (...) as you wish.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿skilful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149], according to the two recitations?
* A student: According to the recitation ﴿فرهِينَ﴾ [farihin], it means exultant. The other recitation, ﴿فَارِهِينَ﴾ [fari-hin], means skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it means skilful.
* The student: The benefit is that both meanings are combined: exultant and skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Eagerness in work and exultation in blessing. This is the benefit of the difference of the two recitations.

He said: ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 152]. In this there are two benefits, one verbal and one semantic. ﴿They spread corruption and do not reform﴾: what is ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: So the semantic benefit here is that their corruption is not mixed with reform. Thus this negation establishes the completeness of their corruption. This is a semantic benefit.
A verbal benefit: I think I did not mention it to you, but it does not contradict. You will find it in the science of rhetoric (badi').
* A student: In the antithesis (muqabala).
* The Shaykh: No, it is tibaq (antithesis). It contains tibaq, because ﴿they spread corruption and do not reform﴾ is like: ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾ [al-Rum 7] and ﴿but most people do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 187], ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾. This is without doubt from the good verbal style, along with what it contains of beauty.

His saying: ﴿who spread corruption﴾, is it a descriptive (explanatory) qualifier or a restrictive (defining) qualifier?
* A student: No, it is an explanatory qualifier.
* The Shaykh: How is that?
* The student: It means that any Muslim (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) this?
* The student: This is not a restriction, meaning there are among them some who do not spread corruption. Rather, it is a disclosure and clarification of their state.
* The Shaykh: Correct. This spreading of corruption in the land, is its doing itself corruption, or is it a cause of it?
* The student: Their action itself is corruption.
* The Shaykh: Their action itself is corruption.
* The student: And it is also a cause.
* The Shaykh: And it is a cause: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41].

The answer of those people to Salih, peace be upon him, contained three things. What are they?
* A student: Also, that he is one of the bewitched, who have been much... they bewitched him (...) greatly, until sorcery overcame his affair.
* The Shaykh: No, (...). But give me it in the Qur'an.
* The student: And also that he is a human like them, and that they obliged him to bring a sign if he is of the truthful.
* The Shaykh: Are these three answers correct or not?
* The student: They involve detail. The answer ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾ is pure falsehood.
* The Shaykh: Correct, this is pure falsehood.
* The student: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾ is correct. ﴿So bring a sign, if you are of the truthful﴾ involves detail: if they intended to seek the truth, then it is a correct request; if they intended incapacitation and challenge, then it is not correct.
* The Shaykh: Good. What is the answer to the first doubt, their answer to the first doubt: ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾?
* A student: We say: this is always the argument of everyone who has nothing; that is, one who does not rely on (...) anything real, and the furthest he has is denial.
* The Shaykh: Insult, abuse and defamation. So it is an unacceptable call. This is shown by the fact that he calls them only to a reasonable matter, and the one who is bewitched is a bewitched and deranged person. This is not something by which one could call people.
﴿you are only a human like us﴾: what is the answer to this doubt?
* A student: If they had confined themselves to this, we would say they truly intended the truth...
* The Shaykh: That does not contradict it, but what is the answer to it? What is the answer to their saying: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾? We say: correct, he is only a human like you. But what is the answer to this? Did they make it a doubt to reject his message?
* The student: Yes, we say: if he is a human like you, this means (...) that you should obey him, and he did not come from a kind other than yours, so that you could say: If he had come to us from our kind, we would have obeyed.
* The Shaykh: No, other than this. The answer that the messengers gave.
* A student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ [Ibrahim 11].
* The Shaykh: Good. We say: it does not contradict it. He is a human like you, but Allah has bestowed on him the message, and there is no obstacle to that.
The third doubt, ﴿then bring a sign﴾?
* The student: ﴿then bring a sign﴾: they asked him for this sign. So if they intended incapacitation, we say: this is like the first, because they are a people who deny and are obstinate. But if they asked for evidence for what he brought, then they are correct.
* The Shaykh: They are correct. That is why he gave them a sign: ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has her share of water, and you have your share on a known day"﴾. Salih, peace be upon him, gave them the sign, whether they were challengers or seekers of truth. He said: this is a she-camel.
What is the aspect of this she-camel being a sign?
* A student: That she has a share of water and they have a share: they drink, they drink from her milk one day and she drinks water one day.
* The Shaykh: That is not what makes her a sign. If I had a camel, one day I milk her and one day I give her water, would that become a sign?
* The student: No, because it is against habit.
* The Shaykh: Yes, against habit. Because her drinking from this well is against habit, since she drinks and is milked. As long as she is drinking, she is being milked, and this is something that does not normally happen with such a animal.
* The student: On the same day?
* The Shaykh: On the same day, on which she drinks, she is milked.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Some say: if he gave her a bucket of water, she gave him a bucket of milk. Others say: no, she stands and drinks, and as long as she is drinking, they milk her. Whoever (...) the drink is milked. As if this water, by the permission of Allah, immediately turns into milk.
* A student: What is meant, Shaykh, by one day she drinks and one day she is milked?
* The Shaykh: No, on the second day she goes out and grazes. That is why on the second day they drink water and are quenched from it.

What was the result of this sign?
* A student: The result was that they hamstrung her, and they became regretful.
* The Shaykh: They hamstrung her.
They became regretful over what?
* A student: It was said: regretful, that is, because they disobeyed the Prophet (...). And it was said, and this is the more likely: they regretted what they had lost for themselves (...).
* The Shaykh: This she-camel.
* The student: Her milk-share.
* The Shaykh: And what does he prefer?
* The student: What he prefers is that they did not (...).
* The Shaykh: If they had regretted what they had done?
* The student: They would have repented.
* The Shaykh: They would have repented.
From this, from their doing this ugly deed, what is derived?
* The student: It is derived that punishment followed the purpose...
* The Shaykh: No, that when the sign came to them, they went to nullify the sign by hamstringing her...
* The student: Transgression and tyranny.
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is derived from it is transgression and tyranny. In it is consolation for every caller to truth: if he is afflicted with something like this. For example, suppose you are calling to the Qur'an and saying: O people, this is the Book of Allah before us, then a wicked man comes and snatches it from you and tears it up. Tearing this Qur'an is similar to hamstringing this she-camel. But it is your duty to be patient and to say: what befell the prophets, who are more honoured with Allah than I am, was greater than this.

And His saying: ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, what is its kind?
* The student: The punishment was the Cry: a quake with a cry.
* The Shaykh: A quake with a cry. What is the evidence for this?
* The student: His exalted saying: ﴿So the quake seized them, and they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 91, 92].
* The Shaykh: No, only ﴿in their homes prostrate﴾, and that is all. Then the cry?
* The student: The cry: ﴿So the cry seized them at morning﴾ [al-Hijr 83, 84] ...
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: In Surat al-Qamar He says: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient. And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share attended. But they called their companion, and he took [it] and hamstrung [her]. Then how was My punishment and warning! Indeed, We sent upon them one cry, and they became like the dry, broken branches of a fence-builder﴾ [al-Qamar 27–31].
* The Shaykh: Well done, excellent.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 157–159 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿So they hamstrung her﴾, meaning some of them hamstrung her with their consent. ﴿So they became regretful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 157] over hamstringing her. ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 158], the one promised to them, and they perished).

He said: "Do not touch her with harm," but they touched her with the worst harm, we seek refuge in Allah. They hamstrung the she-camel. And what is the meaning of ʿaqr (hamstringing)? The apparent meaning is that it refers to killing, not merely cutting the legs. Rather, they destroyed her, so they were punished with the like of what they had committed. "They became regretful." Were they regretful for the sin they had committed, or were they regretful for the benefit they had lost from her?

* Student: Both. They lost the benefit, and the punishment came upon them.

* The Shaykh: The punishment came after that, until now. The apparent meaning is that they regretted the worldly benefit they had lost, because if they had regretted the sin, they would have been repentant and would not have been destroyed. But they regretted. Consider: yesterday we drank milk, and today the milk is gone from us. So the apparent meaning is that this regret was only on account of the loss of the worldly purpose. And how long did they remain after that?

* Student: Three days.

* The Shaykh: Yes, three days. The wisdom behind these three days, Allah knows best, is that perhaps they would repent, but they did not repent. From this has been derived the rule on requesting an apostate to repent: how many days? Three days. If he repents, well and good; otherwise the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out on him. There is a difference of opinion among the scholars on this issue. The important point is that these people did not regret committing the disobedience. Had they regretted it, that would have been repentance. But they regretted only the worldly portion they had lost, so the promised punishment seized them and they perished, except that Allah saved Salih and those with him.

As for His saying ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾: it is well known that not all of them hamstrung her, but because it was done with the consent of all, including their leaders, it was attributed to all of them. You know that the act of a group within a community is considered the act of everyone if the rest do not object. If they stay silent and do not denounce it, it is attributed to all. For this reason, Allah addresses the Jews in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, reminding them of what their predecessors did, and speaks to them as if they were the doers, because they are one community. So if they do not reject what their predecessors did, it is attributed to all of them.

﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, the one promised. What was the punishment that seized them?

* Students: A cry.

* The Shaykh: And a quake. A cry and a quake together. Allah shook the earth beneath them, and Gabriel cried out at them, and they died. They were found in their homes, prostrate, lifeless, we seek refuge in Allah, fallen as one soul. In this is proof of the perfect power of Allah the Exalted, and that Allah is over all things powerful: ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44].

If we, the Muslims, understood and truly believed, we would not be in the state we are in now. That is, we would not fear people more than we fear Allah. Today the leaders of the Muslims, unfortunately, fear people more than they fear Allah, and so they flatter people regarding the rulings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Had they taken pride in the honor of their religion, people would have feared them.

For this reason they say: a person must fear and be shaken, but either he fears Allah or he fears other than Allah. If he fears Allah, all things fear him, and if he fears other than Allah, that fear takes control of him. This is true, it is the truth: whoever fears Allah, everything fears him, and whoever is mindful of Allah, everything is mindful of him. And the reverse is the reverse.

So it is incumbent upon all of us to be confident in the promise of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, not looking at the immediate causes. It is true that if we looked at things with purely material vision, we could not speak with these people, or challenge them in implementing the Shariah and fighting them. But we must not look only at these immediate causes. We must look at other causes beyond matter. Is that not so?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: For this reason, whoever looks only at these visible natural causes will not succeed in his affairs. When the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, fought the Persians and the Romans, did they look at these causes?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: Not at all. They would besiege a great city for a period, then go out in the morning and glorify Allah (takbir). When they glorified Allah, the walls would crumble. This is a widely transmitted report about them in history: they would besiege a city for some time, then when they glorified Allah the Exalted, it was as if cannons and bombs were shattering those walls. But it was a glorification that came from the heart.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 158, 159].

* Student: The people of Salih, did they believe, I mean, setting aside the hamstringing of the she-camel, did they believe in Allah and follow him?

* The Shaykh: No, only a few of them did.

* Student: Then how (...)?

* The Shaykh: How?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, I mean Allah granting them respite for three days means that we grant the disbelievers three days. But the original disbelievers under the Islamic Shariah have special rulings, such as their being permitted to remain upon payment of the jizya (poll tax), for example. As for others who are not permitted to remain upon their religion, namely the apostate (murtadd), they are given three days. So the matter is disputed. Furthermore, apostasy varies: some forms of apostasy may be given respite, and others may not.

* Student: Then let us mention from this the people of Salih. I mean, did they (...), I mean, did they go, or did she die in her place?

* The Shaykh: Yes, (...). The apparent meaning is that every person died in his house.

* Student: In his house?

* The Shaykh: That is the apparent meaning, yes.

* Student: And whoever was overtaken by death at (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...).

* Student: As for the whole tribe, they drank from one well. It is known that they had gardens and crops. Did they not also have rivers?

* The Shaykh: No, because this well is the one suitable for drinking.

* Student: And the others?

* The Shaykh: The others are not fit for drinking.

* Student: The drinking was specified to this well.

* The Shaykh: To this well. For this reason He divided it: ﴿For her is a share of water, and for you is a share of a known day﴾. There is also no objection to this well irrigating everything they have. That is not prohibited. But the closer view, Allah knows best, is that the gardens were spread with springs, and this well was the one from which they took their drinking water.

* Student: ﴿But as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾ [al-Haqqah 5]. It has been said: the quake, or something similar?

* The Shaykh: The apparent meaning is that it is a name for all of it, meaning by what overpowered them.

* Student: By what overpowered them, meaning it overwhelmed them?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it overwhelmed them.

* Student: Shaykh, what was the reason the Messenger ﷺ forbade (...)?

* The Shaykh: Its reasoning (...), because using this water leads to settling in it and feeling at ease. When the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by it, he passed quickly with his head covered, and he said: "If you are not weeping, do not enter upon these people, lest what befell them befall you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. The wording of Muslim: "Do not enter upon these tormented people unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you."]] So the matter is not trivial. It is strange that many people today, may Allah guide us and them, go there for sightseeing and recreation. This is forbidden, it is not permissible. And the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not contradict this: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth parables for you﴾ [Ibrahim 45]. The reason it does not contradict is that...

* Student: The disbelievers (...).

* The Shaykh: The meaning is that their deeds do not indicate permissibility, meaning that the place being inhabited (...). Or it may be said that our Shariah has come with the opposite, prohibiting it. As for the statement of some people: "The whole earth is never free of nations that denied," we say: yes, the earth is never free of nations that denied. But who says that this specific place is the place of a denying nation? Is it permissible now to go down to al-Ahqaf?

* Student: It is not permissible (...).

* The Shaykh: It is permissible, because their dwellings are not known precisely. But the dwellings of Thamud still exist precisely as they are now. When a person enters them, it is as if he is entering them at that time. For this reason the Messenger forbade entering them except while weeping, and he said: "If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] But today people say: they enter with cameras.

* Student: They also travel to a place that is to be feared.

* The Shaykh: No, traveling for the sake of worship is not objectionable.

* Student: For the sake of worship.

* The Shaykh: Yes, traveling for the sake of worship. Some people travel for trade and for other than trade, but traveling for recreation is forbidden.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, is this not permissible?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: What is the case with the one who goes there? The one who goes there, there is no harm. It may be said that this is not harmful, though the matter requires consideration. It may be said that taking lessons from what is in the Qur'an is more eloquent than taking lessons from what is in its (the place's) worldly reality. The matter requires consideration, but it is lighter than the one who goes for recreation and sightseeing. Hearts have hardened.

* Student: Is it not traveling if the intention is worship?

* The Shaykh: No, because he did not intend that specific spot. The original principle is that a person intends a specific spot and travels to it (...). For example, if he says: "I will travel to the Mosque of Riyadh because it is an old mosque that kings have frequented," (...), "I will travel to it," this is forbidden, not permissible. Or traveling to the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus because it is the mosque of the caliphs: we say it is not permissible, it is forbidden.

* Student: For lesson and admonition (...).

* The Shaykh: No. This may be like what we said at the beginning: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you﴾ [Ibrahim 45]. It only indicates... But ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe﴾ [al-Naml 69]. This may be the case if we say that travel in the physical sense includes (...).

* Student: But on condition of weeping?

* The Shaykh: On condition of weeping, yes, on condition that the person takes a lesson.

* Student: He specified the dwellings of Thamud from all regions of the earth.

* The Shaykh: The original principle is that we do not have a specific place indicating that these are the dwellings of that people, except like the town of Lot. For Allah says: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 137, 138]. But Allah rebuked those who pass by and do not take heed.

* Student: The drinking from (...) of Thamud, the cause is need. So if a person were given (...)?

* The Shaykh: Without (...).

* Student: He drinks from it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is known.

* Student: If he were given water from (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is permissible. Even the well of the she-camel, we say it is permissible, because the Muslims used to drink from it without objection. The well of the she-camel...

* Student: Is it known?

* The Shaykh: It was known in earlier times. I do not know now, by Allah, whether it is still known or not. And in the earlier period, according to the words of the jurists, it was known. It was a large well that pilgrims coming from Syria used to visit.

* Student: They have tools (...), their physical strength...

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that they had strength, but you should remember that people among us in the past made things that are not made in the present time.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: They made (...) which they call al-nadiyya. They shaped the geometry in the finest way.

* Student: (...) the jass.

* The Shaykh: Jass, jass is soft.

* Student: Carving.

* The Shaykh: But this is carving (...).

* Student: They engrave them.

* The Shaykh: Yes, they engrave them and decorate them, and they make a rim for them on top. Also what they call jarawa; you say jaru. It is a correct Arabic name. The jaru, you now find (...), and yet it is large enough to hold a great deal of water.

* Student: And it does not break.

* The Shaykh: It does not break when carved. Some of them also place (...) on top.

* Student: And digging wells?

* The Shaykh: Digging wells as well.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best.

* Student: How was the punishment ordered upon the hamstringing of the she-camel, with (...) preceding the hamstringing of the she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because this was a sign, being a sign for them and a proof of his truthfulness (...). It means that hamstringing her was an aggression against the message. That is, she was not an ordinary camel.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: This is disbelief. That is, if they dared to commit this great boldness against the sign of the Messenger, it means they reached the extreme limit, or this was made a sign and a condition for their destruction, in addition to their disbelief.

* Student: Is it not (...) ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾ [al-Isra' 59], that she was not born of a she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Why?

* Student: "Atayna-hum" means "We gave them."

* The Shaykh: ﴿Mubsiratan﴾ means a sign that makes things clear, showing the truth.

* Student: But (...).

* The Shaykh: (...).

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No (...).

* * *

* Student: ﴿When their brother Lut said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Do you approach males among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people. They said: If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be among those expelled. He said: Indeed I am of those who detest your deed. My Lord, save me and my family from what they do. So We saved him and his family entirely, except an old woman among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful. The companions of the thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the losers. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their things and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations. They said: You are only of those bewitched. And you are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful. He said: My Lord is most knowing of what you do. But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a tremendous day. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–191].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Previously was the story of Thamud, to whom Salih was sent. In its beginning there is His saying: ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 145], which was mentioned previously in the story of 'Ad and Nuh.

And in His saying: ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 146], what is the proof of?

* Student: Of their not remaining in (...).

* The Shaykh: That is, they could not (...) without messengers and gratitude for the blessing.

What is the intended meaning of the interrogative form?

* Student: The interrogative is for astonishment and denunciation.

* The Shaykh: That is, they cannot be left alone. It is a negation and a rebuke.
* A student: A warning.
* The Shaykh: No, the rebuke includes a warning, because when they are rebuked, they are being warned.
And in His saying ﴿secure﴾, what is the indication?
* The student: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security, and that it is one of the things that requires great thanks to Allah, the Exalted, and that He is the Giver of security (...).
* The Shaykh: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security. This is correct, for the blessing of security may be set against the blessing of being fed, given drink and being quenched.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 148]?
* A student: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ means that the palm tree is among the finest kinds of fruit, for it is soft and easy to digest.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect?
* The student: Which aspect? That it should be...
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is the aspect by which it is preferred over others?
* The student: ﴿whose spathes are soft﴾, that it...
* The Shaykh: Over others?
* The student: That it yields its fruit every season.
* The Shaykh: But is nothing taken from the context?
* The student: (...) soft spathe in softness and the...
* The Shaykh: No. Who knows?
* The student: To Allah belongs the favour; He has bestowed favour...
* Another student: Specification after generalization.
* The Shaykh: Specification after generalization indicates added excellence and special care.

And what is derived from His saying: ﴿and you hew out homes from the mountains﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149]? What do you derive from it?
* The student: It shows their strength (...).
* The Shaykh: Strength.
* The student: Yes, strength. (...) their houses were hewn in the mountains.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Good, strength. What else?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it: strength, greatness, vigour, and so on. But in another sense other than physical strength.
* The student: In terms of skill in engineering.
* The Shaykh: Good, skill in engineering, because this requires skill, since it is a hidden matter, not something in front of you (...) as you wish.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿skilful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149], according to the two recitations?
* A student: According to the recitation ﴿فرهِينَ﴾ [farihin], it means exultant. The other recitation, ﴿فَارِهِينَ﴾ [fari-hin], means skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it means skilful.
* The student: The benefit is that both meanings are combined: exultant and skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Eagerness in work and exultation in blessing. This is the benefit of the difference of the two recitations.

He said: ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 152]. In this there are two benefits, one verbal and one semantic. ﴿They spread corruption and do not reform﴾: what is ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: So the semantic benefit here is that their corruption is not mixed with reform. Thus this negation establishes the completeness of their corruption. This is a semantic benefit.
A verbal benefit: I think I did not mention it to you, but it does not contradict. You will find it in the science of rhetoric (badi').
* A student: In the antithesis (muqabala).
* The Shaykh: No, it is tibaq (antithesis). It contains tibaq, because ﴿they spread corruption and do not reform﴾ is like: ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾ [al-Rum 7] and ﴿but most people do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 187], ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾. This is without doubt from the good verbal style, along with what it contains of beauty.

His saying: ﴿who spread corruption﴾, is it a descriptive (explanatory) qualifier or a restrictive (defining) qualifier?
* A student: No, it is an explanatory qualifier.
* The Shaykh: How is that?
* The student: It means that any Muslim (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) this?
* The student: This is not a restriction, meaning there are among them some who do not spread corruption. Rather, it is a disclosure and clarification of their state.
* The Shaykh: Correct. This spreading of corruption in the land, is its doing itself corruption, or is it a cause of it?
* The student: Their action itself is corruption.
* The Shaykh: Their action itself is corruption.
* The student: And it is also a cause.
* The Shaykh: And it is a cause: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41].

The answer of those people to Salih, peace be upon him, contained three things. What are they?
* A student: Also, that he is one of the bewitched, who have been much... they bewitched him (...) greatly, until sorcery overcame his affair.
* The Shaykh: No, (...). But give me it in the Qur'an.
* The student: And also that he is a human like them, and that they obliged him to bring a sign if he is of the truthful.
* The Shaykh: Are these three answers correct or not?
* The student: They involve detail. The answer ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾ is pure falsehood.
* The Shaykh: Correct, this is pure falsehood.
* The student: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾ is correct. ﴿So bring a sign, if you are of the truthful﴾ involves detail: if they intended to seek the truth, then it is a correct request; if they intended incapacitation and challenge, then it is not correct.
* The Shaykh: Good. What is the answer to the first doubt, their answer to the first doubt: ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾?
* A student: We say: this is always the argument of everyone who has nothing; that is, one who does not rely on (...) anything real, and the furthest he has is denial.
* The Shaykh: Insult, abuse and defamation. So it is an unacceptable call. This is shown by the fact that he calls them only to a reasonable matter, and the one who is bewitched is a bewitched and deranged person. This is not something by which one could call people.
﴿you are only a human like us﴾: what is the answer to this doubt?
* A student: If they had confined themselves to this, we would say they truly intended the truth...
* The Shaykh: That does not contradict it, but what is the answer to it? What is the answer to their saying: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾? We say: correct, he is only a human like you. But what is the answer to this? Did they make it a doubt to reject his message?
* The student: Yes, we say: if he is a human like you, this means (...) that you should obey him, and he did not come from a kind other than yours, so that you could say: If he had come to us from our kind, we would have obeyed.
* The Shaykh: No, other than this. The answer that the messengers gave.
* A student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ [Ibrahim 11].
* The Shaykh: Good. We say: it does not contradict it. He is a human like you, but Allah has bestowed on him the message, and there is no obstacle to that.
The third doubt, ﴿then bring a sign﴾?
* The student: ﴿then bring a sign﴾: they asked him for this sign. So if they intended incapacitation, we say: this is like the first, because they are a people who deny and are obstinate. But if they asked for evidence for what he brought, then they are correct.
* The Shaykh: They are correct. That is why he gave them a sign: ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has her share of water, and you have your share on a known day"﴾. Salih, peace be upon him, gave them the sign, whether they were challengers or seekers of truth. He said: this is a she-camel.
What is the aspect of this she-camel being a sign?
* A student: That she has a share of water and they have a share: they drink, they drink from her milk one day and she drinks water one day.
* The Shaykh: That is not what makes her a sign. If I had a camel, one day I milk her and one day I give her water, would that become a sign?
* The student: No, because it is against habit.
* The Shaykh: Yes, against habit. Because her drinking from this well is against habit, since she drinks and is milked. As long as she is drinking, she is being milked, and this is something that does not normally happen with such a animal.
* The student: On the same day?
* The Shaykh: On the same day, on which she drinks, she is milked.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Some say: if he gave her a bucket of water, she gave him a bucket of milk. Others say: no, she stands and drinks, and as long as she is drinking, they milk her. Whoever (...) the drink is milked. As if this water, by the permission of Allah, immediately turns into milk.
* A student: What is meant, Shaykh, by one day she drinks and one day she is milked?
* The Shaykh: No, on the second day she goes out and grazes. That is why on the second day they drink water and are quenched from it.

What was the result of this sign?
* A student: The result was that they hamstrung her, and they became regretful.
* The Shaykh: They hamstrung her.
They became regretful over what?
* A student: It was said: regretful, that is, because they disobeyed the Prophet (...). And it was said, and this is the more likely: they regretted what they had lost for themselves (...).
* The Shaykh: This she-camel.
* The student: Her milk-share.
* The Shaykh: And what does he prefer?
* The student: What he prefers is that they did not (...).
* The Shaykh: If they had regretted what they had done?
* The student: They would have repented.
* The Shaykh: They would have repented.
From this, from their doing this ugly deed, what is derived?
* The student: It is derived that punishment followed the purpose...
* The Shaykh: No, that when the sign came to them, they went to nullify the sign by hamstringing her...
* The student: Transgression and tyranny.
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is derived from it is transgression and tyranny. In it is consolation for every caller to truth: if he is afflicted with something like this. For example, suppose you are calling to the Qur'an and saying: O people, this is the Book of Allah before us, then a wicked man comes and snatches it from you and tears it up. Tearing this Qur'an is similar to hamstringing this she-camel. But it is your duty to be patient and to say: what befell the prophets, who are more honoured with Allah than I am, was greater than this.

And His saying: ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, what is its kind?
* The student: The punishment was the Cry: a quake with a cry.
* The Shaykh: A quake with a cry. What is the evidence for this?
* The student: His exalted saying: ﴿So the quake seized them, and they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 91, 92].
* The Shaykh: No, only ﴿in their homes prostrate﴾, and that is all. Then the cry?
* The student: The cry: ﴿So the cry seized them at morning﴾ [al-Hijr 83, 84] ...
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: In Surat al-Qamar He says: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient. And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share attended. But they called their companion, and he took [it] and hamstrung [her]. Then how was My punishment and warning! Indeed, We sent upon them one cry, and they became like the dry, broken branches of a fence-builder﴾ [al-Qamar 27–31].
* The Shaykh: Well done, excellent.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 157–159 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: (﴿So they hamstrung her﴾, meaning some of them hamstrung her with their consent. ﴿So they became regretful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 157] over hamstringing her. ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 158], the one promised to them, and they perished).

He said: "Do not touch her with harm," but they touched her with the worst harm, we seek refuge in Allah. They hamstrung the she-camel. And what is the meaning of ʿaqr (hamstringing)? The apparent meaning is that it refers to killing, not merely cutting the legs. Rather, they destroyed her, so they were punished with the like of what they had committed. "They became regretful." Were they regretful for the sin they had committed, or were they regretful for the benefit they had lost from her?

* Student: Both. They lost the benefit, and the punishment came upon them.

* The Shaykh: The punishment came after that, until now. The apparent meaning is that they regretted the worldly benefit they had lost, because if they had regretted the sin, they would have been repentant and would not have been destroyed. But they regretted. Consider: yesterday we drank milk, and today the milk is gone from us. So the apparent meaning is that this regret was only on account of the loss of the worldly purpose. And how long did they remain after that?

* Student: Three days.

* The Shaykh: Yes, three days. The wisdom behind these three days, Allah knows best, is that perhaps they would repent, but they did not repent. From this has been derived the rule on requesting an apostate to repent: how many days? Three days. If he repents, well and good; otherwise the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out on him. There is a difference of opinion among the scholars on this issue. The important point is that these people did not regret committing the disobedience. Had they regretted it, that would have been repentance. But they regretted only the worldly portion they had lost, so the promised punishment seized them and they perished, except that Allah saved Salih and those with him.

As for His saying ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾: it is well known that not all of them hamstrung her, but because it was done with the consent of all, including their leaders, it was attributed to all of them. You know that the act of a group within a community is considered the act of everyone if the rest do not object. If they stay silent and do not denounce it, it is attributed to all. For this reason, Allah addresses the Jews in the time of the Messenger ﷺ, reminding them of what their predecessors did, and speaks to them as if they were the doers, because they are one community. So if they do not reject what their predecessors did, it is attributed to all of them.

﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, the one promised. What was the punishment that seized them?

* Students: A cry.

* The Shaykh: And a quake. A cry and a quake together. Allah shook the earth beneath them, and Gabriel cried out at them, and they died. They were found in their homes, prostrate, lifeless, we seek refuge in Allah, fallen as one soul. In this is proof of the perfect power of Allah the Exalted, and that Allah is over all things powerful: ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth; indeed He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44].

If we, the Muslims, understood and truly believed, we would not be in the state we are in now. That is, we would not fear people more than we fear Allah. Today the leaders of the Muslims, unfortunately, fear people more than they fear Allah, and so they flatter people regarding the rulings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Had they taken pride in the honor of their religion, people would have feared them.

For this reason they say: a person must fear and be shaken, but either he fears Allah or he fears other than Allah. If he fears Allah, all things fear him, and if he fears other than Allah, that fear takes control of him. This is true, it is the truth: whoever fears Allah, everything fears him, and whoever is mindful of Allah, everything is mindful of him. And the reverse is the reverse.

So it is incumbent upon all of us to be confident in the promise of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, not looking at the immediate causes. It is true that if we looked at things with purely material vision, we could not speak with these people, or challenge them in implementing the Shariah and fighting them. But we must not look only at these immediate causes. We must look at other causes beyond matter. Is that not so?

* Students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: For this reason, whoever looks only at these visible natural causes will not succeed in his affairs. When the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, fought the Persians and the Romans, did they look at these causes?

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: Not at all. They would besiege a great city for a period, then go out in the morning and glorify Allah (takbir). When they glorified Allah, the walls would crumble. This is a widely transmitted report about them in history: they would besiege a city for some time, then when they glorified Allah the Exalted, it was as if cannons and bombs were shattering those walls. But it was a glorification that came from the heart.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 158, 159].

* Student: The people of Salih, did they believe, I mean, setting aside the hamstringing of the she-camel, did they believe in Allah and follow him?

* The Shaykh: No, only a few of them did.

* Student: Then how (...)?

* The Shaykh: How?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, I mean Allah granting them respite for three days means that we grant the disbelievers three days. But the original disbelievers under the Islamic Shariah have special rulings, such as their being permitted to remain upon payment of the jizya (poll tax), for example. As for others who are not permitted to remain upon their religion, namely the apostate (murtadd), they are given three days. So the matter is disputed. Furthermore, apostasy varies: some forms of apostasy may be given respite, and others may not.

* Student: Then let us mention from this the people of Salih. I mean, did they (...), I mean, did they go, or did she die in her place?

* The Shaykh: Yes, (...). The apparent meaning is that every person died in his house.

* Student: In his house?

* The Shaykh: That is the apparent meaning, yes.

* Student: And whoever was overtaken by death at (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...).

* Student: As for the whole tribe, they drank from one well. It is known that they had gardens and crops. Did they not also have rivers?

* The Shaykh: No, because this well is the one suitable for drinking.

* Student: And the others?

* The Shaykh: The others are not fit for drinking.

* Student: The drinking was specified to this well.

* The Shaykh: To this well. For this reason He divided it: ﴿For her is a share of water, and for you is a share of a known day﴾. There is also no objection to this well irrigating everything they have. That is not prohibited. But the closer view, Allah knows best, is that the gardens were spread with springs, and this well was the one from which they took their drinking water.

* Student: ﴿But as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾ [al-Haqqah 5]. It has been said: the quake, or something similar?

* The Shaykh: The apparent meaning is that it is a name for all of it, meaning by what overpowered them.

* Student: By what overpowered them, meaning it overwhelmed them?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it overwhelmed them.

* Student: Shaykh, what was the reason the Messenger ﷺ forbade (...)?

* The Shaykh: Its reasoning (...), because using this water leads to settling in it and feeling at ease. When the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by it, he passed quickly with his head covered, and he said: "If you are not weeping, do not enter upon these people, lest what befell them befall you."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. The wording of Muslim: "Do not enter upon these tormented people unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you."]] So the matter is not trivial. It is strange that many people today, may Allah guide us and them, go there for sightseeing and recreation. This is forbidden, it is not permissible. And the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not contradict this: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth parables for you﴾ [Ibrahim 45]. The reason it does not contradict is that...

* Student: The disbelievers (...).

* The Shaykh: The meaning is that their deeds do not indicate permissibility, meaning that the place being inhabited (...). Or it may be said that our Shariah has come with the opposite, prohibiting it. As for the statement of some people: "The whole earth is never free of nations that denied," we say: yes, the earth is never free of nations that denied. But who says that this specific place is the place of a denying nation? Is it permissible now to go down to al-Ahqaf?

* Student: It is not permissible (...).

* The Shaykh: It is permissible, because their dwellings are not known precisely. But the dwellings of Thamud still exist precisely as they are now. When a person enters them, it is as if he is entering them at that time. For this reason the Messenger forbade entering them except while weeping, and he said: "If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433) and Muslim (2980/38), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] But today people say: they enter with cameras.

* Student: They also travel to a place that is to be feared.

* The Shaykh: No, traveling for the sake of worship is not objectionable.

* Student: For the sake of worship.

* The Shaykh: Yes, traveling for the sake of worship. Some people travel for trade and for other than trade, but traveling for recreation is forbidden.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, is this not permissible?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: What is the case with the one who goes there? The one who goes there, there is no harm. It may be said that this is not harmful, though the matter requires consideration. It may be said that taking lessons from what is in the Qur'an is more eloquent than taking lessons from what is in its (the place's) worldly reality. The matter requires consideration, but it is lighter than the one who goes for recreation and sightseeing. Hearts have hardened.

* Student: Is it not traveling if the intention is worship?

* The Shaykh: No, because he did not intend that specific spot. The original principle is that a person intends a specific spot and travels to it (...). For example, if he says: "I will travel to the Mosque of Riyadh because it is an old mosque that kings have frequented," (...), "I will travel to it," this is forbidden, not permissible. Or traveling to the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus because it is the mosque of the caliphs: we say it is not permissible, it is forbidden.

* Student: For lesson and admonition (...).

* The Shaykh: No. This may be like what we said at the beginning: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you﴾ [Ibrahim 45]. It only indicates... But ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe﴾ [al-Naml 69]. This may be the case if we say that travel in the physical sense includes (...).

* Student: But on condition of weeping?

* The Shaykh: On condition of weeping, yes, on condition that the person takes a lesson.

* Student: He specified the dwellings of Thamud from all regions of the earth.

* The Shaykh: The original principle is that we do not have a specific place indicating that these are the dwellings of that people, except like the town of Lot. For Allah says: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 137, 138]. But Allah rebuked those who pass by and do not take heed.

* Student: The drinking from (...) of Thamud, the cause is need. So if a person were given (...)?

* The Shaykh: Without (...).

* Student: He drinks from it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is known.

* Student: If he were given water from (...)?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is permissible. Even the well of the she-camel, we say it is permissible, because the Muslims used to drink from it without objection. The well of the she-camel...

* Student: Is it known?

* The Shaykh: It was known in earlier times. I do not know now, by Allah, whether it is still known or not. And in the earlier period, according to the words of the jurists, it was known. It was a large well that pilgrims coming from Syria used to visit.

* Student: They have tools (...), their physical strength...

* The Shaykh: There is no doubt that they had strength, but you should remember that people among us in the past made things that are not made in the present time.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: They made (...) which they call al-nadiyya. They shaped the geometry in the finest way.

* Student: (...) the jass.

* The Shaykh: Jass, jass is soft.

* Student: Carving.

* The Shaykh: But this is carving (...).

* Student: They engrave them.

* The Shaykh: Yes, they engrave them and decorate them, and they make a rim for them on top. Also what they call jarawa; you say jaru. It is a correct Arabic name. The jaru, you now find (...), and yet it is large enough to hold a great deal of water.

* Student: And it does not break.

* The Shaykh: It does not break when carved. Some of them also place (...) on top.

* Student: And digging wells?

* The Shaykh: Digging wells as well.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Allah knows best.

* Student: How was the punishment ordered upon the hamstringing of the she-camel, with (...) preceding the hamstringing of the she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Yes, because this was a sign, being a sign for them and a proof of his truthfulness (...). It means that hamstringing her was an aggression against the message. That is, she was not an ordinary camel.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: This is disbelief. That is, if they dared to commit this great boldness against the sign of the Messenger, it means they reached the extreme limit, or this was made a sign and a condition for their destruction, in addition to their disbelief.

* Student: Is it not (...) ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾ [al-Isra' 59], that she was not born of a she-camel?

* The Shaykh: Why?

* Student: "Atayna-hum" means "We gave them."

* The Shaykh: ﴿Mubsiratan﴾ means a sign that makes things clear, showing the truth.

* Student: But (...).

* The Shaykh: (...).

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No (...).

* * *

* Student: ﴿When their brother Lut said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Do you approach males among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a transgressing people. They said: If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be among those expelled. He said: Indeed I am of those who detest your deed. My Lord, save me and my family from what they do. So We saved him and his family entirely, except an old woman among those who remained behind. Then We destroyed the others. And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful. The companions of the thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them: Will you not fear Allah? Indeed I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask of you any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds. Give full measure and do not be among the losers. And weigh with a true balance. And do not deprive people of their things and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief. And fear Him who created you and the former generations. They said: You are only of those bewitched. And you are only a human like us, and we think you are surely among the liars. So cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon us, if you are of the truthful. He said: My Lord is most knowing of what you do. But they denied him, so the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them. Indeed it was the punishment of a tremendous day. Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–191].

* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed. Previously was the story of Thamud, to whom Salih was sent. In its beginning there is His saying: ﴿My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 145], which was mentioned previously in the story of 'Ad and Nuh.

And in His saying: ﴿Will you be left secure in what is here?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 146], what is the proof of?

* Student: Of their not remaining in (...).

* The Shaykh: That is, they could not (...) without messengers and gratitude for the blessing.

What is the intended meaning of the interrogative form?

* Student: The interrogative is for astonishment and denunciation.

* The Shaykh: That is, they cannot be left alone. It is a negation and a rebuke.
* A student: A warning.
* The Shaykh: No, the rebuke includes a warning, because when they are rebuked, they are being warned.
And in His saying ﴿secure﴾, what is the indication?
* The student: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security, and that it is one of the things that requires great thanks to Allah, the Exalted, and that He is the Giver of security (...).
* The Shaykh: It indicates the great magnitude of the blessing of security. This is correct, for the blessing of security may be set against the blessing of being fed, given drink and being quenched.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 148]?
* A student: ﴿and crops and palm trees whose spathes are soft﴾ means that the palm tree is among the finest kinds of fruit, for it is soft and easy to digest.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect?
* The student: Which aspect? That it should be...
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is the aspect by which it is preferred over others?
* The student: ﴿whose spathes are soft﴾, that it...
* The Shaykh: Over others?
* The student: That it yields its fruit every season.
* The Shaykh: But is nothing taken from the context?
* The student: (...) soft spathe in softness and the...
* The Shaykh: No. Who knows?
* The student: To Allah belongs the favour; He has bestowed favour...
* Another student: Specification after generalization.
* The Shaykh: Specification after generalization indicates added excellence and special care.

And what is derived from His saying: ﴿and you hew out homes from the mountains﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149]? What do you derive from it?
* The student: It shows their strength (...).
* The Shaykh: Strength.
* The student: Yes, strength. (...) their houses were hewn in the mountains.
* The Shaykh: Yes. Good, strength. What else?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: It does not contradict it: strength, greatness, vigour, and so on. But in another sense other than physical strength.
* The student: In terms of skill in engineering.
* The Shaykh: Good, skill in engineering, because this requires skill, since it is a hidden matter, not something in front of you (...) as you wish.

What is derived from His saying: ﴿skilful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 149], according to the two recitations?
* A student: According to the recitation ﴿فرهِينَ﴾ [farihin], it means exultant. The other recitation, ﴿فَارِهِينَ﴾ [fari-hin], means skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes, it means skilful.
* The student: The benefit is that both meanings are combined: exultant and skilful.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Eagerness in work and exultation in blessing. This is the benefit of the difference of the two recitations.

He said: ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 152]. In this there are two benefits, one verbal and one semantic. ﴿They spread corruption and do not reform﴾: what is ﴿who spread corruption in the land and do not reform﴾?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: So the semantic benefit here is that their corruption is not mixed with reform. Thus this negation establishes the completeness of their corruption. This is a semantic benefit.
A verbal benefit: I think I did not mention it to you, but it does not contradict. You will find it in the science of rhetoric (badi').
* A student: In the antithesis (muqabala).
* The Shaykh: No, it is tibaq (antithesis). It contains tibaq, because ﴿they spread corruption and do not reform﴾ is like: ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾ [al-Rum 7] and ﴿but most people do not know﴾ [al-A'raf 187], ﴿they know an outward appearance﴾. This is without doubt from the good verbal style, along with what it contains of beauty.

His saying: ﴿who spread corruption﴾, is it a descriptive (explanatory) qualifier or a restrictive (defining) qualifier?
* A student: No, it is an explanatory qualifier.
* The Shaykh: How is that?
* The student: It means that any Muslim (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) this?
* The student: This is not a restriction, meaning there are among them some who do not spread corruption. Rather, it is a disclosure and clarification of their state.
* The Shaykh: Correct. This spreading of corruption in the land, is its doing itself corruption, or is it a cause of it?
* The student: Their action itself is corruption.
* The Shaykh: Their action itself is corruption.
* The student: And it is also a cause.
* The Shaykh: And it is a cause: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned﴾ [al-Rum 41].

The answer of those people to Salih, peace be upon him, contained three things. What are they?
* A student: Also, that he is one of the bewitched, who have been much... they bewitched him (...) greatly, until sorcery overcame his affair.
* The Shaykh: No, (...). But give me it in the Qur'an.
* The student: And also that he is a human like them, and that they obliged him to bring a sign if he is of the truthful.
* The Shaykh: Are these three answers correct or not?
* The student: They involve detail. The answer ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾ is pure falsehood.
* The Shaykh: Correct, this is pure falsehood.
* The student: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾ is correct. ﴿So bring a sign, if you are of the truthful﴾ involves detail: if they intended to seek the truth, then it is a correct request; if they intended incapacitation and challenge, then it is not correct.
* The Shaykh: Good. What is the answer to the first doubt, their answer to the first doubt: ﴿you are only one of the bewitched﴾?
* A student: We say: this is always the argument of everyone who has nothing; that is, one who does not rely on (...) anything real, and the furthest he has is denial.
* The Shaykh: Insult, abuse and defamation. So it is an unacceptable call. This is shown by the fact that he calls them only to a reasonable matter, and the one who is bewitched is a bewitched and deranged person. This is not something by which one could call people.
﴿you are only a human like us﴾: what is the answer to this doubt?
* A student: If they had confined themselves to this, we would say they truly intended the truth...
* The Shaykh: That does not contradict it, but what is the answer to it? What is the answer to their saying: ﴿you are only a human like us﴾? We say: correct, he is only a human like you. But what is the answer to this? Did they make it a doubt to reject his message?
* The student: Yes, we say: if he is a human like you, this means (...) that you should obey him, and he did not come from a kind other than yours, so that you could say: If he had come to us from our kind, we would have obeyed.
* The Shaykh: No, other than this. The answer that the messengers gave.
* A student: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ [Ibrahim 11].
* The Shaykh: Good. We say: it does not contradict it. He is a human like you, but Allah has bestowed on him the message, and there is no obstacle to that.
The third doubt, ﴿then bring a sign﴾?
* The student: ﴿then bring a sign﴾: they asked him for this sign. So if they intended incapacitation, we say: this is like the first, because they are a people who deny and are obstinate. But if they asked for evidence for what he brought, then they are correct.
* The Shaykh: They are correct. That is why he gave them a sign: ﴿He said, "This is a she-camel; she has her share of water, and you have your share on a known day"﴾. Salih, peace be upon him, gave them the sign, whether they were challengers or seekers of truth. He said: this is a she-camel.
What is the aspect of this she-camel being a sign?
* A student: That she has a share of water and they have a share: they drink, they drink from her milk one day and she drinks water one day.
* The Shaykh: That is not what makes her a sign. If I had a camel, one day I milk her and one day I give her water, would that become a sign?
* The student: No, because it is against habit.
* The Shaykh: Yes, against habit. Because her drinking from this well is against habit, since she drinks and is milked. As long as she is drinking, she is being milked, and this is something that does not normally happen with such a animal.
* The student: On the same day?
* The Shaykh: On the same day, on which she drinks, she is milked.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Some say: if he gave her a bucket of water, she gave him a bucket of milk. Others say: no, she stands and drinks, and as long as she is drinking, they milk her. Whoever (...) the drink is milked. As if this water, by the permission of Allah, immediately turns into milk.
* A student: What is meant, Shaykh, by one day she drinks and one day she is milked?
* The Shaykh: No, on the second day she goes out and grazes. That is why on the second day they drink water and are quenched from it.

What was the result of this sign?
* A student: The result was that they hamstrung her, and they became regretful.
* The Shaykh: They hamstrung her.
They became regretful over what?
* A student: It was said: regretful, that is, because they disobeyed the Prophet (...). And it was said, and this is the more likely: they regretted what they had lost for themselves (...).
* The Shaykh: This she-camel.
* The student: Her milk-share.
* The Shaykh: And what does he prefer?
* The student: What he prefers is that they did not (...).
* The Shaykh: If they had regretted what they had done?
* The student: They would have repented.
* The Shaykh: They would have repented.
From this, from their doing this ugly deed, what is derived?
* The student: It is derived that punishment followed the purpose...
* The Shaykh: No, that when the sign came to them, they went to nullify the sign by hamstringing her...
* The student: Transgression and tyranny.
* The Shaykh: Yes, what is derived from it is transgression and tyranny. In it is consolation for every caller to truth: if he is afflicted with something like this. For example, suppose you are calling to the Qur'an and saying: O people, this is the Book of Allah before us, then a wicked man comes and snatches it from you and tears it up. Tearing this Qur'an is similar to hamstringing this she-camel. But it is your duty to be patient and to say: what befell the prophets, who are more honoured with Allah than I am, was greater than this.

And His saying: ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, what is its kind?
* The student: The punishment was the Cry: a quake with a cry.
* The Shaykh: A quake with a cry. What is the evidence for this?
* The student: His exalted saying: ﴿So the quake seized them, and they became in their homes prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf 91, 92].
* The Shaykh: No, only ﴿in their homes prostrate﴾, and that is all. Then the cry?
* The student: The cry: ﴿So the cry seized them at morning﴾ [al-Hijr 83, 84] ...
* The Shaykh: No.
* The student: In Surat al-Qamar He says: ﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them, so watch them and be patient. And inform them that the water is to be shared between them, each share attended. But they called their companion, and he took [it] and hamstrung [her]. Then how was My punishment and warning! Indeed, We sent upon them one cry, and they became like the dry, broken branches of a fence-builder﴾ [al-Qamar 27–31].
* The Shaykh: Well done, excellent.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers. When their brother Lot said to them...﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 160–161].

The people of Lot lived in a town called Sodom, in the land of Palestine. Lot, as the historians say, was the son of Abraham's brother, so Abraham was his paternal uncle. Allah sent him to the people of this town. Along with their disbelief in Allah, the Exalted, they practiced a vile deed, which is counted among the most wicked of actions, and Allah forbid. Allah named it wicked when He said: ﴿And We saved him from the town that used to commit abominations﴾ [al-Anbiya' 74]. So it is (...), because it is ugly by reason, by natural disposition and by the Law. This deed they did was that they would approach males, Allah forbid, just as they approached women.

Here Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–164]. All of this has already been discussed.

Every messenger is sent first to establish monotheism: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. This is the foundation with which all messengers are sent. However, there are particular kinds of sins committed by some nations, on which the messengers, peace be upon them, focus. In the case of the people of Lot, their specific crime was this immorality; therefore He said: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165–166]. This interrogative is for rebuke and denunciation.

﴿Do you approach males﴾: that is, the males, the plural of (dhakar).

﴿From among the worlds﴾ is an explanation of "males"; that is, from among (people), whether they are from your tribe or from other than your tribe. For this reason he did not say, "Do you approach the males among you," but rather said ﴿from among the worlds﴾, indicating that they, Allah forbid, do not restrain themselves from anyone; they are like dogs. Then, in addition to their wickedness, they abandoned the blessing that Allah created for them: ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾.

If they approached males from among the worlds because they were compelled to, and had no lawful option sufficient for them, the matter would be lighter. But they have lawful options sufficient for them, so how do they approach the wicked things and leave the good things? For this reason He said: ﴿and leave﴾ is included in the meaning of the interrogative; that is, "and do you leave ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾?" (tadharun) means: you abandon ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾; that is, (their private parts) is an explanation of His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾; meaning you approach what has been created for you of wives, which is the front passage. This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) held, but the correct view is otherwise. The correct view is that ﴿min﴾ ("of") is an explanation of ﴿ma﴾ ("what"); that is, what your Lord has created for you of wives; meaning: and you leave the wives. This is the meaning, not "their front passages"; you leave the wives, that is, what Allah has created for you of wives.

There is a difference between what you mentioned and what the author held; it is as if he says, "you leave the private parts of women." But if he had said, "Do you approach the backsides of males?" that would be fine, and "you leave the private parts of women," or not? But since he said ﴿Do you approach males﴾, the fitting continuation would be "and you leave the women," yet he said ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾ instead of "your wives," indicating that Allah has made this wife available to the man to enjoy as he wishes, except in what Allah has forbidden, such as the anus. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 223], and He said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 5–6]. This indicates the permissibility of a man's enjoyment of his wife, an absolute permissibility without limits, except for two matters: the anus, and the vagina during menstruation. Everything else is permitted. This adds to the ugliness of their deed, since they leave the good and approach the evil.

In His words ﴿Do you approach﴾ and ﴿and leave﴾ there is the semantic benefit we indicated, namely the increase in ugliness; and the second, verbal benefit, what is it? It is the antithesis (tibaq) between the matter and its opposite: (approach and leave).

His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾: the lam is for permission or for causation; that is, created for your sake; ﴿created for you﴾ means permitted for you.

His words ﴿your Lord﴾ indicate that He, the Exalted, is the one who disposes of it, who (...).

* The student: the "ma'iyyah" (accompaniment), its meaning...

* The Shaykh: the lam in ﴿lakum﴾ (for you).

His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾: ﴿bal﴾ ("rather") is for turning away from something (idrab). But what is the turning away that occurred? That is, what is it that is being turned away from? It is as if he said: you do not approach males by natural disposition, nor as an ordinary action beloved to the natural dispositions; rather, what has driven you to this is pure transgression, Allah forbid, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. Lot, peace be upon him, made clear that what they did is an action rejected by reason and rejected by the Law and by custom, because transgression is something everyone undoubtedly denies, and these people are transgressors.

It is strange that the one who performs the act among them today was the one acted upon yesterday, and the one acted upon today will become the one who acts in the future.
