In the case of the people of Lot, their specific crime was this immorality; therefore He said: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165–166]. This interrogative is for rebuke and denunciation.

﴿Do you approach males﴾: that is, the males, the plural of (dhakar).

﴿From among the worlds﴾ is an explanation of "males"; that is, from among (people), whether they are from your tribe or from other than your tribe. For this reason he did not say, "Do you approach the males among you," but rather said ﴿from among the worlds﴾, indicating that they, Allah forbid, do not restrain themselves from anyone; they are like dogs. Then, in addition to their wickedness, they abandoned the blessing that Allah created for them: ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾.

If they approached males from among the worlds because they were compelled to, and had no lawful option sufficient for them, the matter would be lighter. But they have lawful options sufficient for them, so how do they approach the wicked things and leave the good things? For this reason He said: ﴿and leave﴾ is included in the meaning of the interrogative; that is, "and do you leave ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾?" (tadharun) means: you abandon ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾; that is, (their private parts) is an explanation of His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾; meaning you approach what has been created for you of wives, which is the front passage. This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) held, but the correct view is otherwise. The correct view is that ﴿min﴾ ("of") is an explanation of ﴿ma﴾ ("what"); that is, what your Lord has created for you of wives; meaning: and you leave the wives. This is the meaning, not "their front passages"; you leave the wives, that is, what Allah has created for you of wives.

There is a difference between what you mentioned and what the author held; it is as if he says, "you leave the private parts of women." But if he had said, "Do you approach the backsides of males?" that would be fine, and "you leave the private parts of women," or not? But since he said ﴿Do you approach males﴾, the fitting continuation would be "and you leave the women," yet he said ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾ instead of "your wives," indicating that Allah has made this wife available to the man to enjoy as he wishes, except in what Allah has forbidden, such as the anus. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 223], and He said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 5–6]. This indicates the permissibility of a man's enjoyment of his wife, an absolute permissibility without limits, except for two matters: the anus, and the vagina during menstruation. Everything else is permitted. This adds to the ugliness of their deed, since they leave the good and approach the evil.

In His words ﴿Do you approach﴾ and ﴿and leave﴾ there is the semantic benefit we indicated, namely the increase in ugliness; and the second, verbal benefit, what is it? It is the antithesis (tibaq) between the matter and its opposite: (approach and leave).

His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾: the lam is for permission or for causation; that is, created for your sake; ﴿created for you﴾ means permitted for you.

His words ﴿your Lord﴾ indicate that He, the Exalted, is the one who disposes of it, who (...).

* The student: the "ma'iyyah" (accompaniment), its meaning...

* The Shaykh: the lam in ﴿lakum﴾ (for you).

His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾: ﴿bal﴾ ("rather") is for turning away from something (idrab). But what is the turning away that occurred? That is, what is it that is being turned away from? It is as if he said: you do not approach males by natural disposition, nor as an ordinary action beloved to the natural dispositions; rather, what has driven you to this is pure transgression, Allah forbid, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. Lot, peace be upon him, made clear that what they did is an action rejected by reason and rejected by the Law and by custom, because transgression is something everyone undoubtedly denies, and these people are transgressors.

It is strange that the one who performs the act among them today was the one acted upon yesterday, and the one acted upon today will become the one who acts in the future. This is the utmost of transgression. Glory be to Allah, how can these people, we ask Allah for safety, see a person's son or younger brother subjected to this immorality and not be concerned about it?! It appears that they practice it openly, as His words indicate: ﴿and you commit in your gatherings the evil﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29]. They are not concerned, Allah forbid, that some of them mount others openly; this is the utmost of anger.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. Next is the answer: (﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, from your denunciation of us, you will surely be among those expelled" from our lands.﴾)

This ugly reply, ﴿If you do not desist﴾ from what? From enjoining good and forbidding evil. This is the meaning of ﴿you will surely be among those expelled﴾. This is more emphatic than saying "we will expel you"; it is as if they threaten him with something more terrifying to him: that we have expelled others, and you will be among those expelled, because we have the power and authority to expel you.

In His words ﴿If you do not desist﴾ there is emphasis by oath, by the lam and by the emphatic nun. The ﴿la-in﴾ ("if indeed") here is introductory to the oath, since this lam paves the way for the oath.

﴿la-takununna﴾ ("you will surely be"): the lam falls in the answer to the oath. The answer present here is for the oath or for the condition?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Now the question is: is it for the oath or for the condition?

* The students: For the oath.

* The Shaykh: For the oath.

And when a condition and an oath gather, omit the answer of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory [to omit].

(﴿He said﴾ to them, Lot, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest﴾, the haters.) This contains a kind of challenge to them; that is, if you expel me, I am content with that, and my expulsion does not concern me. Why? Because I am among those who detest your deed. Does a person who detests the deed of a people want to remain with them? He does not want to remain with them. So it is as if he says: I am not concerned if I leave, because I do not desire to remain with you while you are upon this wicked deed which I hate. And nothing is harder on a person than to remain with a people he despises. Al-Mutanabbi says:

"Among the miseries of this world for the free man is that he sees an enemy whose friendship he cannot avoid."

This is true: to remain with a people whose actions you hate is difficult on the souls. So it is as if he says: I desire this, I am ready for it, and I am not concerned with your expelling me. And in this there is evidence..

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...).

* And there is evidence in it that every believer must detest their deed, the deed of these people, because the messengers detest it. This is the purpose of the plural: ﴿among those who detest﴾, that is, those who detest it. Although he had with him only a few of the believers ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We did not find there except one house of the submitting [to Allah]﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]; meaning, no one believed with him except his household, and not all of them either: his wife was among the disbelievers.

﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. The author says: (from His punishment). There is no doubt that this interpretation is deficient, because ﴿from what they do﴾ means from their action, and also from His punishment. It is not impossible to ask Allah, the Exalted, to save him from this deed, not at all, even though messengers cannot commit it; because the firmly established truth is that they are protected from what diminishes honor and nobility, and the deed of the people of Lot diminishes honor. But he supplicated for himself and his family: ﴿save me and my family﴾. Are his family protected from that? They are not protected. The correct view is that he asked Allah to save him from their deed and from their punishment.

Allah said: ﴿So We saved him and his family entirely﴾. The fa' indicates a consequence: that is, as a consequence of his supplication, it was answered: We saved him and his family entirely.

(﴿except an old woman﴾, his wife, ﴿among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind, We destroyed?)

* A student: (She was destroyed).

* The Shaykh: (She was destroyed.) What I have is better. It seems he intends that "We destroyed" governs his words ﴿an old woman﴾: except an old woman We destroyed; that is, except that We destroyed an old woman. What you have also has a clearer meaning, because if he says, "those who remained, We destroyed," the listener may think that the intended meaning is that He destroyed those who remained.

In any case, Allah answered his supplication and saved him and his family. ﴿entirely﴾ indicates that the family were a large number, although the correct view is that we do not know how many they were; rather, they were his family, but ﴿entirely﴾ indicates multitude, because ﴿entirely﴾ is plural, and the least that is said of a plural is three, yet this word ﴿entirely﴾ indicates a group, a numerous group.

As for His words ﴿except an old woman﴾: look, Allah forbid, this woman was an old woman advanced in years, and it would have been fitting for an elderly person to turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since he is close to death; he is nearer to death than a young person. But, Allah forbid, Allah spared us the evil of old age; the young women became wicked, Allah forbid, disbelievers in Allah, yet they concealed this. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Tahrim: what? He said: ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. It was not a betrayal of lust and fornication, but a betrayal of disbelief. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ ... ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]; they did not make the two aware of their disbelief, so it was not known that they were disbelievers.

* A student: Was she supportive of the people's deed?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is an acknowledgment of disbelief; she was a disbeliever and, in addition, supportive.

The affirmation (﴿except an old woman among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind): "the remaining" (al-ghabirin) is applied to several meanings, among them "the remaining" and also "the past," so it contains what is called the antonyms (al-adhdad), because the language has words suitable for a thing and its opposite; these are called antonyms.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ after We had finished with Lot and his family. ﴿We destroyed the others﴾: because after he was commanded to travel with his family by night and leave the town, except his wife, Allah destroyed this town; that is, he went out, and then it was destroyed.

﴿the others﴾: whom does it refer to? His people. The author said: (We destroyed them).

(﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ of stones. He said: it is part of the destruction.) Part of the destruction is that Allah, the Exalted, rained upon them a rain. Apparently to me, His words ﴿And We rained﴾ are an explanatory conjunction to His words ﴿Then We destroyed﴾, because this is what they were destroyed by: that Allah rained upon them a rain. And what is the rain? ﴿stones of baked clay, layered, marked in the sight of your Lord﴾ [Hud 82]: consecutive, marked by Allah.

He, the Exalted, says: (﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾, their rain). ﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾: that is, the rain of these people. He said ﴿those who were warned﴾ to show that the proof had been established against them, and they were not rained upon with punishment except after they had been given warning.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾. In this verse and in other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by these stones, by destruction with stones, and not by overturning. Is that right?

* A student: In this verse and other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by stones.

* The Shaykh: And not by overturning, as is well known among the scholars and many of the exegetes, that their lands were lifted up to the sky and then overturned. Nothing in the Qur'an indicates this; the Qur'an says only: ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74], and making the high become the low can happen without overturning, for when these stones fell upon the dwellings and demolished them, the high parts of the dwellings became low. Moreover, if they were overturned, for example, and people were beneath the earth, what would be the value of the stones at that point? They would have no value.

The main point is that there is nothing from the Prophet ﷺ indicating that their land was lifted up and overturned. Since nothing indicates that, the better view is that they were destroyed by these stones, and the difficulty in His words ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74] is resolved by our saying: when the houses collapse, the high becomes low; its upper part becomes lower.

* From this story is derived, first: happiness in the monotheism of Allah, and the command to be mindful of Him, and so on; this has been mentioned. And sincerity in calling to Allah, the Exalted, and that the caller should not take a wage for his call. All this has been mentioned, but it is also derived from it that some of the children of Adam have their nature and innate disposition reversed until they find the wicked attractive, because this is their condition.

* And also in it: increase in denunciation when a person has an alternative to the unlawful; because of His words ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you﴾.

* And in the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of enjoying one's wife in an absolute manner; because of His words ﴿what He created for you﴾.

* And there is evidence that whoever goes beyond the lawful to the unlawful is a transgressor who wrongs himself and others; because of His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾.

* And there is evidence that opponents of the messengers resort only to their strength and authority, not to reason and persuasion; because of His words ﴿If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled﴾. The people of Noah said the same: ﴿If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 116], though with a different punishment. Likewise Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29], and Azar said to his son Abraham: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾ [Maryam 46]. All of this shows that those who threaten with authority rather than persuasion and reason have no argument.

* And there is evidence that a person must detest what Allah detests, because this is the way of the messengers: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest."﴾

* And there is evidence that no one can dispense with calling upon Allah: ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. As for the saying of some ignorant "knowers" that His knowledge of my condition suffices instead of my asking, this is a false saying; Allah knows the condition of everyone, yet the messengers and their followers have never ceased to call upon Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

And there is in it evidence for the existence of the Lord, glorified and exalted, from His saying: ﴿My Lord, save me﴾ and ﴿So We saved him﴾. This is clear, observable evidence.

And there is in it evidence that Allah answers supplication. This answering includes several attributes: it includes His knowledge, His power, and His mercy.

And there is in it evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, saves the people of truth and destroys the disbelievers, and He destroys the disbelievers even if they are in the embrace of the people of truth. For Allah saved Lot and destroyed his wife while she was in his embrace. This is the secret behind His saying: ﴿And We brought out whoever was there of the believers. But We found there not a single house other than a house of the Muslims﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]. Consider the Qur'anic expression. Were the believers saved or not? But the Muslim household was not wholly saved. The woman who used to display religion while being a Muslim outwardly was not saved. For this reason He said: ﴿other than a house﴾. From where? ﴿of the Muslims﴾. So that household was Muslim, but not all of them were believers. Among them was that old woman, who was a disbeliever. There is no evidence in the verse, as some people say, that faith is Islam, for there is a difference between this and that.

And in the verse there is also evidence that closeness to the prophets and the saints does not benefit a person at all. From where do we take this? From the fact that this was the wife of a prophet, and yet she perished with those who perished. So a person's being close to a saint of Allah does not benefit him in the least. Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and yet no specific disbeliever was named in the Qur'an except Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And the Qur'an did not name any specific individual among the Muslims except Zayd ibn al-Harith, a client (mawla) from among the clients, who was as far as possible from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Thereby it becomes clear that closeness of lineage, closeness by marriage, and other closeness do not avail a person anything. Reflect on the verse of Surah al-Tahrim, in which a story was revealed: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. ﴿Allah presents an example﴾ is because 'A'isha and Hafsah, who conspired against the Prophet (ﷺ), might be deceived by their closeness to the Messenger (ﷺ) and do what they did. So Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that their connection to the Prophet (ﷺ) would not benefit them.

And in this there is evidence that Allah's punishment varies according to the deed. For here they were rained upon with a rain until their dwellings were demolished and their upper part became their lower part. Then afterwards it was submerged, and therefore it is now a lake called the Lake of Lot, well known.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed, but it is a Dead Sea, because it is not connected to the seas.

Student: (...) the Dead Sea.

Shaykh: And it is also water in which fish and whales live as they live in other waters, but it is not like the others, because they (...) are deep seas, so there is no small or large thing in that.

Student: (...) 'Ad, for example?

Shaykh: Yes, 'Ad is possible on the basis that it was submerged with it.

Some scholars have derived from this story that the sodomite (liwati) is to be killed by being stoned to death, by analogy with Allah's stoning of those people with stones. The matter, as we indicated earlier, is subject to disagreement. Among the scholars is one who said: the sodomite is not to be addressed and nothing is said to him; this is one view. The second view: he is to be disciplined (ta'zir) by beating, imprisonment, and the like. The third view: he is like the adulterer; if he is married (muhsan) he is stoned, and if he is not married he is flogged and exiled. The fourth view: he is to be killed in every case, whether married or not. But how is he to be killed? It was said: by stoning; it was said: by the sword; it was said: by burning; and it was said: by throwing him from a height and following him with stones. This last is the fifth view. I think they are four; the fourth view is the one on which the Companions agreed, that he is to be killed.

First: he is not to be touched. Second: he is to be disciplined. Third: his prescribed punishment is like that of the adulterer. Fourth: he is to be killed in every case. Then they differed over the manner of killing. This last view is the correct and definite one: he is to be killed in every case, whether he is the active or the passive partner, provided he is adult and sane. For this is not like fornication; it is more severe and more grave. Moreover, it is a matter that cannot be guarded against, unlike fornication, which can be guarded against. But this cannot be guarded against. If a wicked man seized the hand of a beardless youth, nobody would say: what is this matter, and why is he holding his hand, and the like? So it is a matter that cannot be guarded against. It occurs in men's gatherings and elsewhere. This is the correct, decisive view.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that the Companions agreed on his killing. As for the one who said he is not to be touched, what is his argument? He said: because this is something that human natures recoil from, and what natures recoil from is sufficiently deterred by natural repulsion. Just as we said: the drinker of urine is not punished, whereas the drinker of wine is flogged, because the soul is drawn to wine, and the soul is not drawn to this.

This is a false view, neither in its root nor its branch. As for his saying, "souls are not drawn to it," we say: this is correct. Sound souls undoubtedly are not drawn to it, and they find it repugnant and abhorrent. But are there not wicked souls?

Student: Yes indeed.

Shaykh: Their desire is greater than for women. Their desire, may Allah protect us, is greater than for women. They abandon their wives in their private parts and go to this shameful act.

Second: his saying that the drinker of urine is not to be disciplined and that natural deterrence suffices, this is also false. Rather, it is obligatory to discipline him for the act. And whoever we see drinking urine, we must discipline him, because he has committed a forbidden act, and discipline (ta'zir) is obligatory for every sin that has no prescribed punishment (hadd) and no expiation (kaffarah). So the correct view is that he is to be killed in every case, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed. No one is punished with fire except Allah, glorified and exalted [narrated by al-Bukhari (2954) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. But it seems they saw, because of the enormity of this act, that the intended punishment by fire applies to matters less than this. Otherwise it did occur with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and with 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. Three of the caliphs, all of them agreed upon it.

Student: The preponderant view?

Shaykh: The preponderant view is stoning.

Student: His saying: (...).

Shaykh: No, there is nothing in it except the words of historians.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: The prescribed punishment for the sodomite; that is, the married one is stoned.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, we have said that his prescribed punishment is killing in every case. That is, if someone of seventeen years commits sodomy, and someone of sixteen years, both are killed, even if they were not married.

Student: This is the narration of the school (madhhab).

Shaykh: The school's position is weak on this question.

Student: (...) the second narration.

Shaykh: Where?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: There is a second view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. I do not know whether there is a narration from Ahmad or a view. That is, there is no strong position for the companions (of Ahmad) in this, and Shaykh al-Islam held it. But whether it is a narration, I do not know.

Student: "These are my daughters" [al-Hijr 71].

Shaykh: Yes, that is, I will marry them to you.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Some exegetes said: "my daughters" means the daughters of the nation, because the Messenger is a father to his people, so he stands in the position of a father to them.

Student: Is this valid?

Shaykh: It is not valid, but what prompted them to this is that they said: his daughters are Muslim believing women, and these are disbelievers, and a disbeliever does not marry a believing woman. It is answered: either their law permits that, or the meaning of "these are my daughters" is: then become Muslims and marry them, and the meaning becomes understood.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: How many are coming? That does not contradict. How many are coming?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: The people have come to his certainty.

Student: The people have come.

Shaykh: Because they went to give each other good news about these people.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes, the point is...

Student: The people of the city came (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed, that does not contradict. But the meaning is not that he will definitely distribute his daughters across the whole city. Rather the meaning is: I will marry you to my daughters, and if a number of you does not marry to match my daughters, the rest will take from the women (...).

Then, in truth, it is as if he were saying: I protect my guests more than I protect anything else. That is, I wish to protect them to the point that I give up my daughters, marrying them off, in order to safeguard these guests?

Student: The evidence of the one who said it was overturned (...)?

Shaykh: On the basis that those villages were lifted up, and then overturned.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers. When their brother Lot said to them...﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 160–161].

The people of Lot lived in a town called Sodom, in the land of Palestine. Lot, as the historians say, was the son of Abraham's brother, so Abraham was his paternal uncle. Allah sent him to the people of this town. Along with their disbelief in Allah, the Exalted, they practiced a vile deed, which is counted among the most wicked of actions, and Allah forbid. Allah named it wicked when He said: ﴿And We saved him from the town that used to commit abominations﴾ [al-Anbiya' 74]. So it is (...), because it is ugly by reason, by natural disposition and by the Law. This deed they did was that they would approach males, Allah forbid, just as they approached women.

Here Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–164]. All of this has already been discussed.

Every messenger is sent first to establish monotheism: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. This is the foundation with which all messengers are sent. However, there are particular kinds of sins committed by some nations, on which the messengers, peace be upon them, focus. In the case of the people of Lot, their specific crime was this immorality; therefore He said: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165–166]. This interrogative is for rebuke and denunciation.

﴿Do you approach males﴾: that is, the males, the plural of (dhakar).

﴿From among the worlds﴾ is an explanation of "males"; that is, from among (people), whether they are from your tribe or from other than your tribe. For this reason he did not say, "Do you approach the males among you," but rather said ﴿from among the worlds﴾, indicating that they, Allah forbid, do not restrain themselves from anyone; they are like dogs. Then, in addition to their wickedness, they abandoned the blessing that Allah created for them: ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾.

If they approached males from among the worlds because they were compelled to, and had no lawful option sufficient for them, the matter would be lighter. But they have lawful options sufficient for them, so how do they approach the wicked things and leave the good things? For this reason He said: ﴿and leave﴾ is included in the meaning of the interrogative; that is, "and do you leave ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾?" (tadharun) means: you abandon ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾; that is, (their private parts) is an explanation of His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾; meaning you approach what has been created for you of wives, which is the front passage. This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) held, but the correct view is otherwise. The correct view is that ﴿min﴾ ("of") is an explanation of ﴿ma﴾ ("what"); that is, what your Lord has created for you of wives; meaning: and you leave the wives. This is the meaning, not "their front passages"; you leave the wives, that is, what Allah has created for you of wives.

There is a difference between what you mentioned and what the author held; it is as if he says, "you leave the private parts of women." But if he had said, "Do you approach the backsides of males?" that would be fine, and "you leave the private parts of women," or not? But since he said ﴿Do you approach males﴾, the fitting continuation would be "and you leave the women," yet he said ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾ instead of "your wives," indicating that Allah has made this wife available to the man to enjoy as he wishes, except in what Allah has forbidden, such as the anus. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 223], and He said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 5–6]. This indicates the permissibility of a man's enjoyment of his wife, an absolute permissibility without limits, except for two matters: the anus, and the vagina during menstruation. Everything else is permitted. This adds to the ugliness of their deed, since they leave the good and approach the evil.

In His words ﴿Do you approach﴾ and ﴿and leave﴾ there is the semantic benefit we indicated, namely the increase in ugliness; and the second, verbal benefit, what is it? It is the antithesis (tibaq) between the matter and its opposite: (approach and leave).

His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾: the lam is for permission or for causation; that is, created for your sake; ﴿created for you﴾ means permitted for you.

His words ﴿your Lord﴾ indicate that He, the Exalted, is the one who disposes of it, who (...).

* The student: the "ma'iyyah" (accompaniment), its meaning...

* The Shaykh: the lam in ﴿lakum﴾ (for you).

His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾: ﴿bal﴾ ("rather") is for turning away from something (idrab). But what is the turning away that occurred? That is, what is it that is being turned away from? It is as if he said: you do not approach males by natural disposition, nor as an ordinary action beloved to the natural dispositions; rather, what has driven you to this is pure transgression, Allah forbid, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. Lot, peace be upon him, made clear that what they did is an action rejected by reason and rejected by the Law and by custom, because transgression is something everyone undoubtedly denies, and these people are transgressors.

It is strange that the one who performs the act among them today was the one acted upon yesterday, and the one acted upon today will become the one who acts in the future. This is the utmost of transgression. Glory be to Allah, how can these people, we ask Allah for safety, see a person's son or younger brother subjected to this immorality and not be concerned about it?! It appears that they practice it openly, as His words indicate: ﴿and you commit in your gatherings the evil﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29]. They are not concerned, Allah forbid, that some of them mount others openly; this is the utmost of anger.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. Next is the answer: (﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, from your denunciation of us, you will surely be among those expelled" from our lands.﴾)

This ugly reply, ﴿If you do not desist﴾ from what? From enjoining good and forbidding evil. This is the meaning of ﴿you will surely be among those expelled﴾. This is more emphatic than saying "we will expel you"; it is as if they threaten him with something more terrifying to him: that we have expelled others, and you will be among those expelled, because we have the power and authority to expel you.

In His words ﴿If you do not desist﴾ there is emphasis by oath, by the lam and by the emphatic nun. The ﴿la-in﴾ ("if indeed") here is introductory to the oath, since this lam paves the way for the oath.

﴿la-takununna﴾ ("you will surely be"): the lam falls in the answer to the oath. The answer present here is for the oath or for the condition?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Now the question is: is it for the oath or for the condition?

* The students: For the oath.

* The Shaykh: For the oath.

And when a condition and an oath gather, omit the answer of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory [to omit].

(﴿He said﴾ to them, Lot, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest﴾, the haters.) This contains a kind of challenge to them; that is, if you expel me, I am content with that, and my expulsion does not concern me. Why? Because I am among those who detest your deed. Does a person who detests the deed of a people want to remain with them? He does not want to remain with them. So it is as if he says: I am not concerned if I leave, because I do not desire to remain with you while you are upon this wicked deed which I hate. And nothing is harder on a person than to remain with a people he despises. Al-Mutanabbi says:

"Among the miseries of this world for the free man is that he sees an enemy whose friendship he cannot avoid."

This is true: to remain with a people whose actions you hate is difficult on the souls. So it is as if he says: I desire this, I am ready for it, and I am not concerned with your expelling me. And in this there is evidence..

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...).

* And there is evidence in it that every believer must detest their deed, the deed of these people, because the messengers detest it. This is the purpose of the plural: ﴿among those who detest﴾, that is, those who detest it. Although he had with him only a few of the believers ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We did not find there except one house of the submitting [to Allah]﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]; meaning, no one believed with him except his household, and not all of them either: his wife was among the disbelievers.

﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. The author says: (from His punishment). There is no doubt that this interpretation is deficient, because ﴿from what they do﴾ means from their action, and also from His punishment. It is not impossible to ask Allah, the Exalted, to save him from this deed, not at all, even though messengers cannot commit it; because the firmly established truth is that they are protected from what diminishes honor and nobility, and the deed of the people of Lot diminishes honor. But he supplicated for himself and his family: ﴿save me and my family﴾. Are his family protected from that? They are not protected. The correct view is that he asked Allah to save him from their deed and from their punishment.

Allah said: ﴿So We saved him and his family entirely﴾. The fa' indicates a consequence: that is, as a consequence of his supplication, it was answered: We saved him and his family entirely.

(﴿except an old woman﴾, his wife, ﴿among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind, We destroyed?)

* A student: (She was destroyed).

* The Shaykh: (She was destroyed.) What I have is better. It seems he intends that "We destroyed" governs his words ﴿an old woman﴾: except an old woman We destroyed; that is, except that We destroyed an old woman. What you have also has a clearer meaning, because if he says, "those who remained, We destroyed," the listener may think that the intended meaning is that He destroyed those who remained.

In any case, Allah answered his supplication and saved him and his family. ﴿entirely﴾ indicates that the family were a large number, although the correct view is that we do not know how many they were; rather, they were his family, but ﴿entirely﴾ indicates multitude, because ﴿entirely﴾ is plural, and the least that is said of a plural is three, yet this word ﴿entirely﴾ indicates a group, a numerous group.

As for His words ﴿except an old woman﴾: look, Allah forbid, this woman was an old woman advanced in years, and it would have been fitting for an elderly person to turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since he is close to death; he is nearer to death than a young person. But, Allah forbid, Allah spared us the evil of old age; the young women became wicked, Allah forbid, disbelievers in Allah, yet they concealed this. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Tahrim: what? He said: ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. It was not a betrayal of lust and fornication, but a betrayal of disbelief. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ ... ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]; they did not make the two aware of their disbelief, so it was not known that they were disbelievers.

* A student: Was she supportive of the people's deed?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is an acknowledgment of disbelief; she was a disbeliever and, in addition, supportive.

The affirmation (﴿except an old woman among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind): "the remaining" (al-ghabirin) is applied to several meanings, among them "the remaining" and also "the past," so it contains what is called the antonyms (al-adhdad), because the language has words suitable for a thing and its opposite; these are called antonyms.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ after We had finished with Lot and his family. ﴿We destroyed the others﴾: because after he was commanded to travel with his family by night and leave the town, except his wife, Allah destroyed this town; that is, he went out, and then it was destroyed.

﴿the others﴾: whom does it refer to? His people. The author said: (We destroyed them).

(﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ of stones. He said: it is part of the destruction.) Part of the destruction is that Allah, the Exalted, rained upon them a rain. Apparently to me, His words ﴿And We rained﴾ are an explanatory conjunction to His words ﴿Then We destroyed﴾, because this is what they were destroyed by: that Allah rained upon them a rain. And what is the rain? ﴿stones of baked clay, layered, marked in the sight of your Lord﴾ [Hud 82]: consecutive, marked by Allah.

He, the Exalted, says: (﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾, their rain). ﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾: that is, the rain of these people. He said ﴿those who were warned﴾ to show that the proof had been established against them, and they were not rained upon with punishment except after they had been given warning.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾. In this verse and in other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by these stones, by destruction with stones, and not by overturning. Is that right?

* A student: In this verse and other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by stones.

* The Shaykh: And not by overturning, as is well known among the scholars and many of the exegetes, that their lands were lifted up to the sky and then overturned. Nothing in the Qur'an indicates this; the Qur'an says only: ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74], and making the high become the low can happen without overturning, for when these stones fell upon the dwellings and demolished them, the high parts of the dwellings became low. Moreover, if they were overturned, for example, and people were beneath the earth, what would be the value of the stones at that point? They would have no value.

The main point is that there is nothing from the Prophet ﷺ indicating that their land was lifted up and overturned. Since nothing indicates that, the better view is that they were destroyed by these stones, and the difficulty in His words ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74] is resolved by our saying: when the houses collapse, the high becomes low; its upper part becomes lower.

* From this story is derived, first: happiness in the monotheism of Allah, and the command to be mindful of Him, and so on; this has been mentioned. And sincerity in calling to Allah, the Exalted, and that the caller should not take a wage for his call. All this has been mentioned, but it is also derived from it that some of the children of Adam have their nature and innate disposition reversed until they find the wicked attractive, because this is their condition.

* And also in it: increase in denunciation when a person has an alternative to the unlawful; because of His words ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you﴾.

* And in the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of enjoying one's wife in an absolute manner; because of His words ﴿what He created for you﴾.

* And there is evidence that whoever goes beyond the lawful to the unlawful is a transgressor who wrongs himself and others; because of His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾.

* And there is evidence that opponents of the messengers resort only to their strength and authority, not to reason and persuasion; because of His words ﴿If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled﴾. The people of Noah said the same: ﴿If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 116], though with a different punishment. Likewise Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29], and Azar said to his son Abraham: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾ [Maryam 46]. All of this shows that those who threaten with authority rather than persuasion and reason have no argument.

* And there is evidence that a person must detest what Allah detests, because this is the way of the messengers: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest."﴾

* And there is evidence that no one can dispense with calling upon Allah: ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. As for the saying of some ignorant "knowers" that His knowledge of my condition suffices instead of my asking, this is a false saying; Allah knows the condition of everyone, yet the messengers and their followers have never ceased to call upon Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

And there is in it evidence for the existence of the Lord, glorified and exalted, from His saying: ﴿My Lord, save me﴾ and ﴿So We saved him﴾. This is clear, observable evidence.

And there is in it evidence that Allah answers supplication. This answering includes several attributes: it includes His knowledge, His power, and His mercy.

And there is in it evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, saves the people of truth and destroys the disbelievers, and He destroys the disbelievers even if they are in the embrace of the people of truth. For Allah saved Lot and destroyed his wife while she was in his embrace. This is the secret behind His saying: ﴿And We brought out whoever was there of the believers. But We found there not a single house other than a house of the Muslims﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]. Consider the Qur'anic expression. Were the believers saved or not? But the Muslim household was not wholly saved. The woman who used to display religion while being a Muslim outwardly was not saved. For this reason He said: ﴿other than a house﴾. From where? ﴿of the Muslims﴾. So that household was Muslim, but not all of them were believers. Among them was that old woman, who was a disbeliever. There is no evidence in the verse, as some people say, that faith is Islam, for there is a difference between this and that.

And in the verse there is also evidence that closeness to the prophets and the saints does not benefit a person at all. From where do we take this? From the fact that this was the wife of a prophet, and yet she perished with those who perished. So a person's being close to a saint of Allah does not benefit him in the least. Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and yet no specific disbeliever was named in the Qur'an except Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And the Qur'an did not name any specific individual among the Muslims except Zayd ibn al-Harith, a client (mawla) from among the clients, who was as far as possible from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Thereby it becomes clear that closeness of lineage, closeness by marriage, and other closeness do not avail a person anything. Reflect on the verse of Surah al-Tahrim, in which a story was revealed: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. ﴿Allah presents an example﴾ is because 'A'isha and Hafsah, who conspired against the Prophet (ﷺ), might be deceived by their closeness to the Messenger (ﷺ) and do what they did. So Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that their connection to the Prophet (ﷺ) would not benefit them.

And in this there is evidence that Allah's punishment varies according to the deed. For here they were rained upon with a rain until their dwellings were demolished and their upper part became their lower part. Then afterwards it was submerged, and therefore it is now a lake called the Lake of Lot, well known.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed, but it is a Dead Sea, because it is not connected to the seas.

Student: (...) the Dead Sea.

Shaykh: And it is also water in which fish and whales live as they live in other waters, but it is not like the others, because they (...) are deep seas, so there is no small or large thing in that.

Student: (...) 'Ad, for example?

Shaykh: Yes, 'Ad is possible on the basis that it was submerged with it.

Some scholars have derived from this story that the sodomite (liwati) is to be killed by being stoned to death, by analogy with Allah's stoning of those people with stones. The matter, as we indicated earlier, is subject to disagreement. Among the scholars is one who said: the sodomite is not to be addressed and nothing is said to him; this is one view. The second view: he is to be disciplined (ta'zir) by beating, imprisonment, and the like. The third view: he is like the adulterer; if he is married (muhsan) he is stoned, and if he is not married he is flogged and exiled. The fourth view: he is to be killed in every case, whether married or not. But how is he to be killed? It was said: by stoning; it was said: by the sword; it was said: by burning; and it was said: by throwing him from a height and following him with stones. This last is the fifth view. I think they are four; the fourth view is the one on which the Companions agreed, that he is to be killed.

First: he is not to be touched. Second: he is to be disciplined. Third: his prescribed punishment is like that of the adulterer. Fourth: he is to be killed in every case. Then they differed over the manner of killing. This last view is the correct and definite one: he is to be killed in every case, whether he is the active or the passive partner, provided he is adult and sane. For this is not like fornication; it is more severe and more grave. Moreover, it is a matter that cannot be guarded against, unlike fornication, which can be guarded against. But this cannot be guarded against. If a wicked man seized the hand of a beardless youth, nobody would say: what is this matter, and why is he holding his hand, and the like? So it is a matter that cannot be guarded against. It occurs in men's gatherings and elsewhere. This is the correct, decisive view.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that the Companions agreed on his killing. As for the one who said he is not to be touched, what is his argument? He said: because this is something that human natures recoil from, and what natures recoil from is sufficiently deterred by natural repulsion. Just as we said: the drinker of urine is not punished, whereas the drinker of wine is flogged, because the soul is drawn to wine, and the soul is not drawn to this.

This is a false view, neither in its root nor its branch. As for his saying, "souls are not drawn to it," we say: this is correct. Sound souls undoubtedly are not drawn to it, and they find it repugnant and abhorrent. But are there not wicked souls?

Student: Yes indeed.

Shaykh: Their desire is greater than for women. Their desire, may Allah protect us, is greater than for women. They abandon their wives in their private parts and go to this shameful act.

Second: his saying that the drinker of urine is not to be disciplined and that natural deterrence suffices, this is also false. Rather, it is obligatory to discipline him for the act. And whoever we see drinking urine, we must discipline him, because he has committed a forbidden act, and discipline (ta'zir) is obligatory for every sin that has no prescribed punishment (hadd) and no expiation (kaffarah). So the correct view is that he is to be killed in every case, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed. No one is punished with fire except Allah, glorified and exalted [narrated by al-Bukhari (2954) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. But it seems they saw, because of the enormity of this act, that the intended punishment by fire applies to matters less than this. Otherwise it did occur with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and with 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. Three of the caliphs, all of them agreed upon it.

Student: The preponderant view?

Shaykh: The preponderant view is stoning.

Student: His saying: (...).

Shaykh: No, there is nothing in it except the words of historians.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: The prescribed punishment for the sodomite; that is, the married one is stoned.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, we have said that his prescribed punishment is killing in every case. That is, if someone of seventeen years commits sodomy, and someone of sixteen years, both are killed, even if they were not married.

Student: This is the narration of the school (madhhab).

Shaykh: The school's position is weak on this question.

Student: (...) the second narration.

Shaykh: Where?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: There is a second view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. I do not know whether there is a narration from Ahmad or a view. That is, there is no strong position for the companions (of Ahmad) in this, and Shaykh al-Islam held it. But whether it is a narration, I do not know.

Student: "These are my daughters" [al-Hijr 71].

Shaykh: Yes, that is, I will marry them to you.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Some exegetes said: "my daughters" means the daughters of the nation, because the Messenger is a father to his people, so he stands in the position of a father to them.

Student: Is this valid?

Shaykh: It is not valid, but what prompted them to this is that they said: his daughters are Muslim believing women, and these are disbelievers, and a disbeliever does not marry a believing woman. It is answered: either their law permits that, or the meaning of "these are my daughters" is: then become Muslims and marry them, and the meaning becomes understood.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: How many are coming? That does not contradict. How many are coming?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: The people have come to his certainty.

Student: The people have come.

Shaykh: Because they went to give each other good news about these people.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes, the point is...

Student: The people of the city came (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed, that does not contradict. But the meaning is not that he will definitely distribute his daughters across the whole city. Rather the meaning is: I will marry you to my daughters, and if a number of you does not marry to match my daughters, the rest will take from the women (...).

Then, in truth, it is as if he were saying: I protect my guests more than I protect anything else. That is, I wish to protect them to the point that I give up my daughters, marrying them off, in order to safeguard these guests?

Student: The evidence of the one who said it was overturned (...)?

Shaykh: On the basis that those villages were lifted up, and then overturned.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿The people of Lot denied the messengers. When their brother Lot said to them...﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 160–161].

The people of Lot lived in a town called Sodom, in the land of Palestine. Lot, as the historians say, was the son of Abraham's brother, so Abraham was his paternal uncle. Allah sent him to the people of this town. Along with their disbelief in Allah, the Exalted, they practiced a vile deed, which is counted among the most wicked of actions, and Allah forbid. Allah named it wicked when He said: ﴿And We saved him from the town that used to commit abominations﴾ [al-Anbiya' 74]. So it is (...), because it is ugly by reason, by natural disposition and by the Law. This deed they did was that they would approach males, Allah forbid, just as they approached women.

Here Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah? Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allah and obey me. And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 161–164]. All of this has already been discussed.

Every messenger is sent first to establish monotheism: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid Taghut"﴾ [al-Nahl 36]. This is the foundation with which all messengers are sent. However, there are particular kinds of sins committed by some nations, on which the messengers, peace be upon them, focus. In the case of the people of Lot, their specific crime was this immorality; therefore He said: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives?﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 165–166]. This interrogative is for rebuke and denunciation.

﴿Do you approach males﴾: that is, the males, the plural of (dhakar).

﴿From among the worlds﴾ is an explanation of "males"; that is, from among (people), whether they are from your tribe or from other than your tribe. For this reason he did not say, "Do you approach the males among you," but rather said ﴿from among the worlds﴾, indicating that they, Allah forbid, do not restrain themselves from anyone; they are like dogs. Then, in addition to their wickedness, they abandoned the blessing that Allah created for them: ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾.

If they approached males from among the worlds because they were compelled to, and had no lawful option sufficient for them, the matter would be lighter. But they have lawful options sufficient for them, so how do they approach the wicked things and leave the good things? For this reason He said: ﴿and leave﴾ is included in the meaning of the interrogative; that is, "and do you leave ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾?" (tadharun) means: you abandon ﴿what your Lord has created for you of your wives﴾; that is, (their private parts) is an explanation of His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾; meaning you approach what has been created for you of wives, which is the front passage. This is what the author (al-Mu'allif) held, but the correct view is otherwise. The correct view is that ﴿min﴾ ("of") is an explanation of ﴿ma﴾ ("what"); that is, what your Lord has created for you of wives; meaning: and you leave the wives. This is the meaning, not "their front passages"; you leave the wives, that is, what Allah has created for you of wives.

There is a difference between what you mentioned and what the author held; it is as if he says, "you leave the private parts of women." But if he had said, "Do you approach the backsides of males?" that would be fine, and "you leave the private parts of women," or not? But since he said ﴿Do you approach males﴾, the fitting continuation would be "and you leave the women," yet he said ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾ instead of "your wives," indicating that Allah has made this wife available to the man to enjoy as he wishes, except in what Allah has forbidden, such as the anus. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth however you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 223], and He said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 5–6]. This indicates the permissibility of a man's enjoyment of his wife, an absolute permissibility without limits, except for two matters: the anus, and the vagina during menstruation. Everything else is permitted. This adds to the ugliness of their deed, since they leave the good and approach the evil.

In His words ﴿Do you approach﴾ and ﴿and leave﴾ there is the semantic benefit we indicated, namely the increase in ugliness; and the second, verbal benefit, what is it? It is the antithesis (tibaq) between the matter and its opposite: (approach and leave).

His words ﴿what your Lord has created for you﴾: the lam is for permission or for causation; that is, created for your sake; ﴿created for you﴾ means permitted for you.

His words ﴿your Lord﴾ indicate that He, the Exalted, is the one who disposes of it, who (...).

* The student: the "ma'iyyah" (accompaniment), its meaning...

* The Shaykh: the lam in ﴿lakum﴾ (for you).

His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾: ﴿bal﴾ ("rather") is for turning away from something (idrab). But what is the turning away that occurred? That is, what is it that is being turned away from? It is as if he said: you do not approach males by natural disposition, nor as an ordinary action beloved to the natural dispositions; rather, what has driven you to this is pure transgression, Allah forbid, going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. Lot, peace be upon him, made clear that what they did is an action rejected by reason and rejected by the Law and by custom, because transgression is something everyone undoubtedly denies, and these people are transgressors.

It is strange that the one who performs the act among them today was the one acted upon yesterday, and the one acted upon today will become the one who acts in the future. This is the utmost of transgression. Glory be to Allah, how can these people, we ask Allah for safety, see a person's son or younger brother subjected to this immorality and not be concerned about it?! It appears that they practice it openly, as His words indicate: ﴿and you commit in your gatherings the evil﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29]. They are not concerned, Allah forbid, that some of them mount others openly; this is the utmost of anger.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. Next is the answer: (﴿They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, from your denunciation of us, you will surely be among those expelled" from our lands.﴾)

This ugly reply, ﴿If you do not desist﴾ from what? From enjoining good and forbidding evil. This is the meaning of ﴿you will surely be among those expelled﴾. This is more emphatic than saying "we will expel you"; it is as if they threaten him with something more terrifying to him: that we have expelled others, and you will be among those expelled, because we have the power and authority to expel you.

In His words ﴿If you do not desist﴾ there is emphasis by oath, by the lam and by the emphatic nun. The ﴿la-in﴾ ("if indeed") here is introductory to the oath, since this lam paves the way for the oath.

﴿la-takununna﴾ ("you will surely be"): the lam falls in the answer to the oath. The answer present here is for the oath or for the condition?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Now the question is: is it for the oath or for the condition?

* The students: For the oath.

* The Shaykh: For the oath.

And when a condition and an oath gather, omit the answer of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory [to omit].

(﴿He said﴾ to them, Lot, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest﴾, the haters.) This contains a kind of challenge to them; that is, if you expel me, I am content with that, and my expulsion does not concern me. Why? Because I am among those who detest your deed. Does a person who detests the deed of a people want to remain with them? He does not want to remain with them. So it is as if he says: I am not concerned if I leave, because I do not desire to remain with you while you are upon this wicked deed which I hate. And nothing is harder on a person than to remain with a people he despises. Al-Mutanabbi says:

"Among the miseries of this world for the free man is that he sees an enemy whose friendship he cannot avoid."

This is true: to remain with a people whose actions you hate is difficult on the souls. So it is as if he says: I desire this, I am ready for it, and I am not concerned with your expelling me. And in this there is evidence..

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...).

* And there is evidence in it that every believer must detest their deed, the deed of these people, because the messengers detest it. This is the purpose of the plural: ﴿among those who detest﴾, that is, those who detest it. Although he had with him only a few of the believers ﴿So We brought out those who were in it of the believers. But We did not find there except one house of the submitting [to Allah]﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]; meaning, no one believed with him except his household, and not all of them either: his wife was among the disbelievers.

﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. The author says: (from His punishment). There is no doubt that this interpretation is deficient, because ﴿from what they do﴾ means from their action, and also from His punishment. It is not impossible to ask Allah, the Exalted, to save him from this deed, not at all, even though messengers cannot commit it; because the firmly established truth is that they are protected from what diminishes honor and nobility, and the deed of the people of Lot diminishes honor. But he supplicated for himself and his family: ﴿save me and my family﴾. Are his family protected from that? They are not protected. The correct view is that he asked Allah to save him from their deed and from their punishment.

Allah said: ﴿So We saved him and his family entirely﴾. The fa' indicates a consequence: that is, as a consequence of his supplication, it was answered: We saved him and his family entirely.

(﴿except an old woman﴾, his wife, ﴿among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind, We destroyed?)

* A student: (She was destroyed).

* The Shaykh: (She was destroyed.) What I have is better. It seems he intends that "We destroyed" governs his words ﴿an old woman﴾: except an old woman We destroyed; that is, except that We destroyed an old woman. What you have also has a clearer meaning, because if he says, "those who remained, We destroyed," the listener may think that the intended meaning is that He destroyed those who remained.

In any case, Allah answered his supplication and saved him and his family. ﴿entirely﴾ indicates that the family were a large number, although the correct view is that we do not know how many they were; rather, they were his family, but ﴿entirely﴾ indicates multitude, because ﴿entirely﴾ is plural, and the least that is said of a plural is three, yet this word ﴿entirely﴾ indicates a group, a numerous group.

As for His words ﴿except an old woman﴾: look, Allah forbid, this woman was an old woman advanced in years, and it would have been fitting for an elderly person to turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since he is close to death; he is nearer to death than a young person. But, Allah forbid, Allah spared us the evil of old age; the young women became wicked, Allah forbid, disbelievers in Allah, yet they concealed this. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Tahrim: what? He said: ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. It was not a betrayal of lust and fornication, but a betrayal of disbelief. For this reason He said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ ... ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]; they did not make the two aware of their disbelief, so it was not known that they were disbelievers.

* A student: Was she supportive of the people's deed?

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is an acknowledgment of disbelief; she was a disbeliever and, in addition, supportive.

The affirmation (﴿except an old woman among those who remained﴾, the ones left behind): "the remaining" (al-ghabirin) is applied to several meanings, among them "the remaining" and also "the past," so it contains what is called the antonyms (al-adhdad), because the language has words suitable for a thing and its opposite; these are called antonyms.

﴿Then We destroyed the others﴾ after We had finished with Lot and his family. ﴿We destroyed the others﴾: because after he was commanded to travel with his family by night and leave the town, except his wife, Allah destroyed this town; that is, he went out, and then it was destroyed.

﴿the others﴾: whom does it refer to? His people. The author said: (We destroyed them).

(﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾ of stones. He said: it is part of the destruction.) Part of the destruction is that Allah, the Exalted, rained upon them a rain. Apparently to me, His words ﴿And We rained﴾ are an explanatory conjunction to His words ﴿Then We destroyed﴾, because this is what they were destroyed by: that Allah rained upon them a rain. And what is the rain? ﴿stones of baked clay, layered, marked in the sight of your Lord﴾ [Hud 82]: consecutive, marked by Allah.

He, the Exalted, says: (﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾, their rain). ﴿So evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾: that is, the rain of these people. He said ﴿those who were warned﴾ to show that the proof had been established against them, and they were not rained upon with punishment except after they had been given warning.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾. In this verse and in other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by these stones, by destruction with stones, and not by overturning. Is that right?

* A student: In this verse and other verses there is indication that the people of Lot were destroyed by stones.

* The Shaykh: And not by overturning, as is well known among the scholars and many of the exegetes, that their lands were lifted up to the sky and then overturned. Nothing in the Qur'an indicates this; the Qur'an says only: ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74], and making the high become the low can happen without overturning, for when these stones fell upon the dwellings and demolished them, the high parts of the dwellings became low. Moreover, if they were overturned, for example, and people were beneath the earth, what would be the value of the stones at that point? They would have no value.

The main point is that there is nothing from the Prophet ﷺ indicating that their land was lifted up and overturned. Since nothing indicates that, the better view is that they were destroyed by these stones, and the difficulty in His words ﴿So We made its highest its lowest﴾ [al-Hijr 74] is resolved by our saying: when the houses collapse, the high becomes low; its upper part becomes lower.

* From this story is derived, first: happiness in the monotheism of Allah, and the command to be mindful of Him, and so on; this has been mentioned. And sincerity in calling to Allah, the Exalted, and that the caller should not take a wage for his call. All this has been mentioned, but it is also derived from it that some of the children of Adam have their nature and innate disposition reversed until they find the wicked attractive, because this is their condition.

* And also in it: increase in denunciation when a person has an alternative to the unlawful; because of His words ﴿and leave what your Lord has created for you﴾.

* And in the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of enjoying one's wife in an absolute manner; because of His words ﴿what He created for you﴾.

* And there is evidence that whoever goes beyond the lawful to the unlawful is a transgressor who wrongs himself and others; because of His words ﴿Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾.

* And there is evidence that opponents of the messengers resort only to their strength and authority, not to reason and persuasion; because of His words ﴿If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be among those expelled﴾. The people of Noah said the same: ﴿If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 116], though with a different punishment. Likewise Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among the imprisoned﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 29], and Azar said to his son Abraham: ﴿If you do not desist, I will surely stone you﴾ [Maryam 46]. All of this shows that those who threaten with authority rather than persuasion and reason have no argument.

* And there is evidence that a person must detest what Allah detests, because this is the way of the messengers: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am, of your deed, among those who detest."﴾

* And there is evidence that no one can dispense with calling upon Allah: ﴿My Lord, save me and my family from what they do﴾. As for the saying of some ignorant "knowers" that His knowledge of my condition suffices instead of my asking, this is a false saying; Allah knows the condition of everyone, yet the messengers and their followers have never ceased to call upon Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.

And there is in it evidence for the existence of the Lord, glorified and exalted, from His saying: ﴿My Lord, save me﴾ and ﴿So We saved him﴾. This is clear, observable evidence.

And there is in it evidence that Allah answers supplication. This answering includes several attributes: it includes His knowledge, His power, and His mercy.

And there is in it evidence that Allah, glorified and exalted, saves the people of truth and destroys the disbelievers, and He destroys the disbelievers even if they are in the embrace of the people of truth. For Allah saved Lot and destroyed his wife while she was in his embrace. This is the secret behind His saying: ﴿And We brought out whoever was there of the believers. But We found there not a single house other than a house of the Muslims﴾ [al-Dhariyat 35–36]. Consider the Qur'anic expression. Were the believers saved or not? But the Muslim household was not wholly saved. The woman who used to display religion while being a Muslim outwardly was not saved. For this reason He said: ﴿other than a house﴾. From where? ﴿of the Muslims﴾. So that household was Muslim, but not all of them were believers. Among them was that old woman, who was a disbeliever. There is no evidence in the verse, as some people say, that faith is Islam, for there is a difference between this and that.

And in the verse there is also evidence that closeness to the prophets and the saints does not benefit a person at all. From where do we take this? From the fact that this was the wife of a prophet, and yet she perished with those who perished. So a person's being close to a saint of Allah does not benefit him in the least. Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and yet no specific disbeliever was named in the Qur'an except Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. And the Qur'an did not name any specific individual among the Muslims except Zayd ibn al-Harith, a client (mawla) from among the clients, who was as far as possible from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Thereby it becomes clear that closeness of lineage, closeness by marriage, and other closeness do not avail a person anything. Reflect on the verse of Surah al-Tahrim, in which a story was revealed: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim 10]. ﴿Allah presents an example﴾ is because 'A'isha and Hafsah, who conspired against the Prophet (ﷺ), might be deceived by their closeness to the Messenger (ﷺ) and do what they did. So Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that their connection to the Prophet (ﷺ) would not benefit them.

And in this there is evidence that Allah's punishment varies according to the deed. For here they were rained upon with a rain until their dwellings were demolished and their upper part became their lower part. Then afterwards it was submerged, and therefore it is now a lake called the Lake of Lot, well known.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed, but it is a Dead Sea, because it is not connected to the seas.

Student: (...) the Dead Sea.

Shaykh: And it is also water in which fish and whales live as they live in other waters, but it is not like the others, because they (...) are deep seas, so there is no small or large thing in that.

Student: (...) 'Ad, for example?

Shaykh: Yes, 'Ad is possible on the basis that it was submerged with it.

Some scholars have derived from this story that the sodomite (liwati) is to be killed by being stoned to death, by analogy with Allah's stoning of those people with stones. The matter, as we indicated earlier, is subject to disagreement. Among the scholars is one who said: the sodomite is not to be addressed and nothing is said to him; this is one view. The second view: he is to be disciplined (ta'zir) by beating, imprisonment, and the like. The third view: he is like the adulterer; if he is married (muhsan) he is stoned, and if he is not married he is flogged and exiled. The fourth view: he is to be killed in every case, whether married or not. But how is he to be killed? It was said: by stoning; it was said: by the sword; it was said: by burning; and it was said: by throwing him from a height and following him with stones. This last is the fifth view. I think they are four; the fourth view is the one on which the Companions agreed, that he is to be killed.

First: he is not to be touched. Second: he is to be disciplined. Third: his prescribed punishment is like that of the adulterer. Fourth: he is to be killed in every case. Then they differed over the manner of killing. This last view is the correct and definite one: he is to be killed in every case, whether he is the active or the passive partner, provided he is adult and sane. For this is not like fornication; it is more severe and more grave. Moreover, it is a matter that cannot be guarded against, unlike fornication, which can be guarded against. But this cannot be guarded against. If a wicked man seized the hand of a beardless youth, nobody would say: what is this matter, and why is he holding his hand, and the like? So it is a matter that cannot be guarded against. It occurs in men's gatherings and elsewhere. This is the correct, decisive view.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned that the Companions agreed on his killing. As for the one who said he is not to be touched, what is his argument? He said: because this is something that human natures recoil from, and what natures recoil from is sufficiently deterred by natural repulsion. Just as we said: the drinker of urine is not punished, whereas the drinker of wine is flogged, because the soul is drawn to wine, and the soul is not drawn to this.

This is a false view, neither in its root nor its branch. As for his saying, "souls are not drawn to it," we say: this is correct. Sound souls undoubtedly are not drawn to it, and they find it repugnant and abhorrent. But are there not wicked souls?

Student: Yes indeed.

Shaykh: Their desire is greater than for women. Their desire, may Allah protect us, is greater than for women. They abandon their wives in their private parts and go to this shameful act.

Second: his saying that the drinker of urine is not to be disciplined and that natural deterrence suffices, this is also false. Rather, it is obligatory to discipline him for the act. And whoever we see drinking urine, we must discipline him, because he has committed a forbidden act, and discipline (ta'zir) is obligatory for every sin that has no prescribed punishment (hadd) and no expiation (kaffarah). So the correct view is that he is to be killed in every case, and Allah is the One sought for help.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes indeed. No one is punished with fire except Allah, glorified and exalted [narrated by al-Bukhari (2954) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. But it seems they saw, because of the enormity of this act, that the intended punishment by fire applies to matters less than this. Otherwise it did occur with Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and with 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. Three of the caliphs, all of them agreed upon it.

Student: The preponderant view?

Shaykh: The preponderant view is stoning.

Student: His saying: (...).

Shaykh: No, there is nothing in it except the words of historians.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: The prescribed punishment for the sodomite; that is, the married one is stoned.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, we have said that his prescribed punishment is killing in every case. That is, if someone of seventeen years commits sodomy, and someone of sixteen years, both are killed, even if they were not married.

Student: This is the narration of the school (madhhab).

Shaykh: The school's position is weak on this question.

Student: (...) the second narration.

Shaykh: Where?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: There is a second view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. I do not know whether there is a narration from Ahmad or a view. That is, there is no strong position for the companions (of Ahmad) in this, and Shaykh al-Islam held it. But whether it is a narration, I do not know.

Student: "These are my daughters" [al-Hijr 71].

Shaykh: Yes, that is, I will marry them to you.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Some exegetes said: "my daughters" means the daughters of the nation, because the Messenger is a father to his people, so he stands in the position of a father to them.

Student: Is this valid?

Shaykh: It is not valid, but what prompted them to this is that they said: his daughters are Muslim believing women, and these are disbelievers, and a disbeliever does not marry a believing woman. It is answered: either their law permits that, or the meaning of "these are my daughters" is: then become Muslims and marry them, and the meaning becomes understood.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: How many are coming? That does not contradict. How many are coming?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: The people have come to his certainty.

Student: The people have come.

Shaykh: Because they went to give each other good news about these people.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes, the point is...

Student: The people of the city came (...).
