﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 193–194]. ﴿الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ﴾ (al-Ruh al-Amin, "the Trustworthy Spirit") is Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him. He is described as "the Spirit" because he descends with that which contains life, namely the revelation by which hearts are alive. He is described as "trustworthy" (al-Amin) because the context requires it. The trustworthiness of Jibril, peace be upon him, with respect to the Qur'an is in several respects:

First: He is trustworthy in that he sends it down only to the one he was commanded to send it to. Accordingly, the claim of the Rafidah (a Shi'i sect), may Allah disgrace them, that Jibril was commanded to bring the Qur'an down to 'Ali but betrayed the trust and brought it down to Muhammad (ﷺ), contradicts the description of Jibril as trustworthy.

Second: The requirement of trustworthiness is that he conveys it exactly as he heard it from Allah, without adding to it, subtracting from it, or changing its order.

Third: That he conveys it at the time he was commanded to convey it, so he does not delay when it is revealed to him, except by the permission of Allah.

These three qualities are among the requirements of the trustworthiness of Jibril, peace be upon him.

As for His saying ﴿عَلَى قَلْبِكَ﴾ (ala qalbika, "upon your heart"), He specified the heart because it is the seat of understanding. This indicates Allah's care for the Qur'an and the Messenger's complete preservation of it (ﷺ). What is sent down upon the heart remains firm and is established, unlike what the ear hears, for the ear may reach the heart or may not: the heart may be heedless. But here it was upon the heart.

As for His saying ﴿لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ (li-takuna min al-mundhirin, "that you may be among the warners") [al-Shu'ara' 194], is the lam (ل) for causation (ta'lil) or for consequence ('aqibah)?

* Student: For both.

* The Shaykh: They are interrelated. If we say it is for causation, then he is charged with that task. If it is for consequence, then its outcome is that he becomes a warner even if there is no charge. However, the correct view is that it includes both meanings.

As for His saying ﴿مِنَ الْمُنْذِرِينَ﴾ (min al-mundhirin, "among the warners"), i.e., the Messengers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners﴾ [al-Nisa' 165].

As for His saying ﴿بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ﴾ (bi-lisanin 'arabiyyin mubin, "in a clear Arabic tongue") [al-Shu'ara' 195]: ﴿بِلِسَانٍ﴾ (bi-lisan, "in a tongue") means "in a language" (bi-lughah). The word lisan (tongue) was used to mean language, because it is the place of speech, which is the mark of a language. He said ﴿عَرَبِيٍّ﴾ ('arabi, "Arabic"), a nisbah (relative adjective) to the Arabs. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) was an Arab. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send any Messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make [the message] clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim 4].

This indicates that the Arabic language should be the language of all creation, because the Shari'ah that was revealed in it is the Shari'ah of all creation. Thus the Arabic language should be the language of all creation. This contrasts with those who want to dissolve it in our present age by demanding that the colloquial dialect (al-'ammiyyah) replace Arabic in correspondence, letters and other matters. Even more repugnant are those who try to speak a foreign language, as there are some people who take pride in the English language and others, and you find them showing off by speaking it.

Furthermore, His saying ﴿بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ﴾ is connected to His saying ﴿نَزَلَ بِهِ﴾ (nazala bihi, "brought it down"). His saying ([﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ بَيِّنٍ]، وفيه قراءة بالتشديد ﴿﴿نَزَّلَ﴾ ﴾، ونصب الروح، والفاعل الله) (["mubin" means clear], and there is a reading with the doubled letter in ﴿نَزَّلَ﴾ (nazzala, "caused to descend"), with the Spirit in the accusative, and the subject being Allah) ﴿﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (١٩٢) نَزَّلَ بِهِ الرُّوحَ الْأَمِينَ﴾ ﴾ [And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. He caused the Trustworthy Spirit to bring it down]. There is a benefit in the difference between the two readings: the One who commanded the descent is Allah, so Jibril descended. Thus it combines Jibril's action, which proceeded from Allah's command, with an indication of Allah's command to him to bring it down.

﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 196]: i.e., the mention of the Qur'an revealed upon Muhammad (ﷺ) is in the scriptures (zubur, "books"), "of the former peoples," such as the Tawrah (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel). ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِي زُبُرِ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ The author made the pronoun refer to the Qur'an; that is, the mention of the Qur'an exists in the scriptures of the ancients, their books. The intended meaning is a description of the Qur'an, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, was described in the Torah and the Gospel with his attributes and with the attributes of the Book that was revealed with him.

As for His saying ﴿لَفِي زُبُرِ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, the apparent meaning of this noble verse is generality: that all previous books mentioned the Qur'an and alluded to it, including the Torah and the Gospel. Here the kaf (ك) in ﴿كَمَا﴾ would be for comparison.

* In this there is clear evidence of Allah's care for this Qur'an, of its honouring and exalting, since it was mentioned in every book that came before.

* It also indicates that if this Book had come, all who adhere to the earlier books would have been obligated to believe in it.

(﴿Or is it not a sign for them﴾ for the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿a sign﴾ of that; meaning, a proof that it is true, ﴿that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it﴾) The word ﴿آيَةً﴾ (ayah, "sign") is the predicate (khabar) of ﴿يَكُنْ﴾ (yakun, "it be"), placed before its subject, and ﴿أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ﴾ (an ya'lamahu, "that they know it") is its postponed subject (ism). The meaning is: "Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?" The Children of Israel (Bani Isra'il) are the descendants of Ya'qub (Jacob) ibn Ishaq (Isaac), who branched out from him.

This is one of the clear signs that it is mentioned in the earlier scriptures: the scholars of the Children of Israel knew it, because if it had not been mentioned in their books, they would not have known it. They knew it because it is mentioned in their books.

* In this verse there is evidence that in such matters the reference is to the scholars, the people of knowledge.

As for the statement (like Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions among those who believed, for they inform people of this): this is not necessarily so. Their knowing it is what makes them scholars, whether they inform others or not. For this reason the Qur'an does not say "Is it not a sign for them that it be reported", but rather says ﴿that they know it﴾. The mere knowledge of these people of it is a sign, even if they do not report it.

We say: Abdullah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him, and those who believed are among the scholars of the Children of Israel. They knew and they reported, while others among the scholars who did not believe knew but did not report.

(The reading ﴿يَكُنْ﴾ with a ya' (yā') below and the nasb (accusative) on ﴿آيَةً﴾ is one reading, while the reading with a ta' (tā') above and the raf' (nominative) on ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ is another.)

* Student: (...)

* Shaykh: The reading is ﴿أَوَ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةٌ﴾. According to it, ﴿أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ﴾ is the khabar of ﴿تَكُنْ﴾. According to the first reading, ﴿يَكُنْ﴾ has ﴿آيَةً﴾ in the accusative as its predicate placed before, and ﴿أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ﴾ as its postponed subject.

* Student: Isn't the raf' (nominative) of ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ making kana (to be) complete?

* Shaykh: No. The sentence is not complete with ﴿أَوَ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةٌ﴾; the sentence is not complete there. So is the sentence complete with ﴿أَوَ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةٌ﴾? It is not complete. Therefore kana is incomplete (naqisah) here, in ﴿أَوَ لَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةٌ أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ﴾. The difference between the two readings is only this: ﴿آيَةٌ﴾ in the nominative is the ism (subject) of ﴿تَكُنْ﴾, and its khabar is ﴿أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 198–207:

He said: (﴿And if We had sent it down﴾; i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿upon some of the non-Arabs (a'jamiyn)﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 198], the plural of a'jam, ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾; i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿they would not have believed in it﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 199], out of arrogance toward following it).

﴿If We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: whether this is in the Arabic tongue or in another language, ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾, they would not have believed in it. The meaning is that they would never believe, whether it was brought by Muhammad ﷺ, who is of the very core of the Arabs and whom they know, or was brought by a non-Arab man. That is because they are obstinate, and the obstinate person, we seek refuge with Allah, would not believe even if every sign were brought to him, because there is a difference between the person who seeks the truth and the person who opposes the truth. The obstinate one is arrogant, and it is difficult for him to return to the truth. The meaning is: if Allah had sent down this Qur'an upon some of the non-Arabs, and it were in their language, they still would not believe in it, because they would not have understood it in the tongue of the non-Arabs; and if it were in the Arabic language, they would also not have believed, out of disdain at following a non-Arab man.

(﴿Thus﴾; i.e., like Our insertion of denial of it through the recitation of a non-Arab, ﴿We have inserted it﴾: We have inserted the denial of it, ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 200]; i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, in the recitation of the Prophet, that they do not believe in it. ﴿Thus﴾; i.e., like that insertion or threading, and what is meant by threading is inserting.)

﴿Thus﴾ is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq) of ﴿We have inserted it﴾, meaning "like that." It always comes in the Qur'an in such forms: "thus We did," "thus he denied," and the like. They say that the kaf is a noun meaning "like," and it is in apposition to the demonstrative referring back to the verbal noun understood from the verb. Accordingly, the i'rab of the kaf, a noun meaning "like," is an absolute object, whose governing element is the verb that follows it. That is, Allah, exalted is He, inserted denial into the hearts of the criminals. What is meant by ﴿the criminals﴾ is broader than the disbelievers of Makkah, contrary to what the author said; the criminal, the disbeliever, is such whether he is from the people of Makkah or from elsewhere.

And since denial and arrogance have entered their hearts, ﴿they do not believe in it﴾, and so on to the end [al-Shu'ara' 201]. In this verse there is no proof for the people of disbelief and disobedience who said: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers﴾ [al-An'am 148], because Allah, glorified and exalted, explained in another verse that the cause of their disbelief and polytheism is that they did not want the truth. When they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. Had they wanted the truth, Allah would have expanded their breasts for it, but they have, we seek refuge with Allah, arrogance, pride and haughtiness, and for that reason they were deprived of reaching what is right.

﴿They do not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾ [201]. ﴿Then it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 201–202]. ﴿They do not believe in it﴾; i.e., in the Qur'an. If we say that ﴿the criminals﴾ is general, then ﴿they do not believe in it﴾ means: in what Allah has sent down.

His statement ﴿until they see﴾ (hatta yaraw): is it for the endpoint (li-l-ghayah) or for causation (li-l-ta'lil)?

* Student: For the endpoint.

* Shaykh: For the endpoint. The meaning is that when they see the painful punishment, they might believe, but Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir 85].

His statement ﴿then it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ is the usual pattern for obstinate deniers: Allah gives them respite, so they sink deeper, we seek refuge with Allah, into disbelief, corruption and disobedience, until when the punishment comes to them, it comes upon them suddenly, unawares, as the Messenger ﷺ said: «Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari, and the wording is his (4686), and Muslim (2583 / 61), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may Allah be pleased with him.]]. For if Allah, glorified and exalted, had made them taste the might gradually, perhaps they would have believed and returned, but He, we seek refuge with Allah, gives them time until they reach the summit of disbelief and corruption, and then they are seized. This is something observed even in our present age: now we see that some lands, when they have sunk deep into disbelief and reached its extreme, are seized, we seek refuge with Allah.

He said: ﴿Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 203] (so that we may believe, and it will be said to them: No. They say: When is this punishment? Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [204] and so on to the end), meaning: when the punishment comes upon them suddenly, they will say: ﴿Will we be reprieved?﴾. This interrogative is for wishing; i.e., "if only we might be reprieved." This is the apparent meaning. The author took it on its apparent meaning as an interrogative of inquiry, which is why he says "it will be said to them: No," i.e., you will not be reprieved. But if we take it as a wish, that they wish to be reprieved, then it does not need an answer.

Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾. It has been mentioned before that the hamzah in such a construction either enters upon an implied sentence according to the context, or enters upon the existing sentence, and the original conjunction that follows it stands before it. ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ This is for rebuke and denunciation of them; i.e., do they seek to hasten the punishment of Allah?! He, glorified and exalted, is swift in seizing, so He denounces those who seek to hasten Allah's punishment. How do they seek to hasten the punishment: by act or by word?

* Student: By word and by act.

* Shaykh: We say: by word and by act. By word, they say ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ [Yunus 48]. By act, their deep immersion in disbelief and sins makes them deserving of being hastened in punishment. So this denunciation of them applies whether they hasten by word, as the author said, "they say: When is this punishment?", or hasten by act, by sinking deep and going to extremes in disbelief and sins, for that too is seeking the hastening of Allah's punishment.

Allah, exalted, says: (...).

Allah, exalted, says: Tell me, O addressee, if We grant these people enjoyment for years, and We give them respite and do not hasten their punishment, until they reach the full extent of enjoyment in this world, and then what they were promised comes to them, what good will that enjoyment do them? In reality it only increases them in regret, we seek refuge with Allah, or indeed increases them in punishment in the Fire, because the more a person's sins multiply, the more he increases. This, for example, truly applies to everyone who says to us about a certain person: these disbelievers have been blessed by Allah, and the world has been opened to them; the rains come to them at all times, the land is fertile, and so on. We say to him: ﴿Have you seen? If We grant them enjoyment for years, then what they were promised comes to them, what their enjoyment availed them will not avail them﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 205–207]. We say that this is more severe in its impact upon their hearts, because a person seized in ease of living, comfort and tranquility is more afflicted than one seized in hardship. The one in distress and adversity may perhaps see death as a relief to him, but the one seized, we seek refuge with Allah, in the height of blessing and its strength, is more severely punished.

We have mentioned to you that Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, the judge of judges in Egypt and author of Fath al-Bari, was once walking in a carriage, with people, attendants and servants on his right and left, when he passed by a Jewish oil-seller completely covered in filth from the oil. The Jew stopped him and said: "O our master, I think or words to that effect, your Prophet says: «The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever» [Muslim (2956 / 1), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah may Allah be pleased with him], and now you are a believer and you are in this bliss, while I am a Jewish disbeliever in this hellfire and punishment?" He said to him: "Yes, that is true. But what I have been granted of blessing is, in comparison with the blessing of the Hereafter, a prison, and what you are in of hardship is, in comparison with the punishment of the Hereafter, bliss and a paradise." Allah opened up to this Jew, and he embraced Islam. He recognized that this was true and feared it, because the Jews know and affirm the heavenly scriptures but are arrogant about submitting to them. It is said that he became Muslim.

The summary is that these people, if they are given long enjoyment of the world and its bliss, and then punishment comes to them, what good will that enjoyment do them? It will avail them nothing.

As for His statement ﴿what good did it do them﴾ (ma aghna 'anhum): the ma may be taken as negative, or it may be taken as interrogative but meaning negation. Which is more emphatic? That it be interrogative in meaning negation, because the interrogative with the meaning of negation includes negation and more, since it carries the sense of challenge: "What can you do to me?" That is, "I challenge you that you can do anything to me." ﴿What good did what they used to enjoy do them?﴾ means he challenges them that it can avail them anything. So when ma is suitable for both negation and interrogation, it is more fitting and more emphatic to take it as interrogative.

* Student: On an increase in meaning.

* Shaykh: An increase in meaning and in challenge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 198–207:

He said: (﴿And if We had sent it down﴾; i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿upon some of the non-Arabs (a'jamiyn)﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 198], the plural of a'jam, ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾; i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿they would not have believed in it﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 199], out of arrogance toward following it).

﴿If We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: whether this is in the Arabic tongue or in another language, ﴿and he had recited it to them﴾, they would not have believed in it. The meaning is that they would never believe, whether it was brought by Muhammad ﷺ, who is of the very core of the Arabs and whom they know, or was brought by a non-Arab man. That is because they are obstinate, and the obstinate person, we seek refuge with Allah, would not believe even if every sign were brought to him, because there is a difference between the person who seeks the truth and the person who opposes the truth. The obstinate one is arrogant, and it is difficult for him to return to the truth. The meaning is: if Allah had sent down this Qur'an upon some of the non-Arabs, and it were in their language, they still would not believe in it, because they would not have understood it in the tongue of the non-Arabs; and if it were in the Arabic language, they would also not have believed, out of disdain at following a non-Arab man.

(﴿Thus﴾; i.e., like Our insertion of denial of it through the recitation of a non-Arab, ﴿We have inserted it﴾: We have inserted the denial of it, ﴿into the hearts of the criminals﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 200]; i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, in the recitation of the Prophet, that they do not believe in it. ﴿Thus﴾; i.e., like that insertion or threading, and what is meant by threading is inserting.)

﴿Thus﴾ is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq) of ﴿We have inserted it﴾, meaning "like that." It always comes in the Qur'an in such forms: "thus We did," "thus he denied," and the like. They say that the kaf is a noun meaning "like," and it is in apposition to the demonstrative referring back to the verbal noun understood from the verb. Accordingly, the i'rab of the kaf, a noun meaning "like," is an absolute object, whose governing element is the verb that follows it. That is, Allah, exalted is He, inserted denial into the hearts of the criminals. What is meant by ﴿the criminals﴾ is broader than the disbelievers of Makkah, contrary to what the author said; the criminal, the disbeliever, is such whether he is from the people of Makkah or from elsewhere.

And since denial and arrogance have entered their hearts, ﴿they do not believe in it﴾, and so on to the end [al-Shu'ara' 201]. In this verse there is no proof for the people of disbelief and disobedience who said: ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers﴾ [al-An'am 148], because Allah, glorified and exalted, explained in another verse that the cause of their disbelief and polytheism is that they did not want the truth. When they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate. Had they wanted the truth, Allah would have expanded their breasts for it, but they have, we seek refuge with Allah, arrogance, pride and haughtiness, and for that reason they were deprived of reaching what is right.

﴿They do not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾ [201]. ﴿Then it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 201–202]. ﴿They do not believe in it﴾; i.e., in the Qur'an. If we say that ﴿the criminals﴾ is general, then ﴿they do not believe in it﴾ means: in what Allah has sent down.

His statement ﴿until they see﴾ (hatta yaraw): is it for the endpoint (li-l-ghayah) or for causation (li-l-ta'lil)?

* Student: For the endpoint.

* Shaykh: For the endpoint. The meaning is that when they see the painful punishment, they might believe, but Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir 85].

His statement ﴿then it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ is the usual pattern for obstinate deniers: Allah gives them respite, so they sink deeper, we seek refuge with Allah, into disbelief, corruption and disobedience, until when the punishment comes to them, it comes upon them suddenly, unawares, as the Messenger ﷺ said: «Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari, and the wording is his (4686), and Muslim (2583 / 61), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari may Allah be pleased with him.]]. For if Allah, glorified and exalted, had made them taste the might gradually, perhaps they would have believed and returned, but He, we seek refuge with Allah, gives them time until they reach the summit of disbelief and corruption, and then they are seized. This is something observed even in our present age: now we see that some lands, when they have sunk deep into disbelief and reached its extreme, are seized, we seek refuge with Allah.

He said: ﴿Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 203] (so that we may believe, and it will be said to them: No. They say: When is this punishment? Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ [204] and so on to the end), meaning: when the punishment comes upon them suddenly, they will say: ﴿Will we be reprieved?﴾. This interrogative is for wishing; i.e., "if only we might be reprieved." This is the apparent meaning. The author took it on its apparent meaning as an interrogative of inquiry, which is why he says "it will be said to them: No," i.e., you will not be reprieved. But if we take it as a wish, that they wish to be reprieved, then it does not need an answer.

Allah, exalted, says: ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾. It has been mentioned before that the hamzah in such a construction either enters upon an implied sentence according to the context, or enters upon the existing sentence, and the original conjunction that follows it stands before it. ﴿Do they then seek to hasten Our punishment?﴾ This is for rebuke and denunciation of them; i.e., do they seek to hasten the punishment of Allah?! The meaning is that they would never believe, whether it was brought by Muhammad ﷺ, who is of the very core of the Arabs and whom they know, or was brought by a non-Arab man. That is because they are obstinate, and the obstinate person, we seek refuge with Allah, would not believe even if every sign were brought to him, because there is a difference between the person who seeks the truth and the person who opposes the truth. The obstinate one is arrogant, and it is difficult for him to return to the truth. Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 26, verses 208–215:

(﴿Never did We destroy a town but it had warners⁠—﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 208] messengers warning its people.) His saying, ﴿but it had warners⁠—﴾ is a description of ﴿town﴾; meaning: We did not destroy it except in this state, ﴿but it had warners⁠—﴾.

As for ﴿warners﴾, is the meaning that God Most High warns [through] His messengers, i.e., "except that We are warners to it," or that ﴿but it had warners⁠—﴾ means "messengers who warn"? The author says: ﴿but it had warners⁠—﴾, meaning: except that it had messengers warning it. But from whom were these messengers sent? From God.

(﴿A reminder﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 209] an admonition for them.) Meaning: We send these warners for the sake of a reminder, i.e., an admonition to them. (﴿And We were not unjust⁠—﴾) in destroying them after their warning.

The author says: (﴿And We were not unjust⁠—﴾ in destroying them after their warning), and this is correct. It may also mean ﴿And We were not unjust⁠—﴾, i.e., destroying them without warning, and the meaning is correct on this reading too, as well as on the reading the author mentioned. For God Most High, if He destroys them after their warning and they have disobeyed, has not wronged them. Likewise, it is impossible for Him to destroy one who has not been warned, because that would be injustice.

* This verse is evidence that the law does not bind before one reaches it: legal obligations do not apply except after knowledge, and as long as a person is not aware of the law, he is not held accountable for it.

There are witnesses to this. Among them is what passed us in the story of the one who prayed badly.[[Al-Bukhari (793) and Muslim, with his wording (397/45), from Abu Hurayrah: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered the mosque, and a man entered and prayed, then came and greeted the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned the greeting, and said: "Go back and pray, for you have not prayed." The man went back and prayed as he had prayed, then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and greeted him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And upon you be peace," then said: "Go back and pray, for you have not prayed." This happened three times. The man said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I do not do better than this; teach me." He said: "When you stand to pray, say the takbir, then recite what you can of the Qur'an, then bow until you are settled in bowing, then rise until you are standing straight, then prostrate until you are settled in prostration, then rise until you are settled sitting, and do that throughout your prayer."]] The Messenger did not oblige him to make up what he had missed, because he did not know. Another is the woman who suffered from istihadah and did not pray, and the Prophet (ﷺ) did not command her to make up the prayers.[[Al-Bukhari (320), from Aisha: Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh suffered from istihadah and asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "That is a vein, and it is not menstruation. When menstruation comes, leave the prayer, and when it departs, wash and pray."]] Another is the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim, when he ate after dawn.[[Al-Bukhari (1916) and Muslim (1090/33), from 'Adi ibn Hatim (may God be pleased with him), who said: When the verse ﴿until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread [at dawn]﴾ was revealed, 'Adi ibn Hatim said to him: "O Messenger of God, I place two cords under my pillow, a white cord and a black cord, and I know the night from the day by them." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Your pillow is broad indeed; it is only the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day."]] And many other such things. However, a person may be held accountable for something if he is negligent and careless, such as when it has occurred to his mind, or he was told that this thing is obligatory, but he says, as the common people say: ﴿Do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would trouble you﴾ [al-Ma'idah 101]. Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.[[Al-Bukhari (2753) and Muslim, with his wording (204/348), from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: When this verse ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) called the Quraysh, and they gathered, both general and specific, and he said: "O Banu Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, save yourselves from the Fire. O Banu Murrah ibn Ka'b, save yourselves from the Fire. O Banu 'Abd Shams, save yourselves from the Fire. O Banu 'Abd Manaf, save yourselves from the Fire. O Banu Hashim, save yourselves from the Fire. O Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib, save yourselves from the Fire. O Fatimah, save yourself from the Fire, for I cannot avail you anything against God, except that you have kinship which I will keep in good ties."]]) This was at the beginning of the call: he was commanded to warn his closest kindred. Why? Because they have the greatest right to his kindness; and because by the nature of kinship, not by the nature of reality, they are the first of people to believe in him; and because, by the nature of kinship, they are also the most zealous of people for him; and because, by the nature of kinship, they also have the greatest right over him. Therefore a person is responsible for his family more than he is responsible for strangers, and responsible for relatives more than for one with whom he has no kinship.

His saying ﴿the closest﴾ is a superlative form, which implies that since the ruling is tied to the closest, whoever is closer is more deserving and has greater right.

As for his saying, (and they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib), this is not accurate with respect to just these two clans. Rather, the other two clans, the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal, are without doubt among the closest kindred, but some of them responded and some did not. His uncle Abu Lahab refrained from responding, though he was among the closest people to him, for a man's paternal uncle is the twin of his father. His uncle Abu Talib also refrained from responding, though he too was the twin of his father, but Abu Talib supported and aided him, while Abu Lahab opposed him and forsook him, may God protect us.

Before the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), they became three groups: a group that believed in him, a group that supported him without believing, and a group that neither believed in him nor supported him.

This is part of the wisdom of God, Mighty and Majestic; for had they all supported him and believed in him, it would have been said: "This man wants kingship and lordship." Therefore his relatives followed him while they were in agreement on this scheme, but it is part of God's wisdom that He divided them in this way.

﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ * This is evidence that a person must warn and admonish the nearest first, then the nearer, and he is directly responsible for his family.

(﴿And lower your wing﴾ be gentle toward, ﴿to those who follow you of the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 215], the monotheists.) The warning is for the kindred, and the lowering of the wing is for the believer, whether he is of his kindred or not.

* This is evidence that a person must not be arrogant toward anyone, but especially toward the believer, he should be gentle toward him. But is it not that toward a non-believer he should not be gentle?

* Student: He should not initiate the greeting.

* Shaykh: The point is, he should not be gentle toward him.

God Most High says: ﴿And speak to him with gentle speech﴾ [Ta-Ha 44].

* Student: Before conveying (...) the call, but he refused, and knew the call, and the call reached him, so it is appropriate (...).

* Shaykh: That is, the matter returns to what is beneficial, unless the law indicates otherwise, for the law is the aim; by His saying: ﴿Lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 215].

* In this is evidence that the realization of faith comes by what? By following the Messenger (ﷺ); because when He said ﴿Warn your kindred﴾, he, if he warns, is either followed or not followed.

(﴿فَإِنْ عَصَوْكَ﴾; i.e., your tribe) and the more correct view is "or others," (﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 216] from worshipping other than Allah). The expression ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ does not say "منكم" (from you). Had he said "منكم," it would have been a harsher shock, and it could have implied that this disavowal was personal. Also, there was no aversion to the action itself on his part, because... (...) So when he says ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾, they understand that the reason for the disavowal is the action, which may prompt them to refrain from it, so that they may gain loyalty rather than disavowal.

(﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ read with waw and fa'). This is one of the rare matters in the readings (qira'at), because the usual case in recitation is that the difference lies in the attribute of the word or letter, not in its essence or form. Yet this may sometimes occur with the letter itself, and sometimes by the dropping or non-dropping of a letter, as in the Almighty's words in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١١٥) وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ [al-Baqarah 115, 116], where there is a reading that drops the waw: ﴿قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ﴾. * Student: (...) this reading.

* Shaykh: ﴿﴿فَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ ﴾. Tawakkul is reliance upon Allah together with trust in Him to bring about benefits and ward off harms. (﴿عَلَى الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 217], i.e., Allah; entrust to Him all your affairs.) The expression ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ does not say "منكم" (from you). Had he said "منكم," it would have been a harsher shock, and it could have implied that this disavowal was personal. Also, there was no aversion to the action itself on his part, because... (...) So when he says ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾, they understand that the reason for the disavowal is the action, which may prompt them to refrain from it, so that they may gain loyalty rather than disavowal.

(﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ read with waw and fa'). This is one of the rare matters in the readings (qira'at), because the usual case in recitation is that the difference lies in the attribute of the word or letter, not in its essence or form. Yet this may sometimes occur with the letter itself, and sometimes by the dropping or non-dropping of a letter, as in the Almighty's words in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١١٥) وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ [al-Baqarah 115, 116], where there is a reading that drops the waw: ﴿قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ﴾. This is one of the rare matters in the readings. Recitation may concern the arrangement of the letter, the presence of the letter, or the shape of the letter. Most of it concerns the shape and form of the letter: whether it is lengthened or not, raised or vowelled. But the type of letter is rare, as here with waw and fa'. In what respect is this? In the type of letter, in the presence of the letter, as I indicated in the verse of al-Baqarah ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١١٥) وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ [al-Baqarah 115, 116], and in the reading ﴿قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ﴾, and in Surat al-Ma'idah also the letter (...), there is also the addition of waw in one reading and its omission in another.

As for His saying ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ﴾, tawakkul..

* Student: (...) this reading.

* Shaykh: ﴿﴿فَتَوَكَّلْ﴾ ﴾. Tawakkul is reliance upon Allah together with trust in Him to bring about benefits and ward off harms. (﴿عَلَى الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 217], i.e., Allah; entrust to Him all your affairs.) He did not say "upon Allah" but said ﴿الْعَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾, because the context calls for it: it calls for might (ʿizzah) against those who deny him, and mercy against his fulfilment of the duty of warning. (﴿الَّذِي يَرَاكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ to prayer, ﴿وَتَقَلُّبَكَ﴾ among the pillars of prayer, standing and sitting, bowing and prostrating, ﴿فِي السَّاجِدِينَ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 219]; i.e., those who pray.)

As for His saying ﴿الَّذِي يَرَاكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ﴾ to prayer: some say, "when you rise from your sleep," but the meaning the author mentioned is more general. It has also been said that the meaning is "when you rise in your affairs, whether warning or other than warning"; that is, He sees you when you rise to warn, sees you when you rise to pray, sees you when you rise to fast, and when you rise to perform Hajj, in all circumstances; that is, when you rise to worship Allah. He also sees your movement among those who prostrate; that is, among those who pray, i.e., among them as a whole. This last meaning is more general than all of them.

﴿وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِي السَّاجِدِينَ﴾: prayer is singled out because it is the foundation of physical acts of worship. As for His saying ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 220], this sentence is a resumptive clause to show that, along with His seeing, may He be blessed and exalted, He is also All-Hearing and All-Knowing. So there are three attributes: sight, hearing and knowledge.

(﴿Shall I inform you﴾, i.e., O disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿upon whom the devils descend?﴾ [al-Shu'ara 221], with one of the two taa's deleted from the original, which is "tatanazzalu".) ﴿They descend upon every lying sinner﴾ (kadhdhab), ﴿sinful﴾ (fajir), like Musaylima and others of the soothsayers (kahin, "soothsayer") [al-Shu'ara 222].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?﴾ All of this revolves around the saying of the disbelievers that the Messenger ﷺ was a soothsayer, and that the soothsayer is one upon whom the devils descend. But this Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds; the devils did not bring it down. Allah then clarified this question, either to create suspense or to establish the proof and the challenge. That is, the devils do not descend upon the likes of the Messenger ﷺ, the truthful and trustworthy one, far removed from indecency; rather, they descend upon every lying sinner. Bringing the speech in this form, as a question followed by a statement, is more emphatic in fixing it in the heart, because had it come as a plain statement, it would not have ... the time when it came in the form of a question: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? (221) They descend upon every lying sinner﴾ (kadhdhab) ﴿sinful﴾. The word ﴿affak﴾ here is in the intensive form, meaning one who frequently fabricates (ifk), and ifk means lying, and ﴿athim﴾ means one who sins, i.e., one who combines bad speech with bad action. As for his saying, "like Musaylima and others of the soothsayers," this is an example: "such as such."

(﴿They cast﴾ [al-Shu'ara 223], i.e., the devils, ﴿the hearing﴾, i.e., what they heard from the angels, to the soothsayers, ﴿and most of them are liars﴾, they add to what they heard a great deal of lies. This was before the devils were barred from the heaven.)

﴿They cast the hearing﴾: the pronoun in ﴿they cast﴾ refers to whom? The devils. ﴿The hearing﴾, i.e., what is heard, and it is a verbal noun used in the sense of the passive participle. They cast it upon whom? Upon the soothsayers. They take from what they hear what they take, but they add many lies to it, and therefore He said: ﴿and most of them are liars﴾. The author said: (they add to what is heard a great deal of lies, and this was before the devils were barred from the heaven). Before the mission of the Messenger ﷺ, the devils used to listen to some of what was in the heaven, but at the time of the mission they could no longer listen, as they said: ﴿And we used to sit in it on seats for listening, but whoever listens now finds a watching flame awaiting him﴾ [al-Jinn 9]. They were unable to do so; had they sat in their places as before to listen, the shooting stars would have reached them.

But has this ended with the cessation of revelation, because the ruling revolves with its cause, or has it remained? The apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that it ended with the cessation of revelation, and that at that time the heaven was prevented from the devils. As for after that, they are not prevented; yet they may sometimes be prevented, just as we see many shooting stars.

* Student: We mentioned the hadith: "The devils ride one another..." (...) strength (...) without one of them riding the other (...)?

* Shaykh: (...). I do not know whether this is marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) or mawquf (ending with a companion). If it is marfu', it must be affirmed and we must not object to it; if it is mawquf, we are not obliged to affirm it. Without doubt, they are capable of reaching [distant places], and for this reason, with their speed and lightness, they are not like humans. The ifrit of the jinn said to Sulayman: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ [al-Naml 39]. No human can ever do this, however strong humans may become; they cannot bring anything with such speed.

The connection (...) this is because the disbelievers of Quraysh opposed the Prophet ﷺ by calling him a soothsayer, and they opposed him by calling him a poet: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await the misfortunes of time"?﴾ [al-Tur 30], (...) Allah the Exalted, that he should be a soothsayer in what came before.

Then he said: (﴿As for the poets, those who go astray follow them﴾; i.e., in their poetry, so they speak in its favor and transmit it from them, and so they are blameworthy.) Which is blameworthy, the poets or the misguided ones?

* Student: All of them (...).

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. That is, one must know who follows poetry: only the misguided ones follow it, so it is falsehood. This Qur'an is not like that; only the people of guidance and rectitude follow it. This shows that it is not poetry, because in general it is the misguided person who follows poetry and takes it up. Poetry here refers to what is not taken from the Book and the Sunnah. If it is taken from the Book and the Sunnah, then one may follow it (...), such as some of the odes composed by the people of knowledge and faith. That is not considered poetry that the misguided follow (...). For this reason He said: ﴿except those who believe﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 227].

* Student: (...) Ibn al-Qayyim.

* Shaykh: No, that is something known for the purpose of moving from one thing to another. Ibn al-Qayyim moved from the love poem to the subject, as he did (...).

He said: (﴿Do you not see﴾, i.e., know, ﴿that they wander in every valley﴾ of speech and its various arts ﴿distractedly﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 225], i.e., they are overcome, exceeding the limit in praise and in satire.) This is correct. The poet says what he cannot control himself in, because he exaggerates in praise if he praises, and exaggerates in blame if he blames (...), as if he speaks without awareness, even though it is poetry, because he is seized by feeling. But the poet speaks without awareness. The intended meaning of "the poets" is other than those who believe and do righteous deeds, which is why He made an exception, saying: ﴿except those who believe﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 227] (...). (﴿And that they say﴾, we did, ﴿what they do not do﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 226], i.e., they lie, ﴿they say what they do not do﴾.)

The author says: (﴿They say﴾, we did, ﴿what they do not do﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 226], i.e., they lie.) This needs consideration. But ﴿they say what they do not do﴾ refers to when they praise or satirize: they say, "We do so-and-so," "We will do such-and-such," when they want to draw near to a person: "We will serve you, we will console you with our own selves, we will ransom you with our families," and the like. But do they actually do this? No, because they are misguided, not (...).

Likewise, ﴿they say what they do not do﴾: they say, in satirizing their enemy, "We will strike him on the skull, we will make his children orphans, we will make his women widows," and the like, while they do not do that. It may be that the poet who stirs up the nation with his poetry ends up at the rear, not at the front when the two lines meet.

(﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ among the poets, ﴿and remember Allah much﴾, i.e., poetry did not preoccupy them from remembrance, ﴿and defend themselves﴾ with their satire against the disbelievers ﴿after they had been wronged﴾, i.e., by the disbelievers' satire against them, among the believers as a whole, so they are not blameworthy. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged﴾ [an-Nisa' 148], and ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he has transgressed against you﴾ [al-Baqarah 194].)

This is in His saying: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allah much and defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 227]. These are four attributes: faith, righteous deeds, remembering Allah much, and this indicates that the poet's remembrance of Allah is little, for no heart is filled with poetry without remembrance of Allah being distant from it. Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Love of the Book and love of the melodies of song ∗∗∗ cannot be together in the heart of a servant.

The fourth attribute: ﴿and defend themselves after they have been wronged﴾: they defended themselves, meaning for themselves, ﴿and those who, when wronged, defend themselves﴾ [ash-Shura 39].
﴿after they have been wronged﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 227], by whatever means: either by the disbelievers' satire against them if it is a poet against a poet, or by the disbelievers' aggression against them as well.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And those who wronged will know﴾ among the poets and others, ﴿what return they will be returned to﴾, the place of return, ﴿they will return﴾ after death.) So this statement contains a clear threat, meaning that those who did wrong will soon know what kind of return their turning back will be, which is the return to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. This is a clear threat to the wrongdoers. Wrongdoing is the pasture (...). Wrongdoing is among the things most quickly punished, especially if the wronged person prays against his oppressor, for the matter will swiftly come to that.

Furthermore, wrongdoing is of two kinds: one is oppression that transgresses against others, and the other is oppression of oneself. If it is in disobedience to Allah, it is oppression of oneself; if it is in aggression against others, it is oppression of others, such as if he takes his property or ruins his affairs, for this is transgressing oppression. And Allah knows best.

* Shaykh: Yes, it is permissible not to obey him (...); that is, if he says, for example: "I (...)," there is no objection. But if he demands it, you become obliged to it...
